title.zh: 卷97 島夷桓玄 海夷馮跋 島夷劉裕
title.en: Volume 97: Huan Xuan of the Daoyi People, Feng Ba of the Haiyi, Liu Yu of the Daoyi
title.raw: 卷97 島夷桓玄 海夷馮跋 島夷劉裕 Volume 97: Huan Xuan of the Daoyi People, Feng Ba of the Haiyi, Liu Yu of the Daoyi

sentences.zh: 島夷桓玄 海夷馮跋 島夷劉裕

translations.literal: Island barbarian Huan Xuan; sea barbarian Feng Ba; island barbarian Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan of the Daoyi, Feng Ba of the Haiyi, and Liu Yu of the Daoyi.

sentences.zh: 島夷桓玄，字敬道，本譙國龍亢楚也。

translations.literal: The island barbarian Huan Xuan, courtesy name Jingdao, was originally of Longkang in Qiao commandery, Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan of the Daoyi, whose courtesy name was Jingdao, was originally from Longkang in Qiao commandery in the state of Chu.

sentences.zh: 僭晉大司馬溫之子，溫愛之，臨終命以為後。

translations.literal: He was the son of the usurping Jin Grand Marshal Wen; Wen loved him and on his deathbed ordered that he be made heir.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of Huan Wen, Grand Marshal of the usurping Jin regime. Wen favored him and on his deathbed named him his successor.

sentences.zh: 年七歲，襲封南郡公。

translations.literal: At age seven he inherited the title Duke of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of seven he inherited the title Duke of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 登國五年，為司馬昌明太子洗馬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dengguo he served as attendant to the crown prince of Sima Changming.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Dengguo, he was appointed attendant to the crown prince of Emperor Xiaowu, Sima Changming.

sentences.zh: 玄志氣不倫，欲以雄豪自許。

translations.literal: Xuan's spirit and ambition were out of the ordinary; he wished to reckon himself a hero.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's temperament was unconventional, and he aspired to make a name for himself as a bold champion.

sentences.zh: 朝議以溫有陵虐之迹，故抑玄兄弟，出為義興太守，不得志。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that Wen had shown signs of overbearing cruelty, so Xuan and his brothers were held down; he was sent out as Administrator of Yixing and did not achieve his aims.
translations.idiomatic: Because the court believed Wen had shown signs of tyrannical ambition, Xuan and his brothers were deliberately sidelined. Xuan was posted out as Administrator of Yixing, where he could not advance his ambitions.

sentences.zh: 少時去職。

translations.literal: After a short time he left his post.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he resigned his office.

sentences.zh: 皇始初，司馬德宗立，其會稽王道子擅權，信任尚書僕射王國寶，為時所疾。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangshi, Sima Dezong was enthroned; his Prince of Kuaiji, Daozi, monopolized power and trusted the Minister of Works Wang Guobao, who was detested by the age.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Huangshi, Sima Dezong, Emperor An, took the throne. The Prince of Kuaiji, Sima Daozi, seized power and placed his trust in the Vice Minister of Works Wang Guobao, who was widely hated.

sentences.zh: 玄說荊州刺史殷仲堪，令推德宗兗州刺史王恭為盟主，以討國寶，仲堪從之。

translations.literal: Xuan persuaded the Inspector of Jing province Yin Zhongkan to have Dezong's Inspector of Yan province Wang Gong made alliance leader to attack Guobao; Zhongkan agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan persuaded Yin Zhongkan, Inspector of Jing province, to propose Wang Gong, Inspector of Yan province under Dezong, as leader of the alliance to move against Guobao. Zhongkan agreed.

sentences.zh: 會恭使亦上，相逢於中路，約同大舉，並抗表起兵。

translations.literal: It happened that Gong's envoy was also on the road; they met midway, agreed on a joint rising, and both submitted memorials raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong's envoy was traveling the same route; the parties met on the road, agreed to launch a joint campaign, and both submitted memorials calling for armed rebellion.

sentences.zh: 尋平王國寶等。

translations.literal: Before long they pacified Wang Guobao and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they had defeated Wang Guobao and his faction.

sentences.zh: 天興初，德宗以玄為使持節、督交廣二州諸軍事、建威將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxing, Dezong appointed Xuan Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Supervisor of military affairs in the two provinces of Jiao and Guang, General Who Establishes Might, General Who Pacifies the Yue as Central Commander, and Inspector of Guang province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianxing, Dezong appointed Xuan Bearer of the Staff of Authority, supervisor of military affairs in Jiao and Guang provinces, General Who Establishes Might, Central Commander Who Pacifies the Yue, and Inspector of Guang province.

sentences.zh: 後王恭復與德宗豫州刺史庾楷共起兵，以討其江州刺史王愉、司馬尚之兄弟。

translations.literal: Later Wang Gong again joined Dezong's Inspector of Yu province Yu Kai in raising troops to attack his Inspector of Jiang province Wang Yu and the brothers Sima Shangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Gong again joined forces with Yu Kai, Inspector of Yu province under Dezong, to raise troops against Wang Yu, Inspector of Jiang province, and the brothers Sima Shangzhi.

sentences.zh: 玄及龍驤將軍揚佺期、荊州刺史殷仲堪等率軍應恭。

translations.literal: Xuan, the General of the Flying Dragon Yang Quanqi, the Inspector of Jing province Yin Zhongkan, and others led armies in response to Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, General of the Flying Dragon Yang Quanqi, Yin Zhongkan the Inspector of Jing province, and others led their armies to support Gong.

sentences.zh: 玄等造於石頭。

translations.literal: Xuan and the rest advanced to Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and his allies advanced on Stone City.

sentences.zh: 於時德宗征虜將軍司馬元顯一軍仍守石頭，列舟艦斷淮口。

translations.literal: At that time Dezong's General Who Conquers the Barbarians Sima Yuanxian's army still held Stone City, arraying warships to block the mouth of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Sima Yuanxian, Dezong's General Who Conquers the Barbarians, still held Stone City with his army and lined up warships to block the mouth of the Huai River.

sentences.zh: 道子出軍，將屯中堂，忽有馬驚，軍中擾亂，人馬赴江者甚眾，良久乃定。

translations.literal: Daozi led troops out and was about to encamp at the Central Hall when suddenly horses panicked; the army was thrown into disorder, and very many men and horses rushed into the river; only after a long while was order restored.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi marched out with his army and was about to encamp at the Central Hall when horses suddenly stampeded. The troops fell into chaos, and a great many men and horses plunged into the river. Order was not restored for some time.

sentences.zh: 玄等不知建業危弱，且王恭尋敗，玄甚惶懼，乃回軍于蔡洲。

translations.literal: Xuan and the rest did not know how weak Jianye was, and moreover Wang Gong was soon defeated; Xuan was greatly alarmed and withdrew his army to Cai Isle.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and his allies did not realize how weak the capital at Jianye was, and when Wang Gong was soon defeated Xuan grew deeply alarmed and withdrew his army to Cai Isle.

sentences.zh: 王恭司馬劉牢之率北府軍來次新亭。

translations.literal: Wang Gong's Chief of Staff Liu Laozhi led the Northern Headquarters army and halted at Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi, Wang Gong's chief of staff, led the Northern Headquarters army and encamped at Xinting.

sentences.zh: 於是德宗以桓脩為荊州，仲堪為廣州，玄為江州，佺期為雍州，刺史郗恢為尚書。

translations.literal: Thereupon Dezong made Huan Xiu Inspector of Jing, Zhongkan of Guang, Xuan of Jiang, Quanqi of Yong, and the Inspector Xi Hui Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong then appointed Huan Xiu Inspector of Jing province, Zhongkan Inspector of Guang, Xuan Inspector of Jiang, Quanqi Inspector of Yong, and the former inspector Xi Hui Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 仲堪回師南旋，乃使人徇于玄等軍曰：「若不各散歸，大軍至江陵，當悉戮餘口。」

translations.literal: Zhongkan turned his army southward and sent men to proclaim through Xuan's army: "If you do not each disperse and return, when the main force reaches Jiangling, all remaining mouths will be slaughtered."
translations.idiomatic: As Zhongkan marched his army south, he sent messengers through Xuan's camp proclaiming: "Unless you disperse and return home, when our main force reaches Jiangling we will slaughter every last one of you."

sentences.zh: 仲堪偏將劉系先領兵二千隸于佺期，輒率眾而歸，玄等大懼，乃狼狽而走。

translations.literal: Zhongkan's subordinate general Liu Xixian, who had led two thousand men attached to Quanqi, abruptly led his troops back; Xuan and the rest were greatly afraid and fled in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan's subordinate general Liu Xixian, who commanded two thousand men under Quanqi, abruptly led his troops away. Xuan and his allies were seized with panic and fled in disarray.

sentences.zh: 庾楷亦棄眾奔于南軍。

translations.literal: Yu Kai also abandoned his troops and fled to the southern army.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Kai likewise abandoned his forces and fled to Zhongkan's southern army.

sentences.zh: 玄並趣輕舟追仲堪，至尋陽，而推玄為盟主，鎮於夏口。

translations.literal: Xuan together hastened in light boats to pursue Zhongkan; reaching Xunyang, they made Xuan alliance leader and he garrisoned Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan pressed forward in light boats to pursue Zhongkan. At Xunyang his allies named him leader of the alliance, and he took up position at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 德宗加玄都督荊州四郡，以玄兄西昌公偉為輔國將軍、南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: Dezong added to Xuan's titles Commander over four commanderies of Jing, and appointed Xuan's elder brother the Duke of Xichang, Wei, General Who Assists the State and Colonel of the Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong further appointed Xuan commander over four commanderies in Jing province and made Xuan's elder brother Huan Wei, Duke of Xichang, General Who Assists the State and Colonel of the Southern Man.

sentences.zh: 寵玄兄弟，欲以侵削荊雍。

translations.literal: He favored the Huan brothers, intending thereby to encroach upon and reduce Jing and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: By favoring the Huan brothers, he hoped to weaken the hold of the Jing and Yong regions on power.

sentences.zh: 先是荊州大水，仲堪倉廩空竭，玄乘其虛而伐之，先遣軍襲巴陵。

translations.literal: Earlier Jing province had suffered great floods; Zhongkan's granaries were empty and exhausted. Xuan seized this weakness to attack him, first sending troops to strike Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jing province had been ravaged by floods, and Zhongkan's granaries were empty. Xuan exploited this weakness to attack him, first dispatching troops to strike Baling.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史郭銓當之鎮，路逢玄，玄遣銓為前驅。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Liang province Guo Quan was on his way to his post when he met Xuan on the road; Xuan sent Quan as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Quan, Inspector of Liang province, was traveling to his post when he met Xuan on the road. Xuan pressed him into service as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 玄發夏口，與仲堪書云：「今當入沔，討除佺期，頓兵江口。

translations.literal: Xuan set out from Xiakou and wrote to Zhongkan: "I shall now enter the Mian, eliminate Quanqi, and halt my troops at the river mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Setting out from Xiakou, Xuan wrote to Zhongkan: "I am about to advance up the Mian River to destroy Quanqi and will halt my army at the river mouth.

sentences.zh: 若相與無貳，可殺楊廣，若其不爾，便當率軍入江。」

translations.literal: If you stand with me without disloyalty, you may kill Yang Guang; if not, I shall lead my army into the Yangtze."
translations.idiomatic: If you remain loyal to me, kill Yang Guang. If you do not, I will lead my army down the Yangtze."

sentences.zh: 別與桓偉書，令剋期為內應，偉惶遽，以書示仲堪，仲堪慰喻遣歸，夜乃執之。

translations.literal: Separately he wrote to Huan Wei, ordering him to act as inside contact on a set date. Wei was alarmed and showed the letter to Zhongkan; Zhongkan comforted and instructed him to return, but that night seized him.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote separately to Huan Wei, instructing him to act as an inside contact on a set date. Wei panicked and showed the letter to Zhongkan. Zhongkan reassured him and sent him back, but that night had him arrested.

sentences.zh: 仲堪遣龍驤將軍殷邁、振威將軍劉山民等統眾七千至西江口。

translations.literal: Zhongkan sent the General of the Flying Dragon Yin Mai, the General Who Quells Might Liu Shanmin, and others to command seven thousand men to the West River mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan dispatched Yin Mai, General of the Flying Dragon, Liu Shanmin, General Who Quells Might, and others at the head of seven thousand troops to the West River mouth.

sentences.zh: [1]玄聞邁至，復與其黨苻永道領帳下擊之，邁等敗走。

translations.literal: [1] When Xuan heard that Mai had arrived, he again with his partisan Fu Yongdao led his personal guard to attack; Mai and the rest were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: [1] When Xuan learned that Mai had arrived, he again led his personal guard with his partisan Fu Yongdao to attack. Mai and his forces were defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 玄頓巴陵，收其兵而館其穀，復破楊廣於夏口。

translations.literal: Xuan halted at Baling, took over their troops and quartered their grain, and again defeated Yang Guang at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan halted at Baling, absorbed their troops, and took over their grain stores. He then defeated Yang Guang at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 仲堪既失巴陵之積，又諸將皆敗，江陵駭震，城內大飢，皆以胡麻為廩。

translations.literal: Zhongkan having lost the stores at Baling and his generals all having been defeated, Jiangling was shaken with alarm; within the city there was severe famine, and sesame was used for the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost the stores at Baling and with all his generals defeated, Zhongkan found Jiangling in turmoil. Famine gripped the city, and even sesame seeds were pressed into service as provisions.

sentences.zh: 初，仲堪之得玄書也，急召佺期，佺期曰：「江陵無食，何以待敵？

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhongkan received Xuan's letter, he urgently summoned Quanqi. Quanqi said: "Jiangling has no food—how can we await the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongkan first received Xuan's letter, he urgently summoned Quanqi. Quanqi replied: "Jiangling has no food. How can we stand against the enemy?

sentences.zh: 可來見就，共守襄陽。」

translations.literal: You may come join me, and together we shall hold Xiangyang."
translations.idiomatic: Come join me, and together we will hold Xiangyang."

sentences.zh: 仲堪猶以全軍，無緣棄城迸走，甚憂佺期弗來，乃紿之曰：「比來收集，[2]已有儲矣，可有數萬人百日糧。」

translations.literal: Zhongkan still had his full army and had no reason to abandon the city and flee; he greatly feared Quanqi would not come, so he deceived him, saying: "Recently we have gathered supplies; [2] we already have stores—enough grain for tens of thousands for a hundred days."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan still commanded a full army and could not simply abandon the city and flee. Fearing that Quanqi would not come, he deceived him: "We have been gathering supplies lately; [2] we already have enough grain to feed tens of thousands for a hundred days."

sentences.zh: 佺期信之，乃率步騎八千，既至，仲堪惟以飯餉其軍。

translations.literal: Quanqi believed him and led eight thousand foot and horse; when they arrived, Zhongkan could only supply his army with cooked rice.
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi believed him and led eight thousand infantry and cavalry to Jiangling. When they arrived, Zhongkan could offer his army nothing but plain cooked rice.

sentences.zh: 佺期大怒曰：「今茲敗矣！」

translations.literal: Quanqi said in great anger: "We are defeated this day!"
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi flew into a rage and cried: "We are ruined!"

sentences.zh: 不過見仲堪，使人於艦上橫射玄，玄軍亦射之，佺期乃退。

translations.literal: Without going to see Zhongkan, he had men shoot across at Xuan from the ships; Xuan's army shot back as well, and Quanqi then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Without even meeting Zhongkan, he had his men fire across at Xuan from the ships. Xuan's army returned fire, and Quanqi then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 玄乃渡軍於馬頭，命其諸軍進，破殺仲堪，殺楊廣、佺期、殷道護及仲堪參軍羅企生等。

translations.literal: Xuan then crossed his army at Matou, ordered his various armies to advance, defeated and killed Zhongkan, and killed Yang Guang, Quanqi, Yin Daohu, and Zhongkan's staff officer Luo Qisheng and others.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan then crossed his army at Matou and ordered his forces forward. He defeated and killed Zhongkan, along with Yang Guang, Quanqi, Yin Daohu, and Zhongkan's staff officer Luo Qisheng and others.

sentences.zh: 德宗以玄為持節、都督荊司雍秦梁益寧江八州及揚豫并八郡諸軍事、[3]後將軍、荊江二州刺史。

translations.literal: Dezong appointed Xuan Bearer of the Staff, Commander of military affairs in the eight provinces of Jing, Si, Yong, Qin, Liang, Yi, Ning, and Jiang and eight commanderies of Yang and Yu, [3] General of the Rear, and Inspector of the two provinces of Jing and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong appointed Xuan Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs in the eight provinces of Jing, Si, Yong, Qin, Liang, Yi, Ning, and Jiang plus eight commanderies in Yang and Yu, [3] General of the Rear, and Inspector of both Jing and Jiang provinces.

sentences.zh: 玄大論功賞，以長史卞範之領南郡相，委以心膂之任。

translations.literal: Xuan greatly discussed rewards for merit, making his chief clerk Bian Fanzhi Administrator of Nan commandery and entrusting him with duties at the very core.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan handsomely rewarded his followers, appointing his chief clerk Bian Fanzhi Administrator of Nan commandery and entrusting him with his most confidential responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 乃斷上流，禁商旅。

translations.literal: He then cut off the upper reaches and prohibited merchants and travelers.
translations.idiomatic: He then blockaded the upper Yangtze and barred merchant traffic.

sentences.zh: 德宗下書曰：「豎子桓玄，故大司馬不腆之息，少懷狡惡，長而不悛，遂與王恭協同姦謀，阻兵內侮，三方雲集，志在問鼎，窺擬神器。

translations.literal: Dezong issued a decree saying: "The stripling Huan Xuan, unworthy scion of the late Grand Marshal, harbored cunning wickedness in youth and did not reform in maturity; he then joined Wang Gong in wicked plotting, blocked the army and insulted the court within, with forces gathering from three directions, his aim to inquire of the tripod and his gaze fixed on the sacred regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong issued an edict: "The stripling Huan Xuan, unworthy son of the late Grand Marshal, was treacherous from youth and unrepentant in manhood. He conspired with Wang Gong, raised troops against the court, and gathered forces from three directions with the aim of seizing the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 賴祖宗威靈，宰傅神略，忠義奮發，罪人斯殞。

translations.literal: Relying on the august spirits of the ancestors and the divine strategy of the chief ministers, the loyal and righteous rose up and the guilty perished.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to the august power of our ancestors and the wise strategy of the chief ministers, the loyal rose up and the guilty were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 玄等猖狂失圖，回舟鳥逝。

translations.literal: Xuan and the rest, reckless and without plan, turned their boats and fled like birds.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan and his allies, reckless and bereft of strategy, turned their boats and fled like startled birds.

sentences.zh: 便宜乘會，殲除姦源，于時同異之論，用惑廟策，遂使王憲廢撓，寵授非所。

translations.literal: It would have been fitting to seize the occasion and exterminate the source of treachery; at that time conflicting opinions confused the court's policy, so that royal statutes were abandoned and favor was granted where it should not have been.
translations.idiomatic: The court should have seized the moment to destroy the source of treachery. Conflicting opinions at the time confused imperial policy, royal authority was undermined, and rewards were granted to the wrong men.

sentences.zh: 猶冀玄當洗濯胸腑，小懲大誡，而狼心弗革，悖慢愈甚，割據江湘，擅威荊郢，矯命稱制，與奪在手。

translations.literal: Still it was hoped Xuan would cleanse his breast and accept small punishment as great warning, but his wolfish heart did not change and his insolence grew ever worse; he carved out the Jiang and Xiang, wielded power over Jing and Ying, forged orders and assumed regency, with granting and taking in his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: The court still hoped Xuan would repent and accept correction, but his wolfish heart never changed and his insolence only grew. He carved out the Jiang and Xiang regions, wielded unchecked power over Jing and Ying, forged imperial orders, and held the power of life and death in his own hands.

sentences.zh: 又對侍中王謐放肆醜言，欲縱凶毒，陵陷上京。

translations.literal: Moreover, facing the Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Mi, he uttered vile words without restraint, wishing to unleash vicious harm and overrun the upper capital.
translations.idiomatic: He even spoke vilely and without restraint to the Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Mi, plotting vicious harm and an assault on the capital.

sentences.zh: 無君之心，形於音翰；

translations.literal: His heart without a lord was manifest in his written words;
translations.idiomatic: His disloyalty was plain in his written words;

sentences.zh: 不臣之迹，日月彌著。

translations.literal: his acts as no subject grew daily more evident.
translations.idiomatic: and his treasonous conduct grew more evident by the day.

sentences.zh: 是可忍也，孰不可懷！

translations.literal: If this can be borne, what cannot be borne in the heart!
translations.idiomatic: If this can be tolerated, what outrage cannot?!

sentences.zh: 宜明九伐，以寧西夏。

translations.literal: It is fitting to proclaim the nine punishments and thereby pacify the western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Let the nine punishments be proclaimed to restore order to the realm.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、後將軍元顯可為征討大都督、督十八州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司。」

translations.literal: The Minister of Works and General of the Rear Yuanxian may serve as Grand Commander of the punitive expedition, Commander of military affairs in eighteen provinces, General of Agile Cavalry, and with ritual equal to the Three Excellencies."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian, Minister of Works and General of the Rear, is appointed Grand Commander of the punitive expedition, commander of military affairs in eighteen provinces, General of Agile Cavalry, with ritual honors equal to the Three Excellencies."

sentences.zh: 以劉牢之為前鋒，行征西將軍，權領江州；

translations.literal: Liu Laozhi was made vanguard, acting General Who Conquers the West, with provisional authority over Jiang province;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi was appointed vanguard, acting General Who Conquers the West with provisional authority over Jiang province;

sentences.zh: 命司馬尚之入沔水。

translations.literal: Sima Shangzhi was ordered to enter the Mian waters.
translations.idiomatic: and Sima Shangzhi was ordered to advance up the Mian River.

sentences.zh: 玄聞元顯處分，甚駭懼，欲保江陵。

translations.literal: When Xuan heard of Yuanxian's dispositions, he was greatly alarmed and wished to hold Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan heard of Yuanxian's deployments, he was deeply alarmed and considered holding Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 長史卞範之說玄東下，玄甚狐疑，範之苦勸，玄乃留桓偉守江陵，率軍東下。

translations.literal: His chief clerk Bian Fanzhi urged Xuan to march east; Xuan was very hesitant, but Fanzhi pressed him hard, and Xuan then left Huan Wei to guard Jiangling and led his army east.
translations.idiomatic: His chief clerk Bian Fanzhi urged him to march east. Xuan hesitated, but Fanzhi pressed him insistently. Xuan left Huan Wei to guard Jiangling and led his army eastward.

sentences.zh: 至夏口，乃建牙傳檄曰：

translations.literal: Reaching Xiakou, he raised his standard and issued a proclamation saying:
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Xiakou, he raised his standard and issued a proclamation:

sentences.zh: 案揚州刺史元顯：凶暴之性，自幼加長；

translations.literal: We charge the Inspector of Yang province Yuanxian: his violent and cruel nature has grown since childhood;
translations.idiomatic: We charge Sima Yuanxian, Inspector of Yang province: his violent and cruel nature has grown since childhood;

sentences.zh: 犯禮毀教，發蒙如備。

translations.literal: he violates ritual and destroys instruction, and from the first awakening of understanding he has been fully prepared in wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: he has violated ritual and destroyed moral instruction, and from his earliest years he has been steeped in wickedness.

sentences.zh: 居喪無一日之哀，衰絰為宵征之服，絃觴於殷憂之時，窮色於罔極之日，劫略王國寶妓妾一朝空房，此基惡之始，駭愕視聽者矣。

translations.literal: In mourning he showed not a day's grief; he wore sackcloth as garb for night marches, strummed lutes and raised cups in the midst of deep sorrow, pursued pleasures to the utmost on the day of greatest grief, and plundered the concubines of Wang Guobao so that the palace stood empty in a morning—this was the beginning of his accumulated evil, shocking to all who saw and heard.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning he showed not a day of grief. He wore mourning garb on night expeditions, played music and drank wine in the midst of bereavement, pursued pleasures on the day of greatest mourning, and plundered Wang Guobao's concubines so that the palace stood empty overnight. This was the beginning of his accumulated evil, shocking to all who witnessed it.

sentences.zh: 相王有疾，情無悚懼，幸災擅命，揚州篡授，遂乃父子同錄，比肩連案。

translations.literal: When the Prince Regent fell ill, he felt no fear or dread; rejoicing in disaster, he usurped authority, seized Yang province by force, and father and son were recorded together, shoulder to shoulder in the same case.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince Regent fell ill, he felt no fear. Rejoicing in disaster, he seized power, forcibly took Yang province, and father and son were implicated together in the same charges.

sentences.zh: 既專權重，多行險暴，恐相王知之，杜絕視聽。

translations.literal: Having monopolized heavy power, he often acted with dangerous violence, fearing the Prince Regent would learn of it, and cut off his sight and hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held sole power, he often acted with dangerous violence. Fearing the Prince Regent would learn of his conduct, he cut off his access to information.

sentences.zh: 惡聲無聞，佞譽日至。

translations.literal: Evil reports did not reach him; flatterers' praise came daily.
translations.idiomatic: Reports of wrongdoing never reached him, while flatterers' praise arrived daily.

sentences.zh: 萬機之重，委之厮孽，國典朝政，紛紜淆亂。

translations.literal: The weight of ten thousand affairs he entrusted to base minions; state statutes and court governance were thrown into confusion.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted the weight of state affairs to base minions, and national statutes and court governance fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 又諷旨尚書，使普敬錄公。

translations.literal: He also instructed the Minister of Works to have all pay full respect to the Duke who Records Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also instructed the Minister of Works to have everyone pay full ceremonial respect to the Duke who Records Affairs.

sentences.zh: 錄公之位，非盡敬之所。

translations.literal: The position of Duke who Records Affairs is not one to which full respect is owed.
translations.idiomatic: The position of Duke who Records Affairs does not warrant such full ceremonial respect.

sentences.zh: 苟自尊貴，遂悖朝禮。

translations.literal: Merely to aggrandize himself, he thus violated court ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Merely to aggrandize himself, he violated court ritual.

sentences.zh: 又妖賊陵縱，破軍殄民之後，己為都督，親則刺史，於宜降之日，輒加崇進。

translations.literal: Moreover, when rebel bandits ran rampant, after armies were broken and people exterminated, he himself was made Commander and his intimates made Inspectors; on days when demotion was fitting, he promptly promoted them further.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel bandits ran rampant and armies were destroyed and people slaughtered, he made himself Commander and his intimates Inspectors. On days when demotion was called for, he promoted them instead.

sentences.zh: 弱冠之年，古今莫比。

translations.literal: At the age of weak cap, unmatched in past and present.
translations.idiomatic: At such a young age, his conduct was unmatched in history.

sentences.zh: 宰相懲惡，己獨解錄，推禍委罰，歸之有在，自古僭逆未有若斯之甚者。

translations.literal: When the chief minister punished evil, he alone was released from the Record; he pushed blame and shifted punishment onto others who were at fault—never in antiquity or today has usurpation and rebellion reached such extremity.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief minister punished wrongdoing, Yuanxian alone was released from the Record. He pushed blame onto others—never in history has treason reached such an extreme.

sentences.zh: 取妾之僭，殆同六禮，及使尚書僕射為媒人，長史為迎客，嬖媵饕餮，賀同長秋，所謂無君之心，觸事而發。

translations.literal: His usurpation in taking concubines nearly equaled the six rites; he even made the Vice Minister of Works his matchmaker and the chief clerk his guest-receiver; his favorites feasted gluttonously and were congratulated as if they were the Empress—this is what is called a heart without a lord, breaking out at every turn.
translations.idiomatic: His taking of concubines nearly followed the full six rites of marriage. He made the Vice Minister of Works his matchmaker and his chief clerk his guest-receiver. His favorites feasted gluttonously and were congratulated as if they were the empress. This is what is meant by a disloyal heart that reveals itself in every act.

sentences.zh: 八日觀佛，略人子女，至人家宿，唐突婦妾。

translations.literal: On the eighth-day Buddha viewing he seized people's sons and daughters, lodged in others' homes, and offended against wives and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth-day Buddha-viewing festival he seized people's sons and daughters, lodged in private homes, and assaulted wives and concubines.

sentences.zh: 慶封迄今，甫見易室之飲；

translations.literal: From Qing Feng until now, only now has the drinking of another man's house been seen;
translations.idiomatic: Since the days of Qing Feng, only now has such drinking in another man's house been seen;

sentences.zh: 晉靈以來，忽有支解之刑。

translations.literal: since Jin Ling, suddenly there has been the punishment of dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: and since Emperor Ling of Jin, there has suddenly been the punishment of dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 喜怒輕戮，人士割裂，治城之暴，一睡而斬。

translations.literal: In joy and anger he lightly executed; gentlemen were torn apart; the cruelty at Zhicheng—men were beheaded after a single nap.
translations.idiomatic: He executed on whim, tore gentlemen apart, and at Zhicheng men were beheaded after he merely took a nap.

sentences.zh: 又以四歲孽子，興東海之封。

translations.literal: Moreover, with a four-year-old bastard son, he raised the fief of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed a four-year-old bastard son as lord of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 吳興殘暴之後，橫復若斯之調。

translations.literal: After the cruelty at Wuxing, he again imposed levies such as these.
translations.idiomatic: After the cruelty at Wuxing, he imposed levies such as these once more.

sentences.zh: 妖賊之興，實由此竪。

translations.literal: The rise of rebel bandits in truth stems from this stripling.
translations.idiomatic: The rise of rebel bandits stems in truth from this stripling.

sentences.zh: 居喪極味，孫泰供其膳；

translations.literal: In mourning he sought the utmost flavors; Sun Tai supplied his meals;
translations.idiomatic: During mourning he sought the finest foods; Sun Tai supplied his meals;

sentences.zh: 在夜思遊，亦孫泰延其駕。

translations.literal: at night when he wished to roam, Sun Tai also extended his carriage.
translations.idiomatic: and when he wished to roam at night, Sun Tai provided his carriage as well.

sentences.zh: 泰承其勢，得行威福，雖加誅戮，所染既多。

translations.literal: Tai relied on his power and was able to wield authority and favor; though he was put to death, those he had corrupted were already many.
translations.idiomatic: Tai relied on Yuanxian's power to wield authority and favor. Though he was eventually executed, many had already been corrupted by him.

sentences.zh: 加之以苦發樂屬，枉濫者眾，驅逐徙撥，死叛殆盡。

translations.literal: Added to this were harsh levies of music households; those wrongly condemned were many; driven out and relocated, the dead and deserters were nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: He imposed harsh levies of musician households, wrongly condemned many, and through forced relocation and exile left the region nearly depopulated by death and desertion.

sentences.zh: 改號元興，以為己瑞，莽之符命，於斯尤著。

translations.literal: He changed the era name to Yuanxing, taking it as his own auspice; Wang Mang's mandate of fate was never more evident than in this.
translations.idiomatic: He changed the era name to Yuanxing, taking it as his own auspicious sign. Wang Mang's usurpation was never more clearly echoed than in this.

sentences.zh: 否極必亨，天盈其毒，不義不昵，勢必崩喪，取亂侮亡，實在斯會。

translations.literal: When obstruction reaches its limit, prosperity must come; Heaven fills up his poison; what is unrighteous and unkind must collapse and perish; to take disorder and insult the perishing—truly the moment is now.
translations.idiomatic: When obstruction reaches its limit, prosperity must follow. Heaven has filled him with poison. What is unrighteous cannot endure. To seize disorder and overthrow the doomed—truly the moment is now.

sentences.zh: 三軍文武，憤踊即路。

translations.literal: The civil and military of the three armies, indignant and eager, set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The civil and military officers of the three armies, indignant and eager, march forth.

sentences.zh: 玄亦失荊楚人情，而師出不順，其兵雖強，慮弗為用，恒有回師之計。

translations.literal: Xuan had also lost the hearts of the people of Jing and Chu, and his expedition was ill-omened; though his troops were strong, he feared they would not be used, and constantly planned to turn his army back.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had also lost the loyalty of the people of Jing and Chu, and his campaign lacked popular support. Though his army was strong, he feared his troops would not fight willingly and constantly considered turning back.

sentences.zh: 既過尋陽，不見東軍，玄意乃定。

translations.literal: After he passed Xunyang and did not see the eastern army, Xuan's mind was settled.
translations.idiomatic: After he passed Xunyang without encountering the eastern army, his resolve steadied.

sentences.zh: 於是遂鼓行而進，徑至姑熟，又克歷陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he beat the drums and advanced, going straight to Gushu, and also captured Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then beat the drums and advanced, marching straight to Gushu and capturing Liyang.

sentences.zh: 劉牢之遣子敬宣詣玄請降，玄大喜，與敬宣置酒宴集。

translations.literal: Liu Laozhi sent his son Jingxuan to Xuan to request surrender; Xuan was greatly pleased and held a banquet with Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi sent his son Jingxuan to Xuan to offer surrender. Xuan was delighted and held a banquet with Jingxuan.

sentences.zh: 玄至新亭，元顯棄船，退入國子堂，列陳宣陽門前。

translations.literal: When Xuan reached Xinting, Yuanxian abandoned his boats, withdrew into the Hall of the National University, and arrayed his formations before the Xuanyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan reached Xinting, Yuanxian abandoned his boats, withdrew into the Hall of the National University, and drew up his formations before the Xuanyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 元顯欲挾德宗出戰，而軍中相驚，言玄已及南桁，乃回軍赴宮。

translations.literal: Yuanxian wished to take Dezong out to battle, but the army was mutually alarmed, saying Xuan had already reached the southern bridge, and they turned their army back toward the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian wished to take Dezong out to battle, but panic spread through the army with reports that Xuan had already reached the southern bridge. The troops turned back toward the palace.

sentences.zh: 既至中堂，一時崩散。

translations.literal: When they reached the Central Hall, the army collapsed and scattered all at once.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the Central Hall, the army collapsed and scattered.

sentences.zh: 元顯奔東府，惟張法順一騎隨之。

translations.literal: Yuanxian fled to the Eastern Palace; only Zhang Fashun on a single horse followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian fled to the Eastern Palace with only Zhang Fashun on a single horse following him.

sentences.zh: 玄乃為侍中、都督中外諸軍、丞相、錄尚書事、揚州牧、領徐州刺史，持節、荊江二州、公如故；

translations.literal: Xuan was then made Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander of all armies at home and abroad, Chancellor, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Governor of Yang province, and concurrent Inspector of Xu province, Bearer of the Staff, with his two provinces of Jing and Jiang and his dukedom as before;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was then appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary, commander of all armies at home and abroad, Chancellor, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Governor of Yang province, and concurrent Inspector of Xu province, with his titles in Jing and Jiang provinces and his dukedom unchanged;

sentences.zh: 假黃鉞、羽葆、鼓吹、班劍二十人；

translations.literal: he was given provisional use of the yellow axe, feather canopy, drums and pipes, and twenty guards with patterned swords.
translations.idiomatic: and granted provisional use of the yellow axe, feather canopy, drums and pipes, and twenty guards bearing patterned swords.

sentences.zh: 置左右長史，從事中郎四人；

translations.literal: He appointed left and right Chief Secretaries and four Attendants of the Masters of Writing;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed left and right Chief Secretaries and four Attendants of the Masters of Writing;

sentences.zh: 甲仗二百人入殿。

translations.literal: Two hundred armored guards were permitted to enter the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred armored guards were authorized to enter the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 於是收道子付廷尉，免為庶人，徙于安城郡；

translations.literal: Thereupon he arrested Daozi and handed him over to the Court of Judicial Review, deposed him to commoner status, and banished him to Ancheng commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he arrested Sima Daozi and handed him over to the Court of Judicial Review, stripped him of rank, and banished him to Ancheng commandery;

sentences.zh: 殺元顯并其子，及豫州刺史司馬尚之、吏部郎袁遵、張法順等。

translations.literal: He killed Yuanxian together with his sons, and the Inspector of Yu province Sima Shangzhi, the Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel Yuan Zun, Zhang Fashun, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Yuanxian along with his sons, as well as Sima Shangzhi, Inspector of Yu province, Yuan Zun, Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, Zhang Fashun, and others.

sentences.zh: 又滅庾楷於豫章。

translations.literal: He also destroyed Yu Kai at Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He also eliminated Yu Kai at Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 徙尚之弟丹楊尹恢之、輔國將軍允之，及國寶、王緒諸子于交、廣州。

translations.literal: He banished Shangzhi's younger brothers Huizhi, Governor of Danyang, and Yunzhi, General Who Supports the State, together with the sons of Guobao and Wang Xu, to Jiao and Guang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He banished Shangzhi's brothers—Huizhi, Governor of Danyang, and Yunzhi, General Who Supports the State—as well as the sons of Guobao and Wang Xu, to Jiao and Guang provinces.

sentences.zh: 以劉牢之為會稽內史，將欲解其兵也。

translations.literal: He made Liu Laozhi Administrator of Kuaiji, intending to disarm him.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Liu Laozhi Administrator of Kuaiji, intending thereby to strip him of his military command.

sentences.zh: 初，敬宣既降，隨入東府，至是求歸。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Jingxuan had surrendered, he followed Xuan into the Eastern Palace; now he requested to return.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Jingxuan had surrendered, he had accompanied Xuan into the Eastern Palace; at this time he asked to return home.

sentences.zh: 玄冀牢之受命，乃遣之。

translations.literal: Xuan hoped Laozhi would accept the order, and so sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan hoped Laozhi would accept the appointment, and so allowed him to depart.

sentences.zh: 敬宣既至，牢之知將不免，欲襲玄，眾皆離散，乃於班瀆北走，縊於新洲。

translations.literal: When Jingxuan arrived, Laozhi knew he would not escape, wished to launch a surprise attack on Xuan, but his followers all scattered; he fled north of Banpu and hanged himself on Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingxuan arrived, Laozhi knew he could not escape. He planned a surprise attack on Xuan, but his followers deserted him. He fled north of Banpu and hanged himself on Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 傳首建鄴。

translations.literal: His head was sent to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: His severed head was sent to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 敬宣奔於江北。

translations.literal: Jingxuan fled to the north of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan fled across the Yangzi to the north bank.

sentences.zh: 玄白德宗，大赦，改年為大亨。

translations.literal: Xuan reported to Dezong, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the reign title to Dading.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan reported to Dezong, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Dading.

sentences.zh: 玄讓丞相、荊江徐三州及錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Xuan yielded the chancellorship, the three provinces of Jing, Jiang, and Xu, and the post of Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan resigned the chancellorship, his jurisdictions over Jing, Jiang, and Xu provinces, and the post of Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 乃改授太尉、都督中外、揚州牧、領平西將軍、豫州刺史；

translations.literal: He was then reassigned as Grand Marshal, Commander-in-Chief at home and abroad, Governor of Yang province, concurrent General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Yu province;
translations.idiomatic: He was then reassigned as Grand Marshal, commander-in-chief at home and abroad, Governor of Yang province, concurrent General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Yu province;

sentences.zh: 綠綟綬，加袞冕之服，劍履之禮，入朝不趨，讚拜不名，增班劍六十人，甲仗二百人入殿。

translations.literal: with a green ribbon bearing red tassels, granted the robe and cap of the Son of Heaven, the privilege of wearing sword and shoes in the presence of the emperor, exemption from quickening pace when entering court, exemption from having his name called when praised at audience, an increase of sixty guards with patterned swords, and two hundred armored guards permitted to enter the hall.
translations.idiomatic: with a green ribbon bearing red tassels, along with the imperial robe and cap, the privilege of wearing sword and shoes in the emperor's presence, exemption from quickening pace when entering court and from having his name called in formal addresses, sixty additional guards bearing patterned swords, and authorization for two hundred armored guards to enter the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 玄乃鎮姑熟。

translations.literal: Xuan then established his headquarters at Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan then established his base at Gushu.

sentences.zh: 既而大築府第，田遊無度，政令屢改，驕侈肆欲，朋黨翕習，沮亂內外。

translations.literal: Before long he built great mansions on a vast scale, indulged in hunting without limit, changed edicts repeatedly, was arrogant and extravagant and gave free rein to his desires, his cliques banded together in habit, and threw court and realm into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he built enormous estates and indulged in reckless hunting, issuing and revoking edicts at whim. Arrogant, extravagant, and driven by every appetite, his cliques grew entrenched and threw the court and realm into chaos.

sentences.zh: 朝政皆諮焉，小事則決於左僕射桓謙及丹陽尹卞範之。

translations.literal: All court affairs were referred to him; minor matters were decided by the Left Vice Director Huan Qian and the Governor of Danyang Bian Fanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: All matters of state were referred to him; minor affairs were decided by Huan Qian, Left Vice Director, and Bian Fanzhi, Governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 玄大賦三吳富室，以賑飢民，猶不能濟也。

translations.literal: Xuan heavily taxed the wealthy households of the Three Wu region to relieve the starving people, yet still could not provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan levied crushing taxes on the wealthy households of the Three Wu region to feed the starving populace, yet still could not staunch the famine.

sentences.zh: 東郡既由兵掠，因以飢饉，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: The eastern commanderies, having been ravaged by troops, consequently suffered famine, and very many died.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern commanderies, having been plundered by armies, suffered famine afterward, and vast numbers perished.

sentences.zh: 三吳戶口減半，會稽則十三四，臨海、永嘉死散殆盡。

translations.literal: The registered households of the Three Wu were halved; in Kuaiji only three or four tenths remained; in Linhai and Yongjia the dead and scattered were nearly all gone.
translations.idiomatic: The registered population of the Three Wu region was cut in half; in Kuaiji only thirty or forty percent remained; in Linhai and Yongjia the dead and displaced nearly wiped out the populace entirely.

sentences.zh: 諸舊富室皆衣羅縠，佩金玉，相守閉門而死。

translations.literal: All the old wealthy families wore silk gauze and adorned themselves with gold and jade, locking their gates and dying together within.
translations.idiomatic: The old wealthy families dressed in silks and adorned themselves with gold and jade, then barred their gates and died together within.

sentences.zh: 玄自封豫章郡公，食安成七千五百戶；

translations.literal: Xuan enfeoffed himself as Duke of Yuzhang commandery, with a fief income of seven thousand five hundred households in Ancheng;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan enfeoffed himself as Duke of Yuzhang commandery, with a fief of seven thousand five hundred households in Ancheng;

sentences.zh: 後封桂陽郡公，邑二千五百戶；

translations.literal: later enfeoffed as Duke of Guiyang commandery, with an estate of two thousand five hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: and later as Duke of Guiyang commandery, with an estate of two thousand five hundred households;

sentences.zh: 本封南郡如故。

translations.literal: his original enfeoffment as Duke of Nan commandery remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: while his original title as Duke of Nan commandery remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 既而鴆殺道子。

translations.literal: Before long he poisoned Daozi to death.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he poisoned Sima Daozi to death.

sentences.zh: 玄削奪德宗供奉之具，務盡約陋，殆至飢寒。

translations.literal: Xuan stripped away Dezong's supplies for imperial service, striving to make everything as spare and shabby as possible, nearly to the point of hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan stripped away Dezong's provisions for imperial maintenance, reducing everything to the barest and shabbiest, nearly leaving him in hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 雖殺逆未至，君臣之體盡矣。

translations.literal: Although regicide had not yet been carried out, the forms of ruler and minister were utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Although he had not yet committed regicide, the norms of ruler and subject had been utterly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 進位大將軍，加前後部羽葆鼓吹，奏事不名。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand General, given drums, pipes, and feather canopy before and behind his carriage, and when presenting memorials his name was not to be called.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand General, granted drums, pipes, and feather canopy before and behind his carriage, and exempted from having his name called when presenting memorials.

sentences.zh: 又表請自率諸軍，命諸蕃方兵掃平關洛，德宗不許之。

translations.literal: He also submitted a memorial requesting to lead the armies himself and order the regional forces of all territories to sweep clear Guan and Luo; Dezong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned to lead the armies in person and order regional forces from all directions to reconquer Guanzhong and Luoyang; Dezong refused.

sentences.zh: 玄本無資力，但好為大言，既不辦行，乃云奉詔故止。

translations.literal: Xuan in truth had no resources or strength, but only loved grand talk; unable to carry it out, he then said he stopped because he received an imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan in fact had neither the resources nor the ability for such a campaign and loved nothing but grand rhetoric. Unable to act, he claimed he stopped because the emperor had so ordered.

sentences.zh: 玄既無他處分，先作征行服玩，并制裝書畫之具。

translations.literal: Since Xuan had no other arrangement, he first made campaign garments and playthings, and also prepared outfits and implements for books and paintings.
translations.idiomatic: Having no other plan, Xuan had campaign garments and curios made in advance, along with traveling kits for his books and paintings.

sentences.zh: 或諫曰：「今日之行，必有征無戰，輜重自足相運，不煩復有制造。」

translations.literal: Someone remonstrated: "On today's campaign there will surely be expedition without battle; baggage trains suffice to transport supplies—there is no need to manufacture more."
translations.idiomatic: Someone remonstrated: "This campaign will surely meet no resistance; supply trains can carry everything needed—there is no need to manufacture more."

sentences.zh: 玄曰：「書畫服玩，宜恒在左右，且兵凶戰危，脫有意外，當使輕而易運。」

translations.literal: Xuan said: "Books, paintings, garments, and curios should always be kept at hand; besides, war is perilous—if some mishap occurs, they should be light and easy to transport."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan replied: "My books, paintings, garments, and curios should always stay close at hand. War is perilous—if mishap strikes, they must be light enough to move quickly."

sentences.zh: 眾咸笑之。

translations.literal: All laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd all laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 玄所親仗，惟桓偉而已，先欲徵還，以自副貳。

translations.literal: Of those Xuan relied upon, only Huan Wei remained; he had earlier wished to summon him back to serve as his second.
translations.idiomatic: Of those Xuan truly relied upon, only Huan Wei remained. He had earlier planned to recall Wei to serve as his second-in-command.

sentences.zh: 偉既死，玄甚恇懼。

translations.literal: When Wei died, Xuan was greatly fearful and apprehensive.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei died, Xuan grew deeply fearful and apprehensive.

sentences.zh: 初，玄常以其父王業垂成，以己弱年，不昌前構，常懷恨憤。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xuan had often felt that his father's royal enterprise was nearly accomplished, yet he himself was young and did not bring to completion what had been built before, and he constantly harbored resentment and anger.
translations.idiomatic: For years Xuan had brooded that his father's imperial enterprise was nearly complete, yet he himself, still young, had failed to carry forward what had been begun, and he harbored constant resentment.

sentences.zh: 及昌明死，便有四方之計，既克建業，無復居下之心。

translations.literal: When Changming died, he already had designs on all four directions; having taken Jiankang, he no longer had a mind to remain below others.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu died, he already plotted to seize power across the realm. Having taken Jiankang, he no longer had any intention of remaining subordinate.

sentences.zh: 及偉死，慮一己單危，益欲速成大業。

translations.literal: When Wei died, fearing he stood alone in peril, he all the more wished to complete his great enterprise quickly.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei died, fearful that he stood alone and exposed, he grew all the more eager to complete his usurpation quickly.

sentences.zh: 卞範之之徒，既慮事變，且幸其利，咸共催促，於是殷仲文等並已撰集策命矣。

translations.literal: Bian Fanzhi and his ilk, both fearing a change of affairs and hoping for their own profit, all urged him on together; by then Yin Zhongwen and the others had already compiled the texts of the investiture decree.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Fanzhi and his circle, fearing a turn of events yet eager for their own gain, all urged him forward. By then Yin Zhongwen and others had already drafted the investiture documents.

sentences.zh: 德宗加玄相國，總百揆，封南郡、南平、宜都、天門、零陵、桂陽、營陽、衡陽、義陽、建平十郡為楚王，備九錫之禮，揚州牧、領平西將軍、豫州刺史如故。

translations.literal: Dezong advanced Xuan to Chancellor of State, giving him charge of all affairs of state, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Chu over the ten commanderies of Nan, Nanping, Yidu, Tianmen, Lingling, Guiyang, Yingyang, Hengyang, Yiyang, and Jianping, with the ritual of the nine bestowments; his posts as Governor of Yang, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Yu remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong advanced Xuan to Chancellor of State with authority over all government affairs, enfeoffing him as Prince of Chu over ten commanderies—Nan, Nanping, Yidu, Tianmen, Lingling, Guiyang, Yingyang, Hengyang, Yiyang, and Jianping—with the full ritual of the nine bestowments, while his titles as Governor of Yang, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Yu remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 遣司徒王謐授相國印綬，光祿大夫武陵王司馬遵授楚王璽策。

translations.literal: He sent the Minister of Works Wang Mi to present the seals and cords of Chancellor of State; the Household Minister of the Principality of Wuling, Sima Zun, presented the princely seal and investiture document of the Prince of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Wang Mi, Minister of Works, to present the seals and cords of Chancellor of State, and Sima Zun, Household Minister of the Principality of Wuling, to deliver the Prince of Chu's seal and investiture charter.

sentences.zh: 德宗先遣百僚固請，又云當親幸敦喻。

translations.literal: Dezong had earlier sent all officials to press their requests firmly, and also said he would personally come to urge and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong had earlier sent the entire bureaucracy to press their petitions, and also announced that he would come in person to urge acceptance.

sentences.zh: 十二月，德宗禪位於玄，大赦所部，稱永始元年。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Dezong abdicated the throne to Xuan, proclaimed a general amnesty within his domain, and the era was called Yongshi, first year.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Dezong abdicated in Xuan's favor, proclaimed a general amnesty within his domain, and adopted the era name Yongshi.

sentences.zh: 初欲改年為建始，左丞王納之曰：「建始者，晉趙王倫之號也。」

translations.literal: At first he wished to change the era name to Jianshi; the Left Assistant Director Wang Nazhi said: "Jianshi was the era name of the Jin Prince of Zhao, Lun."
translations.idiomatic: At first he wished to adopt the era name Jianshi. The Left Assistant Director Wang Nazhi said: "Jianshi was the era name of Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao under Jin."

sentences.zh: 於是易為永始，復同王莽始貴之年。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was changed to Yongshi, again matching the year when Wang Mang first rose to prominence.
translations.idiomatic: It was therefore changed to Yongshi, coinciding again with the year when Wang Mang first rose to prominence.

sentences.zh: 玄入建鄴宮，逆風迅激，旌旗、服章、儀飾一皆傾偃。

translations.literal: When Xuan entered the Jiankang palace, a contrary wind blew fierce and swift, and banners, regalia, and ceremonial ornaments all toppled flat.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan entered the Jiankang palace, a headwind blew fierce and swift, and banners, regalia, and ceremonial ornaments all toppled flat.

sentences.zh: 是月酷寒，此日尤甚。

translations.literal: That month was bitterly cold; that day was especially so.
translations.idiomatic: That month was bitterly cold; that day was especially severe.

sentences.zh: 多行苛政而時施小惠。

translations.literal: He issued many harsh policies yet from time to time granted small favors.
translations.idiomatic: He imposed harsh policies while occasionally granting petty favors.

sentences.zh: 迎溫神主進于太廟。

translations.literal: He welcomed Wen's spirit tablet and brought it into the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He welcomed Huan Wen's spirit tablet and installed it in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 玄遊行無度，至此不出。

translations.literal: Xuan's excursions had been without limit; at this time he did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had always traveled without restraint; for once he did not go out.

sentences.zh: 殿上施金額流蘇絳帳，頗類轜車、王莽仙蓋。

translations.literal: In the hall he hung a crimson canopy with gold bands and hanging tassels, rather resembling Wang Mang's carriage canopy and immortal canopy.
translations.idiomatic: In the hall he hung a crimson canopy with gold bands and hanging tassels, closely resembling Wang Mang's carriage canopy.

sentences.zh: 太廟、郊齋皆二日而已。

translations.literal: Offerings at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and suburban altar both lasted only two days.
translations.idiomatic: Rites at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and suburban altar each lasted only two days.

sentences.zh: 又其廟祭不及於祖，以玄曾祖已上名位不顯，故不列序。

translations.literal: Moreover, his temple sacrifices did not extend to his ancestors, because the names and ranks of those above his great-grandfather were not distinguished, and so they were not arrayed in order.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, his temple sacrifices did not honor his remote ancestors, because the names and ranks of his forebears above his great-grandfather were obscure, and so they were not installed in the temple.

sentences.zh: 且以王莽立九廟，見譏前史，遂以一廟矯之。

translations.literal: Moreover, because Wang Mang had established nine temples and was mocked in earlier histories, he therefore used a single temple as a corrective display.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wang Mang had been ridiculed in earlier histories for establishing nine temples, Xuan countered with a single temple only.

sentences.zh: 又毀僭晉小廟，以崇臺榭。

translations.literal: He also destroyed the small temples of the usurping Jin, to exalt his terraces and towers.
translations.idiomatic: He also demolished the minor Jin ancestral shrines to make way for new terraces and towers.

sentences.zh: 其庶母蒸嘗，未有定所。

translations.literal: The seasonal offerings for his father's concubine had no fixed place.
translations.idiomatic: The seasonal offerings for his concubine mother had no fixed place of worship.

sentences.zh: 慢祖忘親，時人知其不永。

translations.literal: Disrespecting his ancestors and forgetting his kin—contemporaries knew he would not last long.
translations.idiomatic: In slighting his ancestors and neglecting his kin, contemporaries knew he would not endure.

sentences.zh: 是月，玄出遊水南，飄風飛其儀蓋。

translations.literal: That month, as Xuan went on an excursion south of the water, a swirling wind blew away his ceremonial canopy.
translations.idiomatic: That month, while Xuan was traveling south of the water, a whirlwind tore away his ceremonial canopy.

sentences.zh: 又欲造大輦，使容三十人坐，以二百人輿之。

translations.literal: He also wished to build a great palanquin able to seat thirty people, borne by two hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: He also planned to build a great palanquin seating thirty people, carried by two hundred bearers.

sentences.zh: 玄驕逸荒縱，不恤時事，奏案停積，了不省覽；

translations.literal: Xuan was arrogant, dissolute, and wildly indulgent, heedless of current affairs; memorials piled up unattended, and he never looked at them at all;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan grew arrogant, dissolute, and recklessly indulgent, heedless of affairs of state. Memorials piled up unread;

sentences.zh: 或親細事，手注直官，自用令史，制度亂出，主司奉答不暇。

translations.literal: or he personally attended to trifling matters, annotating attendants in his own hand, appointing clerks at his own whim, issuing regulations haphazardly, so that responsible officials could not keep up with replies.
translations.idiomatic: or he micromanaged petty matters himself, annotating attendants in his own hand and appointing clerks at whim, issuing regulations without order until responsible officials could not keep pace.

sentences.zh: 晨夜遊獵，文武因乏。

translations.literal: He hunted day and night, and civil and military officers were exhausted thereby.
translations.idiomatic: He hunted day and night, leaving civil and military officers exhausted.

sentences.zh: 直侍之官，皆繫馬省中；

translations.literal: Attendants on immediate duty all tethered their horses within the palace compound;
translations.idiomatic: Attendants on immediate duty tethered their horses inside the palace compound;

sentences.zh: 休下之吏，留供土木之役。

translations.literal: officials who were off duty were kept to perform corvée labor in earthworks and timber.
translations.idiomatic: and officials supposedly off duty were kept behind for construction labor.

sentences.zh: 朝士勞瘁，百姓力盡，民之思亂，十室而八。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen were worn out with toil, the common people had exhausted their strength, and among the people eight of every ten households longed for rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials were worn to exhaustion, the common people drained of strength, and rebellion stirred in eight out of every ten households.

sentences.zh: 德宗彭城內史劉裕因是斬徐州刺史桓脩於京口，與沛國劉毅、東海何無忌收眾濟江。

translations.literal: Dezong's Administrator of Pengcheng within the commandery, Liu Yu, took advantage of this to behead Huan Xiu, Inspector of Xu province, at Jingkou, and together with Liu Yi of Pei and He Wuji of Donghai gathered forces and crossed the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, Administrator of Pengcheng, seized the moment to behead Huan Xiu, Inspector of Xu province, at Jingkou. Together with Liu Yi of Pei and He Wuji of Donghai, he gathered troops and crossed the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 玄加桓謙征討都督，召侍官皆入止省中。

translations.literal: Xuan advanced Huan Qian to Commander of the punitive campaign, and summoned all attendants to enter and remain within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan appointed Huan Qian commander of the punitive campaign and summoned all palace attendants to remain within the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 玄移還上宮，百僚步從。

translations.literal: Xuan moved back to the Upper Palace, and all officials followed on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan moved back to the Upper Palace, with all officials following on foot.

sentences.zh: 赦揚、豫、徐、兗、青、冀六州。

translations.literal: He proclaimed amnesty in the six provinces of Yang, Yu, Xu, Yan, Qing, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed an amnesty in Yang, Yu, Xu, Yan, Qing, and Ji provinces.

sentences.zh: 遣頓丘太守吳甫之、右衞將軍皇甫敷北拒劉裕於江乘。

translations.literal: He sent the Administrator of Dunqiu Wu Fuzhi and the General of the Right Guard Huangfu Fu north to resist Liu Yu at Jiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wu Fuzhi, Administrator of Dunqiu, and Huangfu Fu, General of the Right Guard, north to block Liu Yu at Jiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 裕斬甫之，進至羅落橋，又梟敷首。

translations.literal: Yu beheaded Fuzhi, advanced to Luoluo Bridge, and also displayed Fu's severed head.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu beheaded Wu Fuzhi, advanced to Luoluo Bridge, and displayed Huangfu Fu's severed head.

sentences.zh: 玄外粗猛，內恇怯，及聞二將已沒，志慮荒窘，計無所出，日與巫術道士為厭勝之法。

translations.literal: Outwardly Xuan was fierce and bold, inwardly timid and fearful; when he heard both generals had perished, his mind and plans were frantic and confused, he could devise no plan, and daily joined shamans and Daoist masters in performing suppression rites.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly fierce, inwardly timid, when Xuan heard both generals had fallen, his mind went blank and his plans collapsed. He spent his days with shamans and Daoist priests performing occult rites of suppression.

sentences.zh: 乃謂眾曰：「朕其敗乎？」

translations.literal: He then said to the assembly: "Am I about to be defeated?"
translations.idiomatic: He then asked the assembly: "Am I about to be defeated?"

sentences.zh: 黃門郎曹靖對曰：「神怒民怨，臣實憂懼。」

translations.literal: The Gentleman of the Yellow Gates Cao Jing replied: "The spirits are angry and the people resentful; your servant is truly fearful."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jing, Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, replied: "The spirits are angry and the people resentful—I am truly afraid."

sentences.zh: 玄曰：「民怨可然，神何為怒？」

translations.literal: Xuan said: "Popular resentment is understandable, but why should the spirits be angry?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuan said: "Popular resentment I understand—but why should the spirits be angry?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「移晉宗廟，飄泊無所；

translations.literal: He replied: "You moved the Jin ancestral temples, and they drift without a resting place;
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "You displaced the Jin ancestral temples, leaving them adrift without a home;

sentences.zh: 大楚之祭，不及於祖。

translations.literal: the Great Chu sacrifices do not extend to the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: and the Great Chu's sacrifices do not honor its ancestors.

sentences.zh: 此其所以怒也。」

translations.literal: This is why they are angry."
translations.idiomatic: That is why they are angry."

sentences.zh: 玄曰：「卿何不諫？」

translations.literal: Xuan said: "Why did you not remonstrate?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuan said: "Why did you not remonstrate with me?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「輦上諸君子皆以為堯舜之世，臣何敢諫。」

translations.literal: He replied: "The gentlemen aboard your carriage all thought it was an age of Yao and Shun; how would your servant dare remonstrate?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "The gentlemen on your carriage all thought this an age of Yao and Shun—how could I dare remonstrate?"

sentences.zh: 玄使桓謙、何澹之屯于東掖門，[4]卞範之屯覆舟山西，眾合二萬。

translations.literal: Xuan stationed Huan Qian and He Tanzhi at the Eastern Side Gate [4], and Bian Fanzhi west of Fuzhou Mountain; their forces together numbered twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan stationed Huan Qian and He Tanzhi at the Eastern Side Gate [4] and Bian Fanzhi west of Fuzhou Mountain, with combined forces of twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 又遣武衞庾賾之配以精卒利器，援助謙等。

translations.literal: He also sent the Martial Guard Yu Zhenzhi with picked troops and fine weapons to reinforce Qian and the others.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Yu Zhenzhi of the Martial Guard with elite troops and fine weapons to reinforce them.

sentences.zh: 謙等大敗，玄聲云赴戰，將子姪出南掖門，西至石頭。

translations.literal: Qian and the others were utterly defeated; Xuan loudly proclaimed he was going to battle, took his sons and nephews out through the Southern Side Gate, and went west to Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: Qian and the others suffered a crushing defeat. Xuan loudly announced he was going to battle, led his sons and nephews out through the Southern Side Gate, and fled west to Stone City.

sentences.zh: 先使殷仲文具船於津，遂相與南走。

translations.literal: He had earlier ordered Yin Zhongwen to prepare boats at the ford; they then fled south together.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier ordered Yin Zhongwen to prepare boats at the crossing; they then fled south together.

sentences.zh: 經日不得食，左右進以粗粥，咽不能下。

translations.literal: For a whole day they had nothing to eat; attendants brought coarse porridge, but he could not swallow it down.
translations.idiomatic: For a full day they had nothing to eat. When attendants brought coarse porridge, he could not swallow it.

sentences.zh: 玄子昇五六歲，抱玄胸而撫之，玄悲不自勝。

translations.literal: Xuan's son Sheng, five or six years old, embraced Xuan's chest and stroked him; Xuan grieved beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's son Sheng, five or six years old, clutched his father's chest and patted him; Xuan was overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 玄挾德宗發尋陽，至江陵，西中郎將桓石康納之。

translations.literal: Xuan took Dezong along and set out from Xunyang, reaching Jiangling, where the General of the West, Huan Shikang, received him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan took Dezong with him from Xunyang to Jiangling, where Huan Shikang, General of the West, received them.

sentences.zh: 張幔屋，止城南，署置百官，以卞範之為尚書僕射，殷仲文為徐州，其餘各顯用。

translations.literal: He spread canopy tents and halted south of the city, appointed all officials, made Bian Fanzhi Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Yin Zhongwen Inspector of Xu, and displayed the rest in office according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He pitched canopy tents south of the city, installed a full bureaucracy, appointed Bian Fanzhi Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Yin Zhongwen Inspector of Xu, and assigned the rest to prominent posts.

sentences.zh: 玄謂諸侍臣曰：「卿等並升清塗，翼從朕躬，都下竊位者方應謝罪軍門，其見卿等入石頭，無異雲霄中人也。」

translations.literal: Xuan said to all attendant ministers: "You all have been promoted to noble stations and attend my person. Those who usurped their posts in the capital should soon be begging forgiveness at the army gates. When they see you enter Stone City, it will be no different from seeing people in the clouds."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan told his attendant ministers: "You have all risen to high office and attend my person. The usurpers in the capital will soon be begging forgiveness at the army gates. When they see you enter Stone City again, it will be like meeting people descended from the clouds."

sentences.zh: 玄以奔敗之後，懼法令不肅，遂輕怒妄殺，逾甚暴虐。

translations.literal: After his flight and defeat, fearing lax enforcement of law, Xuan then killed in petty anger and without cause, exceeding even his former brutality.
translations.idiomatic: After his flight and defeat, fearing lax discipline, Xuan killed on whim and without cause, growing even more brutal than before.

sentences.zh: 殷仲文諫之，玄大怒曰：「漢高、魏武幾遇敗，但諸將失利耳。

translations.literal: Yin Zhongwen remonstrated; Xuan flew into a rage and said: "Emperor Gao of Han and Emperor Wu of Wei nearly met defeat—it was only that their generals lost the day.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Zhongwen remonstrated, Xuan flew into a rage: "Emperor Gao of Han and Emperor Wu of Wei nearly met defeat—it was only their generals who lost.

sentences.zh: 以天文惡，故還都舊楚，而羣小愚惑，妄生是非，方當糾之以猛，未宜施之以恩也。」

translations.literal: Because the celestial signs were ill-omened, I returned the capital to old Chu; yet petty men in their folly stir up troubles without cause. I should now correct them with severity—it is not yet time to treat them with kindness."
translations.idiomatic: The heavens were ill-omened, so I moved the capital back to old Chu—yet petty men in their folly stir up troubles without cause. I must now correct them with severity; it is not yet time for leniency."

sentences.zh: 荊、江郡守，以玄播越，咸遣使通表，有匪寧之辭，玄悉不受，乃更令所在表賀遷都。

translations.literal: The Administrators of Jing and Jiang, because Xuan was cast adrift, all sent envoys with memorials expressing unrest; Xuan accepted none of them, and instead ordered each place to submit memorials congratulating the transfer of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The prefects of Jing and Jiang provinces, seeing Xuan adrift in defeat, all sent memorials expressing unrest. Xuan rejected them all and instead ordered each locality to submit congratulations on the move of the capital.

sentences.zh: 玄在道自作起居注，敍其拒劉裕事，自謂算略無失，諸將違節度，以至於敗。

translations.literal: On the road Xuan himself composed an imperial diary, narrating his resistance to Liu Yu, declaring his stratagems without error and that it was the generals who violated regulations that led to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: On the road Xuan composed his own imperial diary of his resistance to Liu Yu, claiming his strategy had been flawless and blaming his generals' disobedience for the defeat.

sentences.zh: 不暇謀議軍事，惟誦述寫傳之。

translations.literal: He had no leisure to deliberate on military affairs, devoting himself only to reciting and copying the text for transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He had no time to discuss military affairs, devoting himself only to reciting and copying the text for posterity.

sentences.zh: 劉裕遣其冠軍將軍劉毅發建鄴，追之。

translations.literal: Liu Yu sent his General Who Conquers Champions, Liu Yi, out from Jiankang in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu dispatched Liu Yi, General Who Conquers Champions, from Jiankang in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 玄軍屢敗。

translations.literal: Xuan's army was repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's army suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 玄常裝輕舸於舫側，故其兵人莫有鬬志。

translations.literal: Xuan often had light boats fitted along the side of his vessel, so his soldiers had no fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan kept light boats rigged along the side of his flagship, so his troops had no will to fight.

sentences.zh: 玄乃棄眾而走，餘軍以次崩散，遂與德宗還江陵。

translations.literal: Xuan then abandoned the masses and fled; the remaining army collapsed in succession, and he returned to Jiangling with Dezong.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan abandoned his army and fled; the rest broke and scattered in turn, and he returned to Jiangling with Dezong.

sentences.zh: 初，玄留德宗妻子巴陵，殷仲文與玄同舟，乃說玄求別舫收集散軍，遂以德宗妻歸于建鄴。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xuan had left Dezong's wife and children at Baling. Yin Zhongwen was on the same boat as Xuan and persuaded him to take a separate vessel to gather the scattered troops, then brought Dezong's wife back to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xuan had left Dezong's wife and children at Baling. Yin Zhongwen, aboard the same vessel, urged Xuan to take another ship to rally the scattered forces, then escorted Dezong's wife back to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 玄入江陵城，南平太守馮該勸玄更戰。

translations.literal: Xuan entered Jiangling city; the Administrator of Nanping, Feng Gai, urged Xuan to fight again.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan entered Jiangling, Feng Gai, Administrator of Nanping, urged him to renew the fight.

sentences.zh: 玄欲出漢中，投梁州刺史桓希，夜中處分將發，城內已亂，禁令不行，將親近腹心百許人出城北。

translations.literal: Xuan wished to go out to Hanzhong and throw himself on Huan Xi, Inspector of Liang; at night he made dispositions to depart, but the city was already in turmoil, orders could not be enforced, and he led some hundred close confidants out the north gate.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan planned to flee to Hanzhong and seek refuge with Huan Xi, Inspector of Liang. He made ready to depart at night, but the city was already in chaos and his orders went unheeded; he took some hundred trusted followers out the north gate.

sentences.zh: 至城門，左右即於闇中斫玄面，前後相殺，交橫盈路。

translations.literal: At the city gate his attendants immediately hacked at Xuan's face in the dark; they killed one another before and behind, corpses filling the road.
translations.idiomatic: At the gate his own men hacked at his face in the dark; they turned on one another, and the dead filled the road.

sentences.zh: 玄僅得至船。

translations.literal: Xuan barely reached the boat.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan barely made it to his ship.

sentences.zh: 德宗入南郡府。

translations.literal: Dezong entered the headquarters of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong entered the seat of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 玄既下船，猶欲走漢中。

translations.literal: Once Xuan had gone aboard, he still wished to flee to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Even after boarding, Xuan still meant to flee to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 玄屯騎校尉毛脩之誘以入蜀，遂與石康等泝江而上。

translations.literal: Mao Xiuzhi, Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry, enticed him to enter Shu, and he then went upriver with Shi Kang and others.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xiuzhi, Colonel of the Garrison Cavalry, persuaded him to flee into Shu, and he sailed upriver with Shi Kang and others.

sentences.zh: 達枚回洲，為益州參軍費恬等迎射之，箭如雨下。

translations.literal: Reaching Meihui Isle, he was met with a volley by Fei Tian, staff officer of Yizhou, and others; arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: At Meihui Isle, Fei Tian and other officers of Yizhou ambushed him with a hail of arrows.

sentences.zh: 玄中流矢，子昇輒拔之。

translations.literal: Xuan was struck by arrows; his son Sheng pulled them out as they came.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was hit by arrows; his son Sheng pulled each one out as it struck.

sentences.zh: 益州督護馮遷抽刃而登玄艦，玄曰：「是何人也，敢殺天子！」

translations.literal: Feng Qian, Protector of Yizhou, drew his blade and boarded Xuan's ship. Xuan said: "What sort of man are you, who dares kill the Son of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qian, Protector of Yizhou, drew his sword and boarded Xuan's vessel. Xuan cried: "Who are you to dare kill the Son of Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 遷曰：「我自欲殺天子之賊耳。」

translations.literal: Qian said: "I merely wish to kill the usurper of the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Qian replied: "I mean only to kill the usurper who stole the throne."

sentences.zh: 遂斬玄首并石康等，斬昇于江陵市，傳送玄首，梟于朱雀門。

translations.literal: He then beheaded Xuan along with Shi Kang and others, executed Sheng in the market of Jiangling, sent Xuan's head onward, and had it displayed at the Vermilion Bird Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded Xuan and Shi Kang and the rest, executed Sheng in the Jiangling market, sent Xuan's head to the capital, and had it displayed at the Vermilion Bird Gate.

sentences.zh: 玄既敗，桓謙匿於沮中。

translations.literal: After Xuan's defeat, Huan Qian hid in Ju.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuan's defeat, Huan Qian went into hiding in Ju.

sentences.zh: 桓振逃于華容之浦，陰聚黨數千人，晨襲江陵，克之。

translations.literal: Huan Zhen fled to the shore at Huarong, secretly gathered several thousand partisans, and at dawn raided Jiangling and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Zhen fled to the Huarong shore, secretly rallied several thousand followers, and at dawn stormed and seized Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 桓謙亦聚眾而出。

translations.literal: Huan Qian also gathered a host and came forth.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Qian likewise rallied his forces and marched out.

sentences.zh: 振既至，問玄子昇所在，知昇已死，欲殺德宗，謙苦禁之。

translations.literal: When Zhen arrived he asked where Xuan's son Sheng was; learning Sheng was already dead, he wished to kill Dezong, but Qian strenuously forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen arrived he asked after Xuan's son Sheng; told that Sheng was dead, he wanted to kill Dezong, but Qian held him back with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 於是為玄舉哀，諡為武悼皇帝。

translations.literal: Thereupon they mourned Xuan and gave him the posthumous title Martial Lament Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They then held mourning for Xuan and gave him the posthumous title Martial Lament Emperor.

sentences.zh: 謙率羣官復立德宗，振自為都督八州、鎮軍將軍、荊州刺史，[5]謙復本職，又加江豫二州刺史。

translations.literal: Qian led the officials to restore Dezong; Zhen made himself Commander-in-Chief of Eight Provinces, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Inspector of Jing;[5] Qian resumed his former post and was additionally made Inspector of Jiang and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Qian led the officials in restoring Dezong. Zhen appointed himself Commander-in-Chief of Eight Provinces, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Inspector of Jing;[5] Qian resumed his former office and was also made Inspector of Jiang and Yu.

sentences.zh: 後德宗益州刺史毛璩殺桓希漢中。

translations.literal: Later Dezong's Inspector of Yizhou, Mao Qi, killed Huan Xi in Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Later Mao Qi, Inspector of Yizhou under Dezong, killed Huan Xi in Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 桓振寇江陵，為唐興所斬。

translations.literal: Huan Zhen raided Jiangling and was beheaded by Tang Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Zhen attacked Jiangling and was slain by Tang Xing.

sentences.zh: 其餘親從，或當時擒獲，或奔散外境，數年之間，並敗滅之。

translations.literal: The rest of his kin and followers were either captured at the time or fled and scattered beyond the borders; within a few years they were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of his kin and followers were either captured on the spot or fled beyond the borders; within a few years they were all wiped out.

sentences.zh: 海夷馮跋，字文起，小名乞直伐，本出長樂信都。

translations.literal: Feng Ba of the Haiyi, style name Wenqi, childhood name Qizhifa, was originally from Xindu in Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba of the Haiyi, courtesy name Wenqi, childhood name Qizhifa, was originally from Xindu in Changle.

sentences.zh: 慕容永僭號長子，以跋父安為將。

translations.literal: Murong Yong declared himself at Changzi and made Ba's father An a general.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong declared himself at Changzi and appointed Ba's father An as a general.

sentences.zh: 永為垂所滅，安東徙昌黎，家于長谷。

translations.literal: Yong was destroyed by Chui; An moved east to Changli and made his home at Changgu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong was destroyed by Murong Chui, An moved east to Changli and settled at Changgu.

sentences.zh: 跋飲酒至一石不亂。

translations.literal: Ba could drink up to one dan of wine without becoming disorderly.
translations.idiomatic: Ba could drink a full dan of wine without losing his composure.

sentences.zh: 母弟素弗，次丕，次洪，皆任俠放逸，不修行業，跋恭慎勤稼穡。

translations.literal: His younger brothers by the same mother were Sufu, next Pi, next Hong—all chivalrous and unrestrained, caring nothing for proper conduct; Ba was respectful, cautious, and diligent in farming.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Sufu, Pi, and Hong were all swaggering ruffians who cared nothing for propriety; Ba alone was respectful, cautious, and diligent in the fields.

sentences.zh: 既家昌黎，遂同夷俗。

translations.literal: Once settled in Changli, they adopted the customs of the barbarians.
