translations.idiomatic: Once they had settled in Changli, they adopted the local barbarian ways.

sentences.zh: 後慕容熙僭號，以跋為殿中左監，稍遷衞中郎將。

translations.literal: Later Murong Xi usurped the title, appointed Ba Left Supervisor in the Palace, and gradually promoted him to General of the Guards Gentlemen of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: Later Murong Xi usurped the title, appointed Ba Left Supervisor in the Palace, and gradually promoted him to General of the Guards Gentlemen of the Household.

sentences.zh: 後坐事逃亡。

translations.literal: Later he was implicated in an affair and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was implicated in an affair and fled.

sentences.zh: 既而熙政殘虐，民不堪命，跋乃與從兄萬泥等二十三人結謀，跋與二弟乘車，使婦人御，潛入龍城，匿於孫護之室以誅熙。

translations.literal: Before long, Xi's government was cruel and oppressive, and the people could not bear his commands. Ba then plotted with his elder cousin Wanni and twenty-three others; Ba and his two younger brothers rode in a carriage, had a woman drive it, secretly entered Longcheng, and hid in Sun Hu's room in order to kill Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Xi's rule became cruel and the people could not endure it. Ba plotted with his elder cousin Wanni and twenty-three others; he and his two younger brothers rode in a carriage driven by a woman, slipped into Longcheng, and hid in Sun Hu's room to kill Xi.

sentences.zh: 乃立夕陽公高雲為主，以跋為侍中、征北大將軍、開府儀同三司，封武邑公，事皆決跋兄弟。

translations.literal: They then established Gao Yun, Duke of Xiyang, as ruler, made Ba Palace Attendant, General-in-Chief Who Campaigns North, and Opening Office with the Same Ceremonies as the Three Excellencies, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Wuyi; all affairs were decided by Ba and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: They then set up Gao Yun, Duke of Xiyang, as ruler. Ba became Palace Attendant, General-in-Chief Who Campaigns North, Opening Office with the Same Ceremonies as the Three Excellencies, and Duke of Wuyi; all affairs were decided by Ba and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，雲為左右所殺，跋乃自立為燕王，置百官，號年太平，于時永興元年也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taizong's reign, Yun was killed by those at his side, and Ba then established himself as Prince of Yan, set up the hundred offices, and named the era Taiping; at the time it was the first year of Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taizong's reign, Yun was killed by his attendants. Ba then set himself up as Prince of Yan, established the offices, and named his era Taiping; this was Yongxing 1.

sentences.zh: 跋撫納契丹等諸落，頗來附之。

translations.literal: Ba soothed and received the Khitan and other tribes, and quite a few came to attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ba conciliated and accepted the Khitan and other tribes, and many came over to him.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣謁者于什門喻之，為跋所留，語在什門傳。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong sent the Attendant-on-Affairs Yu Shimmen to instruct him; Shimmen was detained by Ba—the account is in Shimmen's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong sent the envoy Yu Shimmen to address him; Ba detained him—the full account appears in Shimmen's biography.

sentences.zh: 泰常三年，和龍城有赤氣蔽日，自寅至申，跋太史令張穆以為兵氣，言於跋曰：「大魏威制六合而聘使隔絕，自古鄰國未有不通之理，違義致忿，取敗之道，恐大軍卒至，必致吞滅，宜還魏使，奉修職貢。」

translations.literal: In the third year of Taichang, a red vapor at Helong city blotted out the sun from yin to shen. Ba's Grand Astrologer Zhang Mu took it for a martial omen and said to Ba: "Great Wei holds sway over the six directions yet our envoys are cut off. Never in antiquity have neighboring states failed to maintain contact. To violate righteousness and invite wrath is the path to defeat. I fear a great army will soon arrive and bring utter destruction. You should return the Wei envoy and resume tribute duties."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taichang, a red mist at Helong blotted out the sun from dawn to mid-afternoon. Ba's Grand Astrologer Zhang Mu read it as a martial omen and warned Ba: "Great Wei rules all under heaven, yet our envoys are cut off. Neighboring states have always kept channels open. To defy righteousness and invite wrath is the road to ruin. A great army may come at any moment and swallow us whole. Return the Wei envoy and resume tribute."

sentences.zh: 跋不從。

translations.literal: Ba did not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Ba refused.

sentences.zh: 太宗詔征東大將軍長孫道生率眾二萬討之，跋嬰城固守，不克而還。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong ordered the General Who Conquers the East, Zhangsun Daosheng, to lead twenty thousand men against him. Ba shut himself in the city and held fast; they could not take it and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong ordered Zhangsun Daosheng, General Who Conquers the East, to march against him with twenty thousand men. Ba barred the gates and held out; the Wei army failed to take the city and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 神䴥二年，跋有疾。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenjue, Ba fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shenjue, Ba fell ill.

sentences.zh: 其長子永先死，立次子翼為世子，攝國事，勒兵以備非常。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yong had died earlier; he installed the second son Yi as heir apparent, put him in charge of state affairs, and marshaled troops against emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yong had already died; he named his second son Yi heir apparent, gave him charge of state affairs, and mobilized troops against any emergency.

sentences.zh: 跋妾宋氏規立其子受居，深忌翼，謂之曰：「主上疾將瘳，奈何代父臨國乎？」

translations.literal: Ba's concubine Lady Song plotted to install her son Shouju and deeply resented Yi. She said to him: "Our lord's illness is about to mend—why should you rule in your father's stead?"
translations.idiomatic: Ba's concubine Lady Song plotted to put her son Shouju on the throne and deeply resented Yi. She told him: "The lord's illness is nearly cured—why are you ruling in his place?"

sentences.zh: 翼遂還。

translations.literal: Yi thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yi withdrew.

sentences.zh: 宋氏矯絕內外，遣閹人傳問，翼及跋諸子、大臣並不得省疾，惟中給事胡福獨得出入，專掌禁衞。

translations.literal: Lady Song cut off access inside and out, sending eunuchs to relay messages. Yi, all of Ba's sons, and the great ministers could not visit the sick; only the Palace Attendant Hu Fu alone could enter and exit, holding sole charge of the guard.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Song sealed off the palace, using eunuchs to relay messages. Yi, Ba's other sons, and the ministers were barred from the sickroom; only the Palace Attendant Hu Fu could come and go, commanding the guards alone.

sentences.zh: 跋疾甚，福慮宋氏將成其計，乃言於跋弟文通，勒兵而入。

translations.literal: When Ba's illness grew grave, Fu feared Lady Song would carry out her plot and spoke to Ba's younger brother Wentong, who led troops inside.
translations.idiomatic: As Ba's illness worsened, Fu feared Lady Song would succeed in her plot and appealed to Ba's younger brother Wentong, who marched his troops into the palace.

sentences.zh: 跋驚怖而死，文通襲位。

translations.literal: Ba died of shock and terror; Wentong seized the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Ba died of fright; Wentong seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 翼勒兵出戰，不利，遂死。

translations.literal: Yi led troops out to fight, met with ill fortune, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yi led his forces into battle, was defeated, and died.

sentences.zh: 跋有男百餘人，悉為文通所殺。

translations.literal: Ba had more than a hundred sons; all were killed by Wentong.
translations.idiomatic: Ba had more than a hundred sons; Wentong killed them all.

sentences.zh: 弟文通

translations.literal: Younger brother Wentong
translations.idiomatic: Younger Brother Wentong

sentences.zh: 文通，跋之少弟也，本名犯顯祖廟諱。

translations.literal: Wentong was Ba's youngest brother; his original name violated the taboo of Emperor Xianzu's temple.
translations.idiomatic: Wentong was Ba's youngest brother; his birth name violated the taboo of Emperor Xianzu's temple name.

sentences.zh: 高雲僭號，以為征東大將軍，領中領軍，封汲郡公。

translations.literal: When Gao Yun declared himself, he made him General Who Conquers the East, acting Central Army Commander, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yun declared himself, he appointed Wentong General Who Conquers the East and Central Army Commander, with the title Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 跋立，為尚書左僕射，改封中山，仍為領軍，內掌禁衞，外總朝政，歷位司徒。

translations.literal: When Ba took the throne, he became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Zhongshan, still served as army commander, controlled the inner guard within and the outer government without, and rose to Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Ba took the throne, Wentong became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Zhongshan, retained command of the guards, held sway over court and camp alike, and rose to Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 及自立，乃與劉義隆交通。

translations.literal: Once he had made himself ruler, he opened relations with Liu Yilong.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had seized power, he opened relations with Liu Yilong of Song.

sentences.zh: 延和元年，世祖親討之，文通嬰城固守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanhe, Emperor Shizu personally attacked him; Wentong shut the city and held fast.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanhe, Emperor Shizu marched against him in person; Wentong barred the gates and held out.

sentences.zh: 文通營丘、遼東、成周、樂浪、帶方、玄菟六郡皆降，世祖徙其三萬餘戶于幽州。

translations.literal: The six commanderies of Yingqiu, Liaodong, Chengzhou, Lelang, Daifang, and Xuantu all submitted to Wentong; Emperor Shizu moved more than thirty thousand households to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The six commanderies of Yingqiu, Liaodong, Chengzhou, Lelang, Daifang, and Xuantu all surrendered; Emperor Shizu relocated more than thirty thousand households to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 文通尚書郭淵勸其歸誠進女，乞為附庸，保守宗廟。

translations.literal: Wentong's Master of Writing Guo Yuan urged him to submit in good faith, send a daughter, beg to become a vassal, and preserve the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuan, Master of Writing under Wentong, urged him to submit, send a daughter as tribute, accept vassal status, and preserve the ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 文通曰：「負釁在前，忿形已露，降附取死，不如守志，更圖所適也。」

translations.literal: Wentong said: "Guilt lies upon me already, and their wrath is plain. To submit is to court death; better to hold to our purpose and seek another refuge."
translations.idiomatic: Wentong replied: "I am already guilty in their eyes, and their anger is plain. Submission means death. Better to hold our ground and seek another way out."

sentences.zh: 先是，文通廢其元妻王氏，黜世子崇，令鎮肥如，以後妻慕容氏子王仁為世子。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wentong had deposed his first wife Lady Wang, removed the heir Chong and sent him to garrison Feiru, and made Wang Ren, son of his later wife of the Murong clan, heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wentong had deposed his first wife Lady Wang, removed the heir Chong to garrison Feiru, and named Wang Ren, son of his later Murong wife, as heir.

sentences.zh: 崇母弟廣平公朗、樂陵公邈相謂曰：「大運有在，家國已亡，又慕容之譖，禍將至矣。」

translations.literal: Chong's younger brothers by the same mother, the Duke of Guangping Lang and the Duke of Leling Miao, said to each other: "The Mandate has its holder; our house and state are already lost, and now with Murong slander, disaster is at hand."
translations.idiomatic: Chong's younger brothers Lang, Duke of Guangping, and Miao, Duke of Leling, said to each other: "The Mandate belongs elsewhere; our house is ruined, and Murong intrigue will bring disaster upon us."

sentences.zh: 於是遂出奔遼西，勸崇來降，崇納之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they fled to Liaoxi and urged Chong to submit; Chong accepted.
translations.idiomatic: They fled to Liaoxi and urged Chong to surrender; Chong agreed.

sentences.zh: 會世祖使給事中王德陳示成敗，崇遣邈入朝。

translations.literal: Just then Emperor Shizu sent the Palace Attendant Wang De to set forth success and failure; Chong sent Miao to court.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Shizu sent the Palace Attendant Wang De to explain the stakes; Chong sent Miao to court.

sentences.zh: 世祖遣兼鴻臚李繼持節拜崇假節、侍中、都督幽平二州東夷諸軍事、車騎大將軍、領護東夷校尉、幽平二州牧，封遼西王，錄其國尚書事，食遼西十郡；

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu sent the Acting Grand Herald Li Ji bearing credentials to appoint Chong Acting Credential Holder, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of the Eastern Yi Armies of You and Ping, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Chief Protector of the Eastern Yi, Governor of You and Ping, enfeoffed him as King of Liaoxi, gave him charge of his state's Masters of Writing, and granted him the revenues of ten commanderies of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu sent Acting Grand Herald Li Ji with credentials to appoint Chong Acting Credential Holder, Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of Eastern Yi forces in You and Ping, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Chief Protector of the Eastern Yi, and Governor of You and Ping, enfeoffing him as King of Liaoxi with charge of his state's Masters of Writing and the revenues of ten Liaoxi commanderies.

sentences.zh: 承制，假授文官尚書、刺史，武官征虜已下。

translations.literal: By imperial commission he was empowered to provisionally appoint civil officials as Masters of Writing and inspectors, and military officials down to General Who Conquers the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial commission he could provisionally appoint civil officials as Masters of Writing and inspectors, and military officers down to General Who Conquers the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 文通遣其將封羽率眾圍崇，世祖詔永昌王健督諸軍救之。

translations.literal: Wentong sent his general Feng Yu with a host to besiege Chong; Emperor Shizu ordered Jian, Prince of Yongchang, to supervise all armies in relief.
translations.idiomatic: Wentong sent his general Feng Yu to besiege Chong; Emperor Shizu ordered Prince Jian of Yongchang to lead the relief forces.

sentences.zh: 封羽又以凡城降，徙其三千餘家而還。

translations.literal: Feng Yu also surrendered Fancheng; more than three thousand households were moved, and the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yu also surrendered Fancheng; more than three thousand households were relocated, and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 文通遣其尚書高顒請罪，乞以季女充掖庭。

translations.literal: Wentong sent his Master of Writing Gao Yang to beg forgiveness and offer his youngest daughter for the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Wentong sent his Master of Writing Gao Yang to beg pardon and offer his youngest daughter for the imperial harem.

sentences.zh: 世祖許之，徵其子王仁入朝，文通不遣。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu consented and summoned his son Wang Ren to court, but Wentong did not send him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu agreed and summoned his son Wang Ren to court, but Wentong refused to send him.

sentences.zh: 其散騎常侍劉訓言於文通曰：「雖結婚和通，而未遣侍子，魏若大舉，將有危亡之慮。

translations.literal: His Regular Palace Attendant Liu Xun said to Wentong: "Though we have sealed marriage and made peace, we have not sent a hostage prince. If Wei launches a major campaign, we face the fear of ruin.
translations.idiomatic: His Regular Palace Attendant Liu Xun warned Wentong: "We have sealed a marriage alliance, yet sent no hostage prince. If Wei mounts a full campaign, we face destruction.

sentences.zh: 夫以重山之隘，劉禪銜璧；

translations.literal: With the barrier of towering mountains, Liu Shan still offered his jade seal;
translations.idiomatic: Behind the barrier of towering mountains, Liu Shan still surrendered with jade seal in hand;

sentences.zh: 長江之難，孫皓歸命。

translations.literal: with the difficulty of the Long River, Sun Hao still submitted his fate.
translations.idiomatic: across the barrier of the Yangzi, Sun Hao still bowed to fate.

sentences.zh: 況魏強於晉氏，燕弱于吳蜀，願時遣世子，以恭大國之命。

translations.literal: How much more when Wei is stronger than the Jin house and Yan is weaker than Wu and Shu—I beg you to send the heir apparent in good time to honor the great state's command.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when Wei is stronger than Jin ever was and Yan weaker than Wu or Shu—send the heir now to honor the great power's command.

sentences.zh: 然後收離集散，厚布恩澤，分賑倉廩以濟民乏，勸督農桑以邀秋稔，庶大業危而更安，社稷可以永保。」

translations.literal: Then gather the scattered and disperse the dispersed, lavish grace broadly, distribute grain from the granaries to relieve the people's want, urge and oversee farming and sericulture to secure the autumn harvest—then perhaps the great enterprise, though endangered, may be made secure and the altars of soil and grain long preserved."
translations.idiomatic: Then rally the scattered, show generous mercy, open the granaries to feed the hungry, and urge farming to secure the autumn harvest—so the realm, though imperiled, may yet be saved and the dynasty preserved."

sentences.zh: 文通大怒，殺之。

translations.literal: Wentong flew into a rage and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wentong flew into a rage and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 世祖又詔樂平王丕等討之，日就蹙削，上下危懼。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu again ordered the Prince of Leping Pi and others to attack; day by day their position narrowed, and high and low were filled with dread.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu again ordered Prince Pi of Leping and others to attack; their position shrank daily, and court and camp alike were gripped by fear.

sentences.zh: 文通太常陽㟭復勸文通請罪乞降，速令王仁入侍。

translations.literal: Wentong's Minister of Ceremonies Yang Yan again urged Wentong to beg forgiveness and submit, and quickly send Wang Ren to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Wentong's Minister of Ceremonies Yang Yan again urged him to beg pardon and submit, and send Wang Ren to court at once.

sentences.zh: 文通曰：「吾未忍為此，若事不幸，且欲東次高麗，以圖後舉。」

translations.literal: Wentong said: "I cannot yet bring myself to this. If matters go ill, I mean first to move east to Goguryeo and plan a later effort."
translations.idiomatic: Wentong said: "I cannot bring myself to that. If all fails, I will move east to Goguryeo and plan our next move."

sentences.zh: 㟭曰：「魏以天下之眾擊一隅之地，以臣愚見，勢必土崩。

translations.literal: Yan said: "Wei strikes a single corner of the realm with the hosts of all under heaven—in this humble servant's view, we are bound to collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied: "Wei brings the hosts of all under heaven against this one corner—in my view, we are bound to collapse.

sentences.zh: 且高麗夷狄，難以信期，始雖相親，終恐為變。

translations.literal: Moreover Goguryeo are barbarians, hard to trust for long; though friendly at first, in the end I fear they will turn treacherous.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Goguryeo are barbarians whose word cannot be trusted; they may seem friendly at first, but in the end they will betray us.

sentences.zh: 若不早裁，悔無及也。」

translations.literal: If you do not decide early, regret will come too late."
translations.idiomatic: If you do not act now, it will be too late for regret."

sentences.zh: 文通不聽，乃密求迎於高麗。

translations.literal: Wentong would not listen and secretly sought welcome from Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Wentong would not listen and secretly asked Goguryeo to receive him.

sentences.zh: 太延二年，高麗遣將葛盧等率眾迎之，入和龍城，脫其弊褐，取文通精仗以賦其眾。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiyan, Goguryeo sent the generals Gelu and others with a host to welcome him. Entering Helong city, they stripped off their ragged clothes and took Wentong's fine arms to equip their troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiyan, Goguryeo sent Generals Gelu and others to escort him. Entering Helong, they stripped off their rags and seized Wentong's fine arms to equip their men.

sentences.zh: 文通乃擁其城內士女入于高麗。

translations.literal: Wentong then led the men and women within the city into Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Wentong then took the city's men and women with him into Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 先是，其國有狼夜繞城羣嘷，如是終歲；

translations.literal: Earlier, in his state wolves at night circled the city howling in packs, and so it continued for a full year.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier wolves had circled the city howling by night for a full year;

sentences.zh: 又有鼠集於城西，闐滿數里，西行至水，則在前者銜馬矢，迭相齧尾而渡；

translations.literal: rats also gathered west of the city, filling several li; marching west to the water, those in front carried horse dung in their mouths, each biting the tail of the one before to cross.
translations.idiomatic: rats had massed west of the city for miles; marching to the water, those in front carried horse dung in their mouths, each biting the tail ahead to cross;

sentences.zh: 宿軍地燃，一旬而滅，觸地生蛆，月餘乃止；

translations.literal: the army's encampment ground burned for ten days and then went out; wherever one touched the earth maggots were born, continuing for more than a month before ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: the army camp burned for ten days; wherever one touched the ground maggots swarmed for more than a month;

sentences.zh: 和龍城生白毛，長一尺二寸。

translations.literal: at Helong city white hair grew, a foot and two inches long.
translations.idiomatic: and at Helong white hair sprouted a foot and two inches long.

sentences.zh: 文通至遼東，高麗遣使勞之曰：「龍城王馮君爰適野次，士馬勞乎？」

translations.literal: When Wentong reached Liaodong, Goguryeo sent an envoy to console him, saying: "Lord Feng of Longcheng, having come to this wild lodging—are your men and horses weary?"
translations.idiomatic: When Wentong reached Liaodong, Goguryeo sent an envoy to greet him: "Lord Feng of Longcheng, come to this wilderness—are your men and horses weary?"

sentences.zh: 文通慚怒，稱制答讓之，高麗乃處之於平郭，尋徙北豐。

translations.literal: Wentong, shamed and angry, assumed imperial style in reply and rebuked them; Goguryeo then settled him at Pingguo, soon moving him to Beifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wentong, shamed and furious, answered as a sovereign and rebuked them; Goguryeo lodged him at Pingguo, then moved him to Beifeng.

sentences.zh: 文通素侮高麗，政刑賞罰，猶如其國。

translations.literal: Wentong had always looked down on Goguryeo; in government, punishments, rewards, and penalties he still acted as in his own state.
translations.idiomatic: Wentong had always despised Goguryeo; he still governed, punished, and rewarded as if in his own realm.

sentences.zh: 高麗乃奪其侍人，質任王仁。

translations.literal: Goguryeo then seized his attendants and took Wang Ren as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo seized his attendants and held Wang Ren hostage.

sentences.zh: 文通忿怨之，謀將南奔。

translations.literal: Wentong nursed resentment and plotted to flee south.
translations.idiomatic: Wentong brooded on his grievance and plotted to flee south.

sentences.zh: 世祖又徵文通於高麗，高麗乃殺之於北豐，子孫同時死者十餘人。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu again summoned Wentong from Goguryeo; Goguryeo then killed him at Beifeng, and more than ten of his sons and grandsons died at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu again demanded Wentong from Goguryeo; Goguryeo killed him at Beifeng, and more than ten of his sons and grandsons died with him.

sentences.zh: 文通子朗、邈。

translations.literal: Wentong's sons Lang and Miao.
translations.idiomatic: Wentong's sons Lang and Miao.

sentences.zh: 朗子熙，在外戚傳。

translations.literal: Lang's son Xi is treated in the biography of consort kin.
translations.idiomatic: Lang's son Xi is treated in the biography of the empress's kin.

sentences.zh: 島夷劉裕，字德輿，晉陵丹徒人也。

translations.literal: Liu Yu of the Daoyi, style name Deyu, was a man of Dantu in Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu of the Daoyi, courtesy name Deyu, was from Dantu in Jinling.

sentences.zh: 其先不知所出，自云本彭城彭城人，或云本姓項，改為劉氏，然亦莫可尋也，故其與叢亭、安上諸劉了無宗次。

translations.literal: His ancestors are unknown in origin; he himself said he was originally a man of Pengcheng in Pengcheng, or some say his original surname was Xiang and was changed to Liu—but none of this can be traced, so he had no genealogical connection with the various Liu clans of Congting and Anshang.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestry is unknown; he claimed descent from Pengcheng, or else that his family name was originally Xiang and was changed to Liu—none of which can be verified, so he bore no genealogical tie to the Liu clans of Congting and Anshang.

sentences.zh: 裕家本寒微，住在京口，恒以賣履為業。

translations.literal: Yu's family was originally humble and poor; living at Jingkou, he constantly made his living selling sandals.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's family was poor; he lived at Jingkou and made his living selling straw sandals.

sentences.zh: 意氣楚剌，僅識文字，樗蒲傾產，為時賤薄。

translations.literal: His spirit was fierce and Chu-rough; he barely knew characters; at dice he lost his estate and was despised by his age.
translations.idiomatic: He was rough and fierce, barely literate, ruined himself at dice, and was held in contempt.

sentences.zh: 嘗負驃騎諮議刁逵社錢三萬，經時不還。

translations.literal: He once owed thirty thousand in community funds to Diao Kui, Consultant of the Rapid Cavalry, and for a long time did not repay.
translations.idiomatic: He once owed thirty thousand in community funds to Diao Kui, consultant to the Rapid Cavalry general, and for a long time failed to repay.

sentences.zh: 逵以其無行，錄而徵責，驃騎長史王謐以錢代還，事方得了。

translations.literal: Kui, because of his misconduct, recorded the debt and pressed for payment; the Rapid Cavalry Chief Clerk Wang Mi repaid the money on his behalf, and only then was the matter settled.
translations.idiomatic: Kui, disgusted by his conduct, recorded the debt and pressed for payment; Wang Mi, chief clerk to the Rapid Cavalry general, paid it for him, and only then was the matter closed.

sentences.zh: 落魄不修廉隅。

translations.literal: He was down-and-out and cared nothing for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He was a drifter without a shred of propriety.

sentences.zh: 天興二年，僭晉司馬德宗遣其輔國將軍劉牢之東討孫恩，裕應募，始為牢之參軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianxing, the usurping Jin ruler Sima Dezong sent his General Who Assists the State Liu Laozhi east to attack Sun En; Yu answered the call and first served as Laozhi's staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianxing, the Jin usurper Sima Dezong sent Liu Laozhi, General Who Assists the State, east against Sun En; Yu enlisted and became Laozhi's staff officer.

sentences.zh: 恩北寇海鹽，裕追勝之，以功稍遷建武將軍、下邳太守。

translations.literal: En raided north into Haiyan; Yu pursued and defeated him, and for merit was gradually promoted to General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: When En raided Haiyan in the north, Yu pursued and defeated him; for this he was promoted to General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 劉牢之討桓玄，裕參其軍事。

translations.literal: When Liu Laozhi campaigned against Huan Xuan, Yu served on his military staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Laozhi marched against Huan Xuan, Yu served on his staff.

sentences.zh: 牢之降，裕為玄從兄桓脩中兵參軍。

translations.literal: When Laozhi surrendered, Yu became Central Army Staff Officer under Xuan's cousin Huan Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: When Laozhi surrendered, Yu became staff officer under Huan Xiu, Xuan's cousin and Central Army commander.

sentences.zh: 孫恩死，餘眾推恩妹夫盧循為主，玄遣裕征之，裕破循于東陽、永嘉，循浮海奔逸。

translations.literal: When Sun En died, the remnant host made En's brother-in-law Lu Xun their leader. Xuan sent Yu against him; Yu defeated Xun at Dongyang and Yongjia, and Xun fled over the sea.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun En died, his followers made En's brother-in-law Lu Xun their leader. Xuan sent Yu against him; Yu defeated Xun at Dongyang and Yongjia, and Xun fled by sea.

sentences.zh: 加裕彭城內史。

translations.literal: Yu was additionally made Administrator of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was appointed Administrator of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 及桓玄廢德宗而自立，裕與弟道規、劉毅、何無忌潛謀舉兵。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan deposed Dezong and made himself ruler, Yu secretly plotted to raise troops with his brother Daogui, Liu Yi, and He Wuji.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan deposed Dezong and seized the throne, Yu secretly plotted rebellion with his brother Daogui, Liu Yi, and He Wuji.

sentences.zh: 桓脩弟思祖鎮廣陵，道規劉毅先為之佐。

translations.literal: Huan Xiu's younger brother Sinzu garrisoned Guangling; Daogui and Liu Yi had earlier served as his aides.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xiu's younger brother Sinzu held Guangling; Daogui and Liu Yi had already served on his staff.

sentences.zh: 天賜初，裕與何無忌等旦候城門開，率眾斬玄徐州刺史桓脩於京口，其日，劉毅、道規等亦斬思祖，因收眾濟江。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiansi, Yu and He Wuji and others waited at dawn for the city gates to open, led a host and beheaded Xuan's Inspector of Xu, Huan Xiu, at Jingkou; that same day Liu Yi, Daogui, and others also beheaded Sinzu, then gathered troops and crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tiansi, Yu and He Wuji waited at dawn for the gates to open, led their men, and killed Huan Xiu, Xuan's Inspector of Xu, at Jingkou. That same day Liu Yi and Daogui killed Sinzu, rallied their forces, and crossed the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 河內太守辛扈興、恒農太守王元德、振威將軍童厚之亦與裕剋是日取玄。

translations.literal: The Administrators of Henei, Xin Huxing, and of Hengnong, Wang Yuande, and the General Who Quells Might, Tong Houzhi, also joined Yu in taking Xuan on that day.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Huxing, Administrator of Henei, Wang Yuande, Administrator of Hengnong, and Tong Houzhi, General Who Quells Might, also rose against Xuan that same day.

sentences.zh: 毅兄邁時在建業，毅遣周安要之，邁懼而告玄，玄遣頓丘太守吳甫之、右衞將軍皇甫敷北拒。

translations.literal: Yi's elder brother Mai was then at Jianye; Yi sent Zhou An to summon him, but Mai in fear informed Xuan, and Xuan sent the Administrator of Dunqiu, Wu Fuzhi, and the General of the Right Guard, Huangfu Fu, north to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's elder brother Mai was in Jianye; Yi sent Zhou An to fetch him, but Mai, afraid, informed Xuan. Xuan sent Wu Fuzhi, Administrator of Dunqiu, and Huangfu Fu, General of the Right Guard, north to resist.

sentences.zh: 裕率眾宿于竹里，遇甫之於江乘，裕執長刀直入其陳，斬甫之，進至羅落橋，又斬敷首。

translations.literal: Yu led his host to camp at Zhuli, met Fuzhi at Jiangcheng, seized a long blade and charged straight into his formation, beheaded Fuzhi, advanced to Luoluo Bridge, and again took Fu's head.
translations.idiomatic: Yu camped at Zhuli and met Fuzhi at Jiangcheng. Grasping a long blade, he charged into the enemy line and killed Fuzhi, then advanced to Luoluo Bridge and killed Fu as well.

sentences.zh: 玄使桓謙屯東陵，卞範之屯覆舟山西，裕又破之。

translations.literal: Xuan had Huan Qian encamp at Dongling and Bian Fanzhi at the west of Fuzhou Mountain; Yu defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan posted Huan Qian at Dongling and Bian Fanzhi west of Fuzhou Mountain; Yu defeated them both.

sentences.zh: 玄大懼，乃攜子姪浮江南走。

translations.literal: Xuan was greatly afraid and took his sons and nephews south over the river by boat.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Xuan fled south across the Yangzi with his sons and nephews.

sentences.zh: 裕入鎮石頭，以德宗司徒王謐為錄尚書，領揚州刺史，立留臺，總百官，裕為使持節、都督揚徐兗豫青冀幽并八州、鎮軍將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Yu entered and garrisoned Stone City, made Dezong's Minister of Education Wang Mi Director of the Masters of Writing and concurrent Governor of Yang, established the rear capital, and oversaw all officials; Yu became Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of Yang, Xu, Yan, Yu, Qing, Ji, You, and Bing, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Inspector of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu seized Stone City, appointed Wang Mi Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Yang, set up a rear capital, and took control of the bureaucracy. Yu became Bearer of the Staff of Authority, commander of eight provinces, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Inspector of Xu.

sentences.zh: 令道規等率眾追玄。

translations.literal: He ordered Daogui and others to lead troops in pursuit of Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Daogui and others to pursue Xuan.

sentences.zh: 裕因是相署名位，遣尚書王嘏等迎德宗，燔桓溫神主于宣陽門外。

translations.literal: Yu thereupon had each man sign his rank, sent the Master of Writing Wang Gu and others to welcome Dezong, and burned Huan Wen's spirit tablet outside the Xuanyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had his allies sign a roster of ranks, sent Wang Gu and other Masters of Writing to welcome Dezong, and burned Huan Wen's spirit tablet outside the Xuanyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 尋殺尚書左僕射王愉及其子綏、納等。

translations.literal: Soon he killed the Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yu and his sons Sui, Na, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He soon executed Wang Yu, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, along with his sons Sui, Na, and others.

sentences.zh: 裕以司馬遵為大將軍，承制，入居東宮，公卿以下莫不畢拜。

translations.literal: Yu made Sima Zun Grand General, acting by imperial commission, to enter and dwell in the Eastern Palace; from the dukes and ministers downward none failed to bow fully.
translations.idiomatic: Yu installed Sima Zun as Grand General with imperial commission and lodged him in the Eastern Palace; every official from the highest rank down bowed before him.

sentences.zh: 乃大赦，惟玄等不在例。

translations.literal: He then proclaimed a great amnesty, excepting Xuan and others.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty, excluding Xuan and his followers.

sentences.zh: 是夜，司徒王謐逃走。

translations.literal: That night Minister of Education Wang Mi fled.
translations.idiomatic: That night Wang Mi fled.

sentences.zh: 劉毅以其手解德宗璽綬，宜誅之。

translations.literal: Liu Yi said that because he had personally removed Dezong's seal and cord, he should be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi argued that because Mi had personally removed Dezong's seal and cord, he deserved death.

sentences.zh: 裕以其償錢之惠，固請免之，乃遣丹楊尹孟昶迎焉。

translations.literal: Yu, because of the favor of repaying his debt, firmly begged to spare him and then sent the Governor of Danyang, Meng Chang, to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, remembering that Mi had once repaid his debt, pleaded for his life and sent Meng Chang, Governor of Danyang, to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 無忌、道規至于桑落洲，破桓玄。

translations.literal: Wuji and Daogui reached Sangluo Isle and defeated Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji and Daogui reached Sangluo Isle and defeated Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 諸將進據尋陽，加裕都督江州。

translations.literal: The generals advanced and seized Xunyang; Yu was additionally made Commander-in-Chief of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: The generals advanced and took Xunyang; Yu was made Commander-in-Chief of Jiang province.

sentences.zh: 劉毅復敗桓玄於崢嶸洲，玄乃棄眾單舸奔走，挾德宗奔于江陵。

translations.literal: Liu Yi again defeated Huan Xuan at Zhengrong Isle; Xuan then abandoned his host and fled alone in a single boat, taking Dezong with him to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi defeated Xuan again at Zhengrong Isle; Xuan abandoned his army and fled alone by boat, dragging Dezong with him to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 裕領青州刺史，甲仗百人入殿。

translations.literal: Yu took charge as Inspector of Qing, and a hundred armed men entered the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yu took office as Inspector of Qing and sent a hundred armed men into the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 毅等平巴陵，德宗復位於江陵，改年曰義熙。

translations.literal: Yi and others pacified Baling; Dezong was restored at Jiangling and the era name was changed to Yixi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and the others pacified Baling; Dezong was restored at Jiangling and the era name changed to Yixi.

sentences.zh: 及還建業，裕進侍中、車騎將軍、都督中外諸軍事，飾讓不受；

translations.literal: When he returned to Jianye, Yu was advanced to Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad, but he feigned refusal and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to Jianye, Yu was offered Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and command of all armies; he declined with feigned modesty.

sentences.zh: 加錄尚書事，又詐不受。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Director of the Masters of Writing, and again pretended not to accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was also offered the directorship of the Masters of Writing and again pretended to refuse.

sentences.zh: 乃出鎮丹徒，改授都督十六州，餘如故，又領兗州，乃解青州。

translations.literal: He then went out to garrison Dantu, was reassigned as Commander-in-Chief of sixteen provinces with the rest unchanged, also took charge of Yan, and relinquished Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew to garrison Dantu, was made commander of sixteen provinces, took charge of Yan as well, and gave up Qing.

sentences.zh: 盧循破廣州，裕仍以循為廣州刺史，其黨琅邪人徐道覆為始興相。

translations.literal: Lu Xun captured Guangzhou; Yu still appointed Xun Inspector of Guang, and his partisan Xu Daofu of Langya became Chancellor of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun seized Guangzhou; Yu nonetheless appointed him Inspector of Guang, with his lieutenant Xu Daofu of Langya as Chancellor of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 裕又都督交廣二州。

translations.literal: Yu was additionally made Commander-in-Chief of Jiao and Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was also made commander of Jiao and Guang provinces.

sentences.zh: 又封裕豫章郡公，邑萬戶，絹三萬匹。

translations.literal: He was further enfeoffed as Duke of Yuzhang with a fief of ten thousand households and thirty thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Yuzhang with ten thousand households and thirty thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 加侍中，進號驃騎將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: [7] He was additionally made Palace Attendant and advanced in title to Rapid Cavalry General [8] with the ceremonial privileges of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: [7] He was made Palace Attendant and promoted to Rapid Cavalry General [8] with the ceremonial rank of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 又進裕揚州刺史，錄尚書事，居於東府。

translations.literal: He further advanced Yu to Governor of Yang, Director of the Masters of Writing, dwelling in the Eastern Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was further promoted to Governor of Yang and Director of the Masters of Writing, with his seat in the Eastern Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 裕遣劉敬宣伐蜀，為譙道福所敗，乃免敬宣官，裕自降為中軍將軍，開府如故。

translations.literal: Yu sent Liu Jingxuan to campaign against Shu; he was defeated by Qiao Daofu, whereupon Jingxuan was dismissed from office and Yu himself demoted to Central Army General, his headquarters remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent Liu Jingxuan against Shu; defeated by Qiao Daofu, Jingxuan was dismissed and Yu demoted himself to Central Army General while keeping his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 永興初，慕容超大掠淮北，執德宗陽平太守劉千載、濟南太守趙元，驅掠千餘家而歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxing, Murong Chao raided heavily north of the Huai, seized Dezong's Administrators of Yangping, Liu Qianzai, and of Jinan, Zhao Yuan, and drove off more than a thousand households before returning.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongxing, Murong Chao raided north of the Huai, captured Liu Qianzai, Administrator of Yangping, and Zhao Yuan, Administrator of Jinan, and carried off more than a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 裕乃伐超，遂屠廣固，執超，斬其王公以下三千人，納口萬餘、馬二千匹，夷其城隍。

translations.literal: Yu then campaigned against Chao, slaughtered Guanggu, seized Chao, beheaded three thousand from princes and dukes downward, took more than ten thousand captives and two thousand horses, and leveled the walls and moat.
translations.idiomatic: Yu marched against Chao, sacked Guanggu, captured him, executed three thousand nobles and officials, took more than ten thousand captives and two thousand horses, and razed the walls.

sentences.zh: 送超于建業，斬之。

translations.literal: Chao was sent to Jianye and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Chao was sent to Jianye and executed.

sentences.zh: 裕是行也，徐道覆勸盧循令乘虛而出，循從之，於是南康、廬陵、豫章諸郡守皆奔走。

translations.literal: On this campaign of Yu's, Xu Daofu urged Lu Xun to strike while the opportunity was open; Xun agreed, and the Administrators of Nankang, Luling, Yuzhang, and other commanderies all fled.
translations.idiomatic: While Yu was on campaign, Xu Daofu urged Lu Xun to strike at the opening; Xun agreed, and the prefects of Nankang, Luling, Yuzhang, and other commanderies all fled.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史何無忌率軍至豫章，戰歿。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Jiang, He Wuji, led troops to Yuzhang and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji, Inspector of Jiang, marched to Yuzhang and was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 于時羣議欲令德宗北徙渡江。

translations.literal: At the time the assembly debated having Dezong move north and cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated moving Dezong north across the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 循遂寇湘中，破劉道規於長沙，敗劉毅於桑落洲，席卷而下。

translations.literal: Xun then raided central Xiang, defeated Liu Daogui at Changsha, defeated Liu Yi at Sangluo Isle, and swept downriver.
translations.idiomatic: Xun raided Hunan, defeated Liu Daogui at Changsha and Liu Yi at Sangluo Isle, and swept down the river.

sentences.zh: 裕將孟昶、諸葛長民勸裕擁德宗過江，裕不從。

translations.literal: Yu's generals Meng Chang and Zhuge Changmin urged Yu to take Dezong across the river; Yu would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang and Zhuge Changmin urged Yu to escort Dezong across the Yangzi; Yu refused.

sentences.zh: 昶謂事必不濟，乃自殺。

translations.literal: Chang said the affair was bound to fail and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, convinced all was lost, killed himself.

sentences.zh: 裕發居人治石頭城。

translations.literal: Yu mobilized the residents to repair Stone City.
translations.idiomatic: Yu mobilized the populace to fortify Stone City.

sentences.zh: 道覆等至，即欲於新亭白石渚焚舟而上。

translations.literal: When Daofu and others arrived, they wished at once to burn their boats at the White Stone Ford of Xinting and advance upstream.
translations.idiomatic: When Daofu arrived, he wanted to burn the boats at White Stone Ford near Xinting and press upstream at once.

sentences.zh: 盧循曰：「大軍未至，孟昶便逆自殺，以此而推，建業尋應有變，但按甲守之，不憂不濟也。」

translations.literal: Lu Xun said: "The great army has not yet arrived, yet Meng Chang has already killed himself in despair. From this one may infer that Jianye will soon see turmoil. We need only hold our arms and wait—there is no need to fear failure."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun said: "The main army has not yet arrived, yet Meng Chang has already killed himself in despair. Jianye must be near collapse. We need only hold our ground and wait—victory is assured."

sentences.zh: 乃屯軍於蔡洲。

translations.literal: He then encamped his army at Cai Isle.
translations.idiomatic: He encamped at Cai Isle.

sentences.zh: 循乃率眾數萬上南岸，至于丹陽郡，遂遣焚京口、金城、姑熟，寇掠塗中及江寧、蕪湖。

translations.literal: Xun then led several tens of thousands up the south bank to Danyang Commandery, then sent parties to burn Jingkou, Jincheng, and Guniu, and raided Tuzhong as well as Jiangning and Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Xun led tens of thousands up the south bank to Danyang, burned Jingkou, Jincheng, and Guniu, and raided Tuzhong, Jiangning, and Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 循以阮賜為豫州刺史，裕中軍參軍尚靖、宣城內史毛脩之破賜於姑熟，獲其輜重，賜乃退。

translations.literal: Xun made Ruan Ci Inspector of Yu; Yu's Central Army staff officer Shang Jing and the Administrator of Xuancheng, Mao Xiuzhi, defeated Ci at Guniu, seized his baggage train, and Ci withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xun appointed Ruan Ci Inspector of Yu; Shang Jing and Mao Xiuzhi, Administrator of Xuancheng, defeated him at Guniu, captured his baggage train, and Ci retreated.

sentences.zh: 又加裕太尉、中書監、黃鉞，裕受黃鉞。

translations.literal: Yu was further made Grand Marshal, Director of the Secretariat, and bearer of the yellow axe; Yu accepted the yellow axe.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was made Grand Marshal, Director of the Secretariat, and bearer of the imperial axe; he accepted the axe.

sentences.zh: 盧循既不戰，乃告道覆曰：「師老矣，可還據尋陽，并力取荊州，徐以三分有二之勢與下流爭衡，猶可以濟也。」

translations.literal: Since Lu Xun would not fight, he told Daofu: "The army is weary. We can return and hold Xunyang, combine forces to take Jing, and slowly with a two-thirds advantage contend with the lower reaches—we may yet succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun, refusing battle, told Daofu: "Our army is exhausted. Let us fall back on Xunyang, seize Jing together, and with two-thirds of the realm contest the lower Yangzi—we may yet prevail."

sentences.zh: 乃自蔡洲南退。

translations.literal: He then withdrew south from Cai Isle.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew south from Cai Isle.

sentences.zh: 裕遣輔國將軍王仲德等追之。

translations.literal: Yu sent the General Who Assists the State, Wang Zhongde, and others in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent Wang Zhongde, General Who Assists the State, and others in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 裕又遣建威將軍孫季高率眾自海道襲番禺。

translations.literal: Yu also sent the General Who Establishes Might, Sun Jigao, with a host by the sea route to strike Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu also sent Sun Jigao, General Who Establishes Might, by sea to strike Panyu.

sentences.zh: 裕自以舟師南伐。

translations.literal: Yu himself led the fleet south in campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Yu himself led the fleet south.

sentences.zh: 季高乘海兼行，奄至番禺。

translations.literal: Jigao traveled by sea day and night and suddenly arrived at Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: Jigao sailed day and night and suddenly appeared at Panyu.

sentences.zh: 循不以海道為防，既至而覺，眾乃大驚。

translations.literal: Xun had not guarded against the sea route; when they arrived and he realized it, his host was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had not guarded the sea route; when the fleet appeared, his men panicked.

sentences.zh: 季高悉力而上，四面攻之，仍屠其城。

translations.literal: Jigao pressed up with all his strength, attacked from four sides, and slaughtered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jigao attacked from all sides with full force and sacked the city.

sentences.zh: 盧循父嘏及長史孫建之並以輕舟奔始興。

translations.literal: Lu Xun's father Gu and Chief Clerk Sun Jianzhi both fled in light boats to Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun's father Gu and Chief Clerk Sun Jianzhi fled by light boat to Shixing.

sentences.zh: 循與道覆率眾而下，裕眾軍擊之，循等還尋陽。

translations.literal: Xun and Daofu led their host downriver; Yu's armies struck them, and Xun and the others returned to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xun and Daofu marched downriver; Yu's armies attacked and drove them back to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 循欲遁於豫章，乃悉力柵斷左里。

translations.literal: Xun wished to escape to Yuzhang and therefore used all his strength to barricade and block Zuoli.
translations.idiomatic: Xun meant to flee to Yuzhang and threw up barricades at Zuoli.

sentences.zh: 裕諸軍乘勝而擊之，循單舸徑還廣州，道覆還始興。

translations.literal: Yu's armies pressed the victory and attacked; Xun alone in a single boat went straight back to Guangzhou, and Daofu returned to Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's armies pressed the attack; Xun fled alone by boat to Guangzhou, and Daofu retreated to Shixing.

sentences.zh: 裕還，為大將軍、揚州牧、班劍二十人，本官如故。

translations.literal: When Yu returned he was made Grand General and Governor of Yang with twenty ceremonial guards, his former offices unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Yu was made Grand General and Governor of Yang with twenty ceremonial guards, his other offices unchanged.

sentences.zh: 徐道覆至始興，猶據山澗，劉蕃等攻之，道覆先鴆妻子，然後自殺。

translations.literal: When Xu Daofu reached Shixing he still held the mountain ravines; Liu Fan and others attacked him; Daofu first poisoned his wife and children, then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu held the mountain ravines at Shixing; Liu Fan and others attacked. Daofu poisoned his wife and children, then killed himself.

sentences.zh: 盧循至番禺，收眾攻季高，劉蕃遣沈田子討之，循奔走。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun reached Panyu he gathered troops to attack Jigao; Liu Fan sent Shen Tianzi against him, and Xun fled.
translations.idiomatic: At Panyu Xun rallied troops against Jigao; Liu Fan sent Shen Tianzi against him, and Xun fled.

sentences.zh: 餘眾從嶺道襲合浦，克之。

translations.literal: The remnant host took the mountain route to strike Hepu and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: The remnants took the mountain route, seized Hepu, and held it.

sentences.zh: 進攻交阯，交州刺史杜惠度屢戰克捷，循投水而死。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Jiaozhi, they met Du Huidu, Inspector of Jiao, who repeatedly won in battle; Xun threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing on Jiaozhi, they met Du Huidu, Inspector of Jiao, who defeated them repeatedly; Xun drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 裕自為太尉、中書監。

translations.literal: Yu made himself Grand Marshal and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Yu appointed himself Grand Marshal and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 裕殺尚書左僕射謝混、兗州刺史劉蕃。

translations.literal: Yu killed the Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xie Hun and the Inspector of Yan Liu Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu executed Xie Hun, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Liu Fan, Inspector of Yan.

sentences.zh: 裕既權重，便懷異志，以荊州刺史劉毅頗有勇略，又據上流之所，心畏惡之，遂自討毅，遣參軍王鎮惡等襲江陵。

translations.literal: Once Yu's power was heavy he harbored rebellious intent; because the Inspector of Jing, Liu Yi, was quite bold in stratagem and held the upper reaches, he feared and hated him in his heart, and therefore campaigned against Yi himself, sending his staff officer Wang Zhen'e and others to strike Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: With power consolidated, Yu turned against his allies. Liu Yi, Inspector of Jing, was bold and held the upper Yangzi; Yu feared him and marched against him, sending Wang Zhen'e to strike Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡至豫章口，焚毅舟艦。

translations.literal: Zhen'e reached the mouth of Yuzhang and burned Yi's ships.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e reached the Yuzhang mouth and burned Yi's fleet.

sentences.zh: 毅兵逆戰不能抗，鎮惡馳入外城。

translations.literal: Yi's troops met them in battle but could not resist; Zhen'e galloped into the outer city.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's troops could not hold; Zhen'e galloped into the outer city.

sentences.zh: 于時毅病，乃阻內城。

translations.literal: Yi was then ill and barred himself in the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was ill and barred himself in the inner city.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡焚諸門攻之，其徒乃潰。

translations.literal: Zhen'e burned the gates and attacked; Yi's followers then collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e burned the gates and attacked; Yi's men broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 毅自北門出走，縊于道側，斬屍於市，誅其子姪。

translations.literal: Yi fled out the north gate, hanged himself by the roadside, his corpse was beheaded in the market, and his sons and nephews were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yi fled out the north gate and hanged himself by the road; his body was displayed in the market and his sons and nephews executed.

sentences.zh: 裕至江陵，誅南蠻校尉郗僧施、衞軍諮議謝邵等。

translations.literal: When Yu reached Jiangling he executed the Colonel of the Southern Man Xi Sheng, the Consultant of the Guard Army Xie Shao, and others.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangling Yu executed Xi Sheng, Colonel of the Southern Man, Xie Shao, consultant to the Guard Army, and others.

sentences.zh: 裕本寒微，不參士伍，及擅時政，便肆意殺戮，以威懼下。

translations.literal: Yu was originally humble and poor and had not joined the gentry ranks; once he monopolized the government of the age, he killed at will to terrify those below.
translations.idiomatic: Born humble and outside the gentry, once Yu seized power he killed at will to terrify his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 初以刁逵縛之之怨，誅其兄弟；

translations.literal: At first, because of the grudge of Diao Kui binding him, he executed Kui's brothers;
translations.idiomatic: First, remembering Diao Kui's humiliation, he executed Kui's brothers;

sentences.zh: 又以王愉、謝混、郗僧施之徒並皆時望，遂悉害之。

translations.literal: then because Wang Yu, Xie Hun, Xi Sheng, and their like were all men of repute in the age, he killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: then because Wang Yu, Xie Hun, Xi Sheng, and others enjoyed great renown, he killed them all.

sentences.zh: 分荊州為湘州，裕自總督。

translations.literal: He divided Jing to form Xiang, and Yu himself took overall command.
translations.idiomatic: He split Jing to create Xiang province and took overall command himself.

sentences.zh: 裕還於東府，召諸葛長民屏人閑語，密令壯士丁旿等出自幔後，於座拉之，長民墜地，死於牀側。

translations.literal: When Yu returned to the Eastern Headquarters he summoned Zhuge Changmin for a private talk with attendants dismissed, secretly ordered the stalwart Ding Wu and others to emerge from behind the curtain, seize him at his seat, and Changmin fell to the ground and died beside the couch.
translations.idiomatic: Back at the Eastern Headquarters, Yu summoned Zhuge Changmin for a private talk, then had stalwarts emerge from behind the curtain, seize him at his seat, and strike him dead beside the couch.

sentences.zh: 亦以才雄見忌也。

translations.literal: He too was killed because his talent and dominance aroused jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: He too was killed because his talent aroused Yu's jealousy.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史司馬休之頗得眾心，裕內懷忌憚，神䴥二年，率眾討之，遣龍驤將軍蒯恩等為前軍。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Jing, Sima Xiuzhi, had won considerable popular support; Yu harbored jealousy and dread within. In the second year of Shenjue he led troops against him and sent the Dragon Cavalry General Kuai En and others as the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi, Inspector of Jing, had won the people's loyalty; Yu feared him. In the second year of Shenjue he marched against him, with Kuai En, Dragon Cavalry General, in the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 裕進領荊州刺史，加黃鉞。

translations.literal: Yu advanced to take charge as Inspector of Jing and was given the yellow axe.
translations.idiomatic: Yu took office as Inspector of Jing and received the imperial axe.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史魯宗之率其子軌會休之于江陵。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Yong, Lu Zongzhi, led his son Gui to join Xiuzhi at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zongzhi, Inspector of Yong, led his son Gui to join Xiuzhi at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 軌等軍敗，乃與休之俱奔襄陽。

translations.literal: Gui and the others were defeated in battle and fled with Xiuzhi to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's army was defeated; he fled with Xiuzhi to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 裕自領南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: Yu himself took charge as Colonel of the Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: Yu took the post of Colonel of the Southern Man himself.

sentences.zh: 休之等奔姚興。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi and the others fled to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi and his followers fled to Yao Xing of Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 裕為太傅、揚州牧；

translations.literal: Yu was made Grand Tutor and Governor of Yang;
translations.idiomatic: Yu was made Grand Tutor and Governor of Yang;

sentences.zh: 劍履上殿，入朝不趨，讚拜不名；

translations.literal: he might wear sword and shoes in the hall, need not hasten when entering court, and in memorials of praise was not named;
translations.idiomatic: he might wear sword and shoes in the hall, enter court without hastening, and be addressed without his personal name in memorials;

sentences.zh: 置左右長史、司馬，從事中郎四人；

translations.literal: he was given left and right Chief Clerks, Marshals, and four Attendant Gentlemen;
translations.idiomatic: he was given left and right chief clerks, marshals, and four attendant gentlemen;

sentences.zh: 餘如故。

translations.literal: the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: his other privileges remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 裕又領平北將軍、徐兗二州刺史，增督南秦州，尋督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: Yu also took charge as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xu and Yan, was additionally made overseer of Southern Qin, and soon Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Yu also became General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xu and Yan, gained oversight of Southern Qin, and soon command of all armies.

sentences.zh: 裕志傾僭晉，若不外立功名，恐人望不許，乃西伐姚泓。

translations.literal: Yu's intent was to overturn the usurping Jin; if he did not win merit abroad, he feared popular expectation would not permit it, and therefore he campaigned west against Yao Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Yu meant to overthrow the Jin usurpers; fearing he lacked public support without foreign glory, he marched west against Yao Hong.

sentences.zh: 自領征西將軍、司豫二州刺史，尋領北雍州刺史，加前後部羽葆鼓吹，增班劍為四十人。

translations.literal: He himself took charge as General Who Campaigns West and Inspector of Si and Yu, soon also Inspector of Northern Yong, was given front and rear feathered banners and drums, and his ceremonial guard was increased to forty.
translations.idiomatic: He took office as General Who Campaigns West and Inspector of Si and Yu, soon also Northern Yong, gained imperial banners and drums, and forty ceremonial guards.

sentences.zh: 子義符為中軍將軍，監太尉留府事，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: His son Yifu was made Central Army General, supervised the Grand Marshal's affairs left at headquarters, and was given one set of drums and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yifu became Central Army General, supervised affairs at headquarters, and received a band of drums and pipes.

sentences.zh: 右僕射劉穆之為左僕射，領軍、中軍二府軍司，[9]入居東府，總攝內外。

translations.literal: The Right Vice Director Liu Muzhi was made Left Vice Director and army secretary of the Guard and Central Army headquarters;[9] he entered the Eastern Headquarters and took overall charge within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi was moved from Right to Left Vice Director and made army secretary of the Guard and Central Army headquarters;[9] he entered the Eastern Headquarters and took charge of court and camp.

sentences.zh: 穆之謂龍驤將軍王鎮惡曰：「公今委卿以關中，卿其勉之。」

translations.literal: Muzhi said to the Dragon Cavalry General Wang Zhen'e: "The lord now entrusts you with Guanzhong—do your utmost."
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi told Wang Zhen'e, Dragon Cavalry General: "The lord entrusts Guanzhong to you—do not fail him."

sentences.zh: 鎮惡曰：「吾今不克咸陽，誓不濟江，而公九錫不至者，亦卿之責矣。」

translations.literal: Zhen'e said: "If I do not take Xianyang now, I swear not to cross the river again—and if the lord's nine bestowals do not arrive, that too will be your responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e replied: "If I do not take Xianyang, I swear never to cross the Yangzi again—and if the nine bestowals do not come, that will be your fault as well."

sentences.zh: 裕率眾軍至彭城，加鎮北將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Yu led the mass of armies to Pengcheng and was additionally made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu led his armies to Pengcheng and was made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xu.

sentences.zh: 遣中兵參軍沈林子自汴入河，冠軍檀道濟與王鎮惡步出淮肥，裕將王仲德汎濟入河。

translations.literal: He sent the Central Army staff officer Shen Linzi from Bian into the Yellow River; the Champion Tan Daoji and Wang Zhen'e marched out from the Huai-Fei region, and Yu's general Wang Zhongde crossed by boat into the river.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Shen Linzi from Bian into the Yellow River; Tan Daoji and Wang Zhen'e marched from the Huai-Fei region, and Wang Zhongde crossed by boat into the river.

sentences.zh: 德宗封裕十郡為宋公，加相國、九錫，僭擬魏晉故事。

translations.literal: Dezong enfeoffed Yu with ten commanderies as Duke of Song, additionally made him Chancellor and bestowed the nine gifts, usurping the precedents of Wei and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong enfeoffed Yu as Duke of Song with ten commanderies, made him Chancellor, and bestowed the nine imperial gifts, following the usurpers' precedent of Wei and Jin.

sentences.zh: 王鎮惡進至宜陽，獨取潼關，沈林子自襄邑屯于陝城，姚泓諸將不能抗。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen'e advanced to Yiyang and alone took Tong Pass; Shen Linzi from Xiangyi encamped at Shancheng, and Yao Hong's generals could not resist.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e advanced to Yiyang and seized Tong Pass alone; Shen Linzi encamped at Shancheng from Xiangyi, and Yao Hong's generals could not hold.

sentences.zh: 始裕入河西上，太宗遣將軍娥清、長孫嵩等屯於河畔。

translations.literal: When Yu first entered the west of the river and marched upstream, Emperor Taizong sent the generals E Qing and Zhangsun Song and others to encamp on the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu marched west up the Yellow River, Emperor Taizong sent Generals E Qing and Zhangsun Song to encamp on the bank.

sentences.zh: 裕遣朱超石、劉榮祖等渡河，長孫道生破之，擒斬其將楊豐等。

translations.literal: Yu sent Zhu Chaoshi, Liu Rongzu, and others across the river; Zhangsun Daosheng defeated them and captured and beheaded their general Yang Feng and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent Zhu Chaoshi and Liu Rongzu across the river; Zhangsun Daosheng defeated them and killed their general Yang Feng.

sentences.zh: 裕遣將軍王仲德、趙倫之率沈田子等入武關，屯軍青泥。

translations.literal: Yu sent the generals Wang Zhongde and Zhao Lunzhi leading Shen Tianzi and others through Wu Pass to encamp at Qingni.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent Wang Zhongde and Zhao Lunzhi with Shen Tianzi through Wu Pass to camp at Qingni.

sentences.zh: 沈林子由秦嶺會田子於堯柳城。

translations.literal: Shen Linzi came by the Qin Mountains to join Tianzi at Yao Willow City.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Linzi crossed the Qin Mountains and joined Tianzi at Yao Willow City.

sentences.zh: 姚泓率眾數萬，不戰而還。

translations.literal: Yao Hong led several tens of thousands but returned without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong led tens of thousands but withdrew without a fight.

sentences.zh: 裕至關頭。

translations.literal: Yu reached Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Yu reached Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡至渭橋，破泓軍於橫門。

translations.literal: Zhen'e reached Wei Bridge and defeated Hong's army at Heng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e reached Wei Bridge and defeated Hong's army at Heng Gate.

sentences.zh: 裕至長安，執姚泓以歸，斬于建業市。

translations.literal: Yu reached Chang'an, took Yao Hong captive and brought him back, and executed him in the market of Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Yu entered Chang'an, took Yao Hong captive, and executed him in the Jianye market.

sentences.zh: 裕以其子義真為雍州刺史，鎮咸陽。

translations.literal: Yu made his son Yizhen Inspector of Yong and garrisoned him at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu appointed his son Yizhen Inspector of Yong and garrisoned him at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 進裕為宋王，增十郡，置百官，一擬舊制。

translations.literal: Yu was advanced to Prince of Song, given ten more commanderies, and all officials were installed, all modeled on the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was promoted to Prince of Song with ten more commanderies, a full bureaucracy installed on the old model.

sentences.zh: 裕還彭城。

translations.literal: Yu returned to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yu returned to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 赫連屈丐掠渭陽，義真遣沈田子率軍討之。

translations.literal: Helian Qubug raided the Wei River north bank; Yizhen sent Shen Tianzi with troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Qubug raided north of the Wei; Yizhen sent Shen Tianzi against him.

sentences.zh: 田子退軍陘上，鎮惡往就田子議之，田子斬鎮惡於幕下，又殺其兄弟羣從七人。

translations.literal: Tianzi withdrew his army to the heights; Zhen'e went to Tianzi to consult, and Tianzi beheaded Zhen'e beneath the tent canopy, then killed seven of his brothers and kin.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi withdrew to the heights; Zhen'e came to consult, and Tianzi killed him in the tent, then executed seven of his brothers and kin.

sentences.zh: 田子馳還，云「鎮惡有異志」，義真長史王脩執而斬之。

translations.literal: Tianzi galloped back and said Zhen'e harbored rebellious intent; Yizhen's Chief Clerk Wang Xiu seized and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi galloped back claiming Zhen'e was plotting treason; Wang Xiu, Yizhen's chief clerk, seized and executed him.

sentences.zh: 義真與左右多為不法，王脩每裁割之，左右咸怨，白義真曰：「王脩以關中阻險，兵食又足，欲謀反叛，宜早圖之。」

translations.literal: Yizhen and his attendants committed many unlawful acts; Wang Xiu constantly restrained them. The attendants all resented this and told Yizhen: "Wang Xiu, because Guanzhong is rugged and troops and grain are ample, intends to rebel—you should deal with him early."
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen and his attendants broke the law constantly; Wang Xiu restrained them. They resented him and told Yizhen: "With Guanzhong's defenses and ample supplies, Xiu means to rebel—you must act first."

sentences.zh: 義真遂遣左右殺脩。

translations.literal: Yizhen then sent his attendants to kill Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen sent his attendants to kill Xiu.

sentences.zh: 裕聞之，以朱齡石為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yu heard of this he made Zhu Lingshi Inspector of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Yu appointed Zhu Lingshi Inspector of Yong.

sentences.zh: 義真發自長安，將走江東，諸將競收財貨，次於灞上。

translations.literal: Yizhen set out from Chang'an intending to flee to the Jiang east; the generals vied to seize valuables and halted at Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen left Chang'an for the east; his generals plundered greedily and camped at Bashang.

sentences.zh: 赫連昌率眾追之，既至青泥，義真大敗，蒯恩與安西司馬毛脩之並被擒獲，參軍段橫，名犯高祖廟諱，單馬負義真走歸。

translations.literal: Helian Chang led troops in pursuit; when they reached Qingni, Yizhen suffered a great defeat. Kuai En and the Anxi Army Marshal Mao Xiuzhi were both captured; the staff officer Duan Heng—his name violating the taboo of Emperor Gaozu's temple—alone on horseback carried Yizhen and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Chang pursued them; at Qingni Yizhen was routed. Kuai En and Mao Xiuzhi were captured; Duan Heng, whose name violated Gaozu's taboo, fled alone on horseback with Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 朱齡石亦棄長安，奔就龍驤將軍王敬先于曹公故壘，既而城陷，被執見殺。

translations.literal: Zhu Lingshi also abandoned Chang'an and fled to the Dragon Cavalry General Wang Jingxian at Cao Cao's old rampart; soon the city fell, he was seized and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Lingshi abandoned Chang'an and fled to Wang Jingxian at Cao Cao's old fort; the city fell, and he was captured and killed.

sentences.zh: 德宗死，裕立德宗弟德文，裕又自增十郡。

translations.literal: Dezong died; Yu installed Dezong's younger brother Dewen, and Yu himself added ten more commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong died, Yu installed his brother Dewen and added ten commanderies to his own domain.

sentences.zh: 裕遣司馬傅亮赴建業，令徵己入輔。

translations.literal: Yu sent his Marshal Fu Liang to Jianye with orders to summon him to assist at court.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent Fu Liang to Jianye to summon him to court.

sentences.zh: 德文禪其位，遂自號為宋，改年為永初，時泰常五年也。

translations.literal: Dewen abdicated in his favor; Yu then styled himself Song, changed the era name to Yongchu—it was the fifth year of Taichang.
translations.idiomatic: Dewen abdicated; Yu declared the Song dynasty and changed the era to Yongchu, in the fifth year of Taichang.

sentences.zh: 裕既僭立，頻請和通，太宗許之。

translations.literal: Once Yu had usurped the throne he repeatedly sought peace and communication; Emperor Taizong consented.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yu had usurped the throne he repeatedly sought peace; Emperor Taizong agreed.

sentences.zh: 六年，裕遣其中軍將軍沈範、索季孫等朝貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Yu sent his Central Army General Shen Fan, Suo Jisun, and others on tribute missions to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Yu sent Shen Fan, Suo Jisun, and others to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 七年五月裕死。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year Yu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventh year Yu died.

sentences.zh: 子義符僭立。

translations.literal: His son Yifu usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yifu seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 太宗以其禮敬不足，遣山陽公奚斤等率步騎二萬於滑臺渡河南討。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong, because his courtesy was insufficient, sent the Duke of Shanyang, Xi Jin, and others with twenty thousand foot and horse to cross south of the Yellow River at Huatai in campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Finding his courtesy lacking, Emperor Taizong sent Duke Xi Jin of Shanyang with twenty thousand troops across the Yellow River at Huatai.

sentences.zh: 義符司州刺史毛德祖遣司馬翟廣領步騎三千來拒。

translations.literal: Yifu's Inspector of Si, Mao Dezu, sent his Marshal Zhai Guang leading three thousand foot and horse to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Dezu, Yifu's Inspector of Si, sent Zhai Guang with three thousand troops to resist.

sentences.zh: 司空奚斤以千餘騎徇陳留，太守嚴稜率眾降。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Xi Jin with more than a thousand horse raided Chenliu; the Administrator Yan Ling led his host in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin raided Chenliu with a thousand cavalry; Administrator Yan Ling surrendered.

sentences.zh: 仍攻滑臺，其東郡太守王景度奔走，斬其司馬陽瓚。

translations.literal: He then attacked Huatai; Yifu's Administrator of Dong, Wang Jingdu, fled, and his Marshal Yang Zan was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Huatai; Wang Jingdu, Administrator of Dong, fled, and his marshal Yang Zan was killed.

sentences.zh: 德祖又遣其將竇應明攻輜重于石濟。

translations.literal: Dezu again sent his general Dou Yingming to attack the baggage train at Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: Dezu sent Dou Yingming to attack the baggage train at Shiji.

sentences.zh: 奚斤於土樓大破廣等，乘勝徑至虎牢。

translations.literal: Xi Jin at Tulu greatly defeated Guang and others, pressed the victory straight to Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin routed Guang at Tulu and pressed on to Hulao.

sentences.zh: 義符遣其將杜垣等與徐州刺史王仲德次湖陸。

translations.literal: Yifu sent his generals Du Yuan and others with the Inspector of Xu, Wang Zhongde, to camp at Hulu.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu sent Du Yuan and Wang Zhongde, Inspector of Xu, to camp at Hulu.

sentences.zh: 太宗詔安平公叔孫建等軍於泗瀆口，義符兗州刺史徐琰委尹卯城奔退，於是泰山諸郡悉棄戍而走。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong ordered the Duke of Ping'an, Sunjian, and others to encamp at the mouth of the Si River; Yifu's Inspector of Yan, Xu Yan, abandoned Yincheng and fled, and thereupon all the commanderies of Taishan abandoned their garrisons and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong ordered Duke Sunjian of Ping'an to camp at the Si mouth; Xu Yan, Inspector of Yan, abandoned Yincheng and fled, and the Taishan commanderies abandoned their garrisons.

sentences.zh: 太宗詔蒼梧子公孫表等復攻虎牢，義符遣將檀道濟率師赴救。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong ordered the son of Cangwu, Gongsun Biao, and others again to attack Hulao; Yifu sent the general Tan Daoji with troops to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong ordered Gongsun Biao to attack Hulao again; Yifu sent Tan Daoji to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 八年，義符改年為景平。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Yifu changed the era name to Jingping.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Yifu changed the era name to Jingping.

sentences.zh: 奚斤進攻金墉，義符河南太守王涓之出奔。

translations.literal: Xi Jin advanced to attack Jinyong; Yifu's Administrator of Henan, Wang Juanzhi, fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin attacked Jinyong; Wang Juanzhi, Administrator of Henan, fled.

sentences.zh: 太宗南巡至鄴。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong made a southern tour to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong toured south to Ye.

sentences.zh: 奚斤自金墉還圍虎牢。

translations.literal: Xi Jin returned from Jinyong to besiege Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin returned from Jinyong to besiege Hulao.

sentences.zh: 太宗又詔安平公叔孫建等東擊青州，其刺史竺夔守東陽城，濟南太守垣苗自梁鄒奔夔。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong again ordered the Duke of Ping'an, Sunjian, and others east to strike Qing; its Inspector Zhu Kui held Dongyang city, and the Administrator of Jinan, Yuan Miao, fled from Liangzou to join Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong ordered Sunjian east against Qing; Zhu Kui held Dongyang, and Yuan Miao, Administrator of Jinan, fled from Liangzou to join him.

sentences.zh: 奚斤分軍攻潁川，太守李元德奔還項城。

translations.literal: Xi Jin divided his army to attack Yingchuan; the Administrator Li Yuande fled back to Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin attacked Yingchuan; Li Yuande, the administrator, fled to Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 斤又遣騎破高平郡所統五縣，略居人二千餘家。

translations.literal: Jin again sent cavalry to defeat the five counties under Gaoping Commandery and carried off more than two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent cavalry against five Gaoping counties and carried off more than two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 叔孫建以時暑班師。

translations.literal: Sunjian withdrew the army because of the summer heat.
translations.idiomatic: Sunjian withdrew because of the summer heat.

sentences.zh: 檀道濟、王仲德向青州，遂不敢進。

translations.literal: Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde moved toward Qing and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde moved toward Qing but dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 太宗至虎牢，因幸洛陽，乃北渡河。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong reached Hulao, then visited Luoyang, and crossed the river north.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong reached Hulao, visited Luoyang, and crossed north of the river.

sentences.zh: 斤克虎牢，擒德祖及其滎陽太守翟廣、廣武將軍竇霸等，義符豫州刺史劉粹屯項城，不敢進。

translations.literal: Jin took Hulao and captured Dezu along with his Administrator of Xingyang, Zhai Guang, the General of Broad Might Dou Ba, and others; Yifu's Inspector of Yu, Liu Cui, encamped at Xiangcheng and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Jin took Hulao and captured Dezu, Zhai Guang, Dou Ba, and others; Liu Cui, Inspector of Yu, held Xiangcheng and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 斤遣步騎至許昌，潁川太守索元德奔項城；

translations.literal: Jin sent foot and horse to Xuchang; the Administrator of Yingchuan, Suo Yuande, fled to Xiangcheng;
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent troops to Xuchang; Suo Yuande, Administrator of Yingchuan, fled to Xiangcheng;

sentences.zh: 遂圍汝陽，太守王公度突圍而出；

translations.literal: then besieged Ruyang; the Administrator Wang Gongdu broke out of the encirclement and fled;
translations.idiomatic: then besieged Ruyang; Wang Gongdu, the administrator, broke out and fled;

sentences.zh: 仍破邵陵，掠萬餘口而還。

translations.literal: then defeated Shaoling and carried off more than ten thousand people before returning.
translations.idiomatic: then took Shaoling and carried off more than ten thousand people.

sentences.zh: 始光初，義符司空徐羨之、尚書令傅亮、領軍謝晦等專其朝政，收其廬陵王義真，徙于新安郡，殺之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shiguang, Yifu's Minister of Works Xu Xianzhi, Director of the Masters of Writing Fu Liang, Army Commander Xie Hui, and others monopolized court government, seized his Prince of Luling Yizhen, moved him to Xin'an Commandery, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shiguang, Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, and Xie Hui monopolized the court, seized Prince Yizhen of Luling, exiled him to Xin'an, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 義符昏暴失德，羨之等勒兵入殿，時義符在華林舟中，兵士競進，殺其侍者，扶義符出東閤，廢為營陽王。

translations.literal: Yifu was benighted, brutal, and lost in virtue; Xianzhi and the others led troops into the hall. At the time Yifu was in a boat at Hualin; soldiers vied to advance, killed his attendants, and helped Yifu out the eastern gate, deposing him as Prince of Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu was brutal and lost the Mandate; Xianzhi's troops entered the palace while Yifu was boating at Hualin. They killed his attendants, dragged him out, and deposed him as Prince of Yingyang.

sentences.zh: 遂徙于吳郡，於金昌亭殺之。

translations.literal: He was then moved to Wu Commandery and killed at Jinchang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was exiled to Wu and killed at Jinchang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 亮等立義符弟荊州刺史義隆，號年元嘉。

translations.literal: Liang and the others installed Yifu's younger brother, the Inspector of Jing Yilong, and proclaimed the era Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: They installed Yifu's younger brother Yilong, Inspector of Jing, and proclaimed the era Yuanjia.

sentences.zh: 遣使趙道生朝貢。

translations.literal: He sent the envoy Zhao Daosheng on tribute missions to court.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhao Daosheng to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 二年，徐羨之、傅亮等歸政於義隆，不許。

translations.literal: In the second year Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, and others returned government to Yilong; he did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang tried to return power to Yilong; he refused.

sentences.zh: 三年，義隆信其侍中王華之言，誅羨之、傅亮，遣其將檀道濟等討荊州刺史謝晦。

translations.literal: In the third year Yilong believed his Palace Attendant Wang Hua and executed Xianzhi and Fu Liang, sending his generals Tan Daoji and others to campaign against the Inspector of Jing, Xie Hui.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Yilong believed Wang Hua and executed Xianzhi and Fu Liang, then sent Tan Daoji against Xie Hui, Inspector of Jing.

sentences.zh: 晦率眾東下，謀廢義隆，以討王華為辭，破義隆將到彥之。

translations.literal: Hui led his host east, plotting to depose Yilong under the pretext of punishing Wang Hua, and defeated Yilong's general Dao Yanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Hui marched east to depose Yilong, claiming to punish Wang Hua, and defeated Dao Yanzhi.

sentences.zh: 及聞道濟將至，晦眾崩散。

translations.literal: When he heard Daoji was coming, Hui's host collapsed and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Daoji was coming, Hui's army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 晦走江陵，乃攜其弟遁等北走，至安陸延頭，為戍主光順之所執，斬于建業。

translations.literal: Hui fled to Jiangling, then took his younger brother Dun and others north; reaching Yantou at Anlu, he was seized by the garrison commander Guang Shunzhi and beheaded at Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Hui fled to Jiangling, then north with his brother Dun; at Yantou in Anlu he was captured by Guang Shunzhi and executed at Jianye.

sentences.zh: 八月，義隆使其殿中將軍吉恒朝貢。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Yilong sent his Palace General Ji Heng on tribute missions to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Yilong sent Ji Heng to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 神䴥二年，又遣殿中將軍孫橫之朝貢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenjue he again sent the Palace General Sun Hengzhi on tribute missions to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shenjue he sent Sun Hengzhi to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 三年，又遣殿中將軍田奇朝貢。

translations.literal: In the third year he again sent the Palace General Tian Qi on tribute missions to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he sent Tian Qi to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 尋遣其右將軍到彥之、安北將軍王仲德、兗州刺史竺靈秀舟師入河，驍騎將軍段橫寇虎牢；

translations.literal: Soon he sent his General of the Right Dao Yanzhi, General Who Pacifies the North Wang Zhongde, and the Inspector of Yan Zhu Lingxiu with a fleet into the river, and the Rapid Cavalry General Duan Heng to raid Hulao;
translations.idiomatic: Soon he sent Dao Yanzhi, Wang Zhongde, and Zhu Lingxiu with a fleet up the river, and Duan Heng to raid Hulao;

sentences.zh: 又遣其豫州刺史劉德武、後將軍、長沙王義欣至彭城為後繼。

translations.literal: he also sent his Inspector of Yu Liu Dewu and the Rear General, Prince of Changsha Yixin, to Pengcheng as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: he sent Liu Dewu, Inspector of Yu, and Prince Yixin of Changsha to Pengcheng as reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 到彥之寇碻磝，分軍向虎牢及洛陽。

translations.literal: Dao Yanzhi raided Que'ao and divided his army toward Hulao and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Yanzhi attacked Que'ao and sent detachments toward Hulao and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 世祖詔河南諸軍收眾北渡以驕之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu ordered the armies of Henan to gather their forces and cross north of the river to make them overconfident.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu ordered the Henan armies to withdraw north of the river to lure them on.

sentences.zh: 尋詔冠軍將軍安頡等率眾自盟津渡，攻金墉，義隆建武將軍杜驥出奔，遂乘勝進攻虎牢，陷之，斬其司州刺史尹沖。

translations.literal: Soon he ordered the General Who Conquers Champions An Pi and others to lead troops across from Meng Ford, attack Jinyong; Yilong's General Who Establishes Might Du Ji fled, and they pressed the victory to attack Hulao, took it, and beheaded his Inspector of Si Yin Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon An Pi crossed at Meng Ford and attacked Jinyong; Du Ji fled; they took Hulao and killed Yin Chong, Inspector of Si.

sentences.zh: 叔孫建大破竺靈秀，追至湖陸。

translations.literal: Sunjian greatly defeated Zhu Lingxiu and pursued to Hulu.
translations.idiomatic: Sunjian routed Zhu Lingxiu and pursued to Hulu.

sentences.zh: 四年，頡攻滑臺，彥之與王仲德等焚舟棄甲，走歸彭城。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Pi attacked Huatai; Yanzhi and Wang Zhongde and others burned their boats, cast off their armor, and fled back to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Pi attacked Huatai; Yanzhi and Wang Zhongde burned their boats, abandoned their armor, and fled to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 義隆又遣檀道濟救滑臺，叔孫建、長孫道生擊之。
