translations.literal: Yilong again sent Tan Daoji to relieve Huatai; Sunjian and Zhangsun Daosheng struck them.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong sent Tan Daoji to relieve Huatai; Sunjian and Zhangsun Daosheng attacked.

sentences.zh: 道濟至高梁山，頡等攻克滑臺，擒其司徒從事中郎朱脩之等，道濟走奔歷城，夜乃遁還。

translations.literal: Daoji reached Gaoliang Mountain; Pi and others took Huatai and captured his Palace Attendant of the Secretariat Zhu Xiuzhi and others; Daoji fled to Licheng and slipped away by night.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji reached Gaoliang Mountain; Pi took Huatai and captured Zhu Xiuzhi; Daoji fled to Licheng and escaped by night.

sentences.zh: 義隆青州刺史蕭思話亦棄鎮奔于平昌，其東陽積粟為百姓所焚。

translations.literal: Yilong's Inspector of Qing Xiao Sihua also abandoned his post and fled to Pingchang; the grain stored at Dongyang was burned by the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Sihua, Inspector of Qing, abandoned his post and fled to Pingchang; the people burned the grain at Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 延和元年五月，義隆又遣趙道生朝貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of Yanhe 1, Yilong again sent Zhao Daosheng to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Yanhe 1, Yilong again sent Zhao Daosheng to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，詔兼散騎常侍宋宣使於義隆，且為皇太子結親。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, an edict ordered Song Xuan, Acting Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, to go as envoy to Yilong and also to arrange a marriage for the imperial crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year, an edict ordered Song Xuan, Acting Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, to go as envoy to Yilong and also to arrange a marriage for the imperial crown prince.

sentences.zh: 九月，義隆遣趙道生貢馴象一。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Yilong sent Zhao Daosheng to present one trained elephant as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Yilong sent Zhao Daosheng to present one trained elephant as tribute.

sentences.zh: 太延二年三月，義隆遣使會元紹朝貢。

translations.literal: In the third month of Taiyan 2, Yilong sent envoys together with Yuan Shao to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Taiyan 2, Yilong sent envoys together with Yuan Shao to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 義隆忌其司空檀道濟，遂誅之。

translations.literal: Yilong feared his Minister of Works Tan Daoji, and so executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong feared his Minister of Works Tan Daoji, and so executed him.

sentences.zh: 道濟臨死，脫幘投地曰：「乃復壞汝萬里長城。」

translations.literal: As Daoji was about to die, he took off his headcloth, threw it to the ground, and said, “You have destroyed your Great Wall of ten thousand li.”
translations.idiomatic: As Daoji was about to die, he took off his headcloth, threw it to the ground, and said, “You have destroyed your Great Wall of ten thousand li.”

sentences.zh: 三年三月，義隆遣其散騎常侍劉熙伯朝貢，且論納幣。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year, Yilong sent his Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Liu Xibo to court with tribute and also to discuss presenting betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the third year, Yilong sent his Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Liu Xibo to court with tribute and also to discuss presenting betrothal gifts.

sentences.zh: 六月，義隆女死，不果為婚。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Yilong’s daughter died, so the marriage did not take place.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Yilong’s daughter died, so the marriage did not take place.

sentences.zh: 五年十一月，義隆遣黃延年獻馴象。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fifth year, Yilong sent Huang Yannian to present a trained elephant.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fifth year, Yilong sent Huang Yannian to present a trained elephant.

sentences.zh: 真君初，義隆徙其弟大將軍義康於豫章。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenjun era, Yilong moved his younger brother Yikang, General-in-Chief, to Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenjun era, Yilong moved his younger brother Yikang, General-in-Chief, to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 二年，其龍驤參軍巴東扶令育詣義隆理義康，義隆大怒，收育殺之。

translations.literal: In the second year, Fu Lingyu of Badong, a Consulting Officer of the Dragon-Surging command, went to Yilong to plead Yikang’s case. Yilong was furious, arrested Lingyu, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Fu Lingyu of Badong, a Consulting Officer of the Dragon-Surging command, went to Yilong to plead Yikang’s case. Yilong was furious, arrested Lingyu, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 四月，義隆遣使黃延年朝貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Yilong sent the envoy Huang Yannian to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, Yilong sent the envoy Huang Yannian to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 十二月，義隆又遣黃延年朝貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Yilong again sent Huang Yannian to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Yilong again sent Huang Yannian to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 是歲，義隆梁州刺史劉真道將裴方明攻擊楊難當，難當捨仇池，將妻子來奔。

translations.literal: That year Yilong's Inspector of Liang Liu Zhendao and his general Pei Fangming attacked Yang Dang; Dang abandoned Chouchi and came fleeing with wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: That year Liu Zhendao and Pei Fangming attacked Yang Dang; Dang abandoned Chouchi and fled with his family.

sentences.zh: 三年，世祖詔琅邪王司馬楚之等討之。

translations.literal: In the third year Emperor Shizu ordered the Prince of Langya, Sima Chuzhi, and others to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Emperor Shizu ordered Prince Sima Chuzhi of Langya against him.

sentences.zh: 安西將軍古弼、[11]平西將軍元濟等邀義隆秦州刺史胡崇之於濁水，破擒之，餘眾奔漢中。

translations.literal: The General Who Pacifies the West Gu Bi [11] and the General Who Pacifies the West Yuan Ji and others intercepted Yilong's Inspector of Qin Hu Chongzhi at Zhuoshui, defeated and captured him, and the remnant host fled to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Bi, General Who Pacifies the West,[11] and Yuan Ji ambushed Hu Chongzhi, Inspector of Qin, at Zhuoshui, captured him, and the remnants fled to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 義隆立難當兄子文德為秦州刺史、武都王，戍茄蘆，弼等討平之。

translations.literal: Yilong installed Dang's elder brother's son Wendé as Inspector of Qin and King of Wudu, garrisoned Jialu, and Bi and others campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong installed Wendé as Inspector of Qin and King of Wudu at Jialu; Bi pacified them.

sentences.zh: 義隆遂殺真道、方明。

translations.literal: Yilong then killed Zhendao and Fangming.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong then executed Zhendao and Fangming.

sentences.zh: 五年，義隆復遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Yilong again sent envoys on tribute missions to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Yilong sent tribute envoys again.

sentences.zh: 六年，其員外散騎侍郎孔熙先以才學而不見用，太子詹事范曄以家門淫汙，為世所薄，與熙先及外生謝綜謀殺義隆，立其弟前大將軍義康。

translations.literal: In the sixth year his Extraordinary Gentleman Attendant Kong Xixian, though talented in learning, was not employed; the Grand Tutor of the Heir Fan Ye, because his household was licentious and filthy, was despised by the age—together with Xixian and his sister's son Xie Zong they plotted to kill Yilong and install his younger brother, the former Grand General Yikang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Kong Xixian, talented but unemployed, and Fan Ye, Grand Tutor of the Heir, despised for his family's debauchery, plotted with Xixian and Xie Zong to kill Yilong and install his brother Yikang.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹徐湛之告之，乃誅曄等，徙義康於安成郡，御史監守。

translations.literal: The Governor of Danyang Xu Chenzhi informed on them; they then executed Ye and the others and moved Yikang to Ancheng Commandery under censor surveillance.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chenzhi, Governor of Danyang, informed; they executed Ye and exiled Yikang to Ancheng under guard.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔諸軍掠濟陰、金鄉等七縣，并驅其青冀二州民戶而還。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he ordered the armies to raid seven counties including Jiyin and Jinxiang, and drove off the households of Qing and Ji as well before returning.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the armies raided seven counties including Jiyin and Jinxiang and drove off the people of Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 北地人蓋吳聚眾反，義隆以吳為安西將軍、雍州刺史，封北地公，規亂雍州，詔諸軍討平之。

translations.literal: Gai Wu of Beidi gathered a host in rebellion; Yilong made Wu General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong, enfeoffed him as Duke of Beidi, and plotted turmoil in Yong; he ordered the armies to campaign and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Wu of Beidi rebelled; Yilong made him General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yong, Duke of Beidi, to stir trouble in Yong; the armies crushed him.

sentences.zh: 義隆好行小計，扇動邊民，內起山苑，窮侈極麗，役使百姓，江南苦之。

translations.literal: Yilong loved petty stratagems, stirred the border peoples, raised mountain parks within, exhausted extravagance to the utmost splendor, and pressed the common people into service—the Jiang south suffered bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong loved petty schemes, stirred the borders, built lavish mountain parks, and oppressed the people—the south suffered bitterly.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，義隆遣使獻孔雀。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year Yilong sent envoys presenting peacocks.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year Yilong sent peacocks as tribute.

sentences.zh: 十一年二月，世祖欲獵於雲夢，發使告義隆，勿相猜阻，義隆請奉詔。

translations.literal: In the second month of the eleventh year Emperor Shizu wished to hunt at Yunmeng and sent envoys telling Yilong not to suspect or obstruct; Yilong asked to obey the decree.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the eleventh year Emperor Shizu planned to hunt at Yunmeng and asked Yilong not to interfere; Yilong agreed.

sentences.zh: 世祖南巡，義隆邊城閉門拒守，世祖忿之，乃攻懸瓠。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu toured south; Yilong's border cities shut their gates and held fast. The emperor was angry and attacked Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: On his southern tour, Yilong's border cities barred their gates; enraged, Emperor Shizu attacked Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 分遣使者安慰降民，其不服者誅戮之。

translations.literal: He sent envoys separately to comfort those who submitted; those who would not submit were executed.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to comfort those who submitted; those who resisted were killed.

sentences.zh: 義隆汝南、南頓、汝陽、潁川太守，並棄城奔走。

translations.literal: Yilong's Administrators of Runan, Nandun, Ruyang, and Yingchuan all abandoned their cities and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The administrators of Runan, Nandun, Ruyang, and Yingchuan all fled.

sentences.zh: 義隆安北將軍、武陵王駿遣參軍劉泰之、臧肇之，殿中將軍尹懷義、程天祚等以千餘騎至汝陽，永昌王仁擊破之，[12]斬泰之、肇之，執天祚等。

translations.literal: Yilong's General Who Pacifies the North, the Prince of Wuling Jun, sent his staff officers Liu Taizhi and Zang Zhaozhi and the Palace Generals Yin Huaiyi and Cheng Tianzuo and others with more than a thousand horse to Ruyang; the Prince of Yongchang Ren defeated them,[12] beheaded Taizhi and Zhaozhi, and seized Tianzuo and others.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jun of Wuling sent Liu Taizhi, Zang Zhaozhi, and others with a thousand cavalry to Ruyang; Prince Ren of Yongchang defeated them,[12] killed Taizhi and Zhaozhi, and captured Tianzuo.

sentences.zh: 義隆又遣寧朔將軍王玄謨率其太子步兵校尉沈慶之、鎮軍諮議參軍申坦等入河，青冀二州刺史蕭斌及駿水陸並進，太子左衞率臧質統驍騎將軍王方回、安蠻司馬劉康祖、右軍參軍梁坦造許、洛，右將軍豫州刺史南平王鑠。

translations.literal: Yilong again sent the General of the Pacifying North Wang Xuemo leading his Heir's Commandant of Footsoldiers Shen Qingzhi, the Pacifying Army Consultant Shen Tan, and others into the river; the Inspectors of Qing and Ji Xiao Bin and Jun advanced by land and water together; the Heir's Left Guard Leader Zang Zhi commanded the Rapid Cavalry General Wang Fanghui, the Southern Man Army Marshal Liu Kangzu, and the Right Army staff officer Liang Tan to strike Xu and Luo; the General of the Right and Inspector of Yu, the Prince of Nanping Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong sent Wang Xuemo with Shen Qingzhi and Shen Tan up the river; Xiao Bin and Jun advanced by land and sea; Zang Zhi led Wang Fanghui, Liu Kangzu, and Liang Tan against Xu and Luo; Prince Shuo of Nanping held Yu.

sentences.zh: [13]太尉江夏王義恭為諸軍節度，梁、南秦二州刺史劉秀之統輔國將軍楊文德、宣威將軍劉洪宗向汧隴，護軍將軍蕭思話部龍驤將軍杜坦、竟陵太守劉德願向武關。

translations.literal: [13] The Grand Marshal, Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, was commander of all armies; the Inspectors of Liang and Southern Qin Liu Xiuzhi commanded the General Who Assists the State Yang Wende and the General Who Displays Might Liu Hongzong toward Qian-Long; the Guard Army General Xiao Sihua deployed the Dragon Cavalry General Du Tan and the Administrator of Jingling Liu Deyuan toward Wu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: [13] Prince Yigong of Jiangxia commanded all armies; Liu Xiuzhi led Yang Wende and Liu Hongzong toward Qian-Long; Xiao Sihua sent Du Tan and Liu Deyuan toward Wu Pass.

sentences.zh: 義隆令王公妃主及其朝士牧守下逮富人通出私財，以助軍費，士庶怨之。

translations.literal: Yilong ordered princes, dukes, consorts, princesses, court ministers, prefects, administrators, and down to the wealthy to contribute private wealth to aid military expenses; gentry and commoners resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong forced princes, officials, and the wealthy to fund the war from private wealth; the people resented it.

sentences.zh: 南兗及青、冀、兗、豫三五簡發，以配戎行；

translations.literal: From Southern Yan and Qing, Ji, Yan, and Yu, three or five men from each household were selected for draft;[14] they were assigned to the army ranks;
translations.idiomatic: From Southern Yan, Qing, Ji, Yan, and Yu, three to five men per household were drafted;[14] they were assigned to the ranks;

sentences.zh: 揚、南徐、兗、江州富民並四分之一。

translations.literal: from Yang, Southern Xu, Yan, and Jiang, one quarter of the wealthy households as well.
translations.idiomatic: from Yang, Southern Xu, Yan, and Jiang, one quarter of wealthy households as well.

sentences.zh: [15]建威司馬申元吉趣泗瀆，蕭斌至碻磝，王玄謨遣軍主王寶惠攻滑臺，右軍蕭鑠遣中兵參軍梁坦等進軍小索。

translations.literal: [15] The Establishing Might Army Marshal Shen Yuanji hastened to the Si River mouth; Xiao Bin reached Que'ao; Wang Xuemo sent the army commander Wang Baohui to attack Huatai; the Right Army Xiao Shuo sent the Central Army staff officer Liang Tan and others to advance on Xiaosuo.
translations.idiomatic: [15] Shen Yuanji hastened to the Si mouth; Xiao Bin reached Que'ao; Wang Xuemo sent Wang Baohui against Huatai; Xiao Shuo sent Liang Tan against Xiaosuo.

sentences.zh: 世祖詔諸軍援滑臺，大敗王寶惠等，王玄謨走還碻磝。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu ordered the armies to relieve Huatai, greatly defeated Wang Baohui and others, and Wang Xuemo fled back to Que'ao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu relieved Huatai, routed Wang Baohui, and Xuemo fled to Que'ao.

sentences.zh: 蕭斌遣申坦與梁坦、垣護之據兩當城，斌退還歷下。

translations.literal: Xiao Bin sent Shen Tan with Liang Tan and Yuan Huzhi to hold Liangdang city; Bin withdrew to Lixia.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bin posted Shen Tan, Liang Tan, and Yuan Huzhi at Liangdang and withdrew to Lixia.

sentences.zh: 及車駕渡河，梁坦退走，棄甲山積。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage crossed the river, Liang Tan retreated in flight, casting off armor in mountain heaps.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor crossed the river, Liang Tan fled, leaving armor heaped like hills.

sentences.zh: 車駕發滑臺，過碻磝，義隆又遣雍州刺史、竟陵王誕率其將薛安都、柳元景等入盧氏，進攻弘農。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage set out from Huatai, passed Que'ao; Yilong again sent the Inspector of Yong, the Prince of Jingling Dan, leading his generals Xue Andu, Liu Yuanjing, and others into Lushi to attack Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor left Huatai, passed Que'ao; Yilong sent Prince Dan of Jingling with Xue Andu and Liu Yuanjing through Lushi against Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 詔洛州刺史張提率眾度崤，蒲城鎮將何難於風陵堆濟河，秦州刺史杜道生至閿鄉。

translations.literal: He ordered the Inspector of Luo Zhang Ti to lead troops across Xiao; the garrison commander of Pucheng He Nan crossed the river at Fenglingdui; the Inspector of Qin Du Daosheng reached Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ti crossed Xiao; He Nan crossed at Fenglingdui; Du Daosheng reached Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 元景退走。

translations.literal: Yuanjing retreated in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing fled.

sentences.zh: 十一月，車駕從東安山出下邳，義隆鄒山戍主、魯陽陽平二郡太守崔邪利降。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the imperial carriage came out from Dong'an Mountain to Xiapi; the garrison commander of Zou Mountain and the Administrator of the two commanderies of Luyang and Yangping, Cui Xieli, surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the emperor came from Dong'an Mountain to Xiapi; Cui Xieli, garrison commander of Zou Mountain, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 楚王建、南康侯杜道儁進軍清西，至留城。

translations.literal: The Prince of Chu Jian and the Marquis of Nankang Du Daojun advanced west of Qing to Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian of Chu and Marquis Du Daojun of Nankang advanced to Liucheng.

sentences.zh: 義隆鎮軍劉駿參軍馬文恭至蕭城，軍主嵇玄敬至留城，並為覘候，見官軍俱時退走。

translations.literal: Yilong's Pacifying Army Liu Jun's staff officer Ma Wengong reached Xiaocheng; the army commander Ji Xuanjing reached Liucheng—both as scouts—and seeing the imperial armies all withdrew at once.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Wengong reached Xiaocheng and Ji Xuanjing Liucheng as scouts; seeing the imperial armies, both withdrew.

sentences.zh: 永昌王仁攻懸瓠，拔之，獲義隆守將趙淮，過定項城，破尉武戍，執其戍主。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yongchang Ren attacked Xuancheng, took it, captured Yilong's garrison general Zhao Huai, passed and pacified Xiangcheng, broke the Wei Wu garrison, and seized its commander.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ren of Yongchang took Xuancheng, captured Zhao Huai, pacified Xiangcheng, and seized the Wei Wu garrison.

sentences.zh: 進攻壽陽，屯兵於孫叔敖冢，[16]掠馬頭、鍾離二郡。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Shouyang, encamped at the tomb of Sun Shu'ao,[16] and raided the two commanderies of Matou and Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Shouyang, camped at Sun Shu'ao's tomb,[16] and raided Matou and Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 義隆遣左軍將軍劉康祖赴壽陽，與仁相遇，仁大破之，盡坑其眾，斬康祖，傳首示壽春，獲其將胡盛之、王羅漢等。

translations.literal: Yilong sent the Left Army General Liu Kangzu to Shouyang; he met Ren, and Ren greatly defeated him, buried all his host alive, beheaded Kangzu, sent the head to display at Shouchun, and captured his generals Hu Shengzhi, Wang Luohan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kangzu marched to Shouyang, met Ren, and was routed; Ren buried his army alive, killed Kangzu, displayed his head at Shouchun, and captured Hu Shengzhi and Wang Luohan.

sentences.zh: 以所斬首使軍士曳之，遶城三匝，積之城西，高與城齊。

translations.literal: He had soldiers drag the severed heads around the city three circuits, heaping them west of the wall as high as the wall itself.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers dragged the heads around the city three times and heaped them west of the wall as high as the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 劉鑠乃焚四郭廬舍，嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Liu Shuo then burned the dwellings of the four outer wards and shut the city, holding fast.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shuo burned the outer wards and barred the gates.

sentences.zh: 車駕至盱眙、淮、泗。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage reached Xuyi, the Huai, and the Si.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reached Xuyi and the Huai-Si region.

sentences.zh: 義隆遣輔國將軍臧質率師至盱眙，頓軍城北。

translations.literal: Yilong sent the General Who Assists the State Zang Zhi with troops to Xuyi, encamping north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong sent Zang Zhi to Xuyi, camping north of the city.

sentences.zh: 六軍於上流濟淮，質遣司馬胡崇之等率所領於山上立營，建威將軍毛熙祚據城前大浦。

translations.literal: The six armies crossed the Huai upstream; Zhi sent his Marshal Hu Chongzhi and others to lead their commands and camp on the mountain; the General Who Establishes Might Mao Xizuo held the great ford before the city.
translations.idiomatic: The six armies crossed upstream; Hu Chongzhi camped on the heights; Mao Xizuo held the ford before the city.

sentences.zh: 詔攻二軍，斬崇之、熙祚等及他首數千級，眾悉赴水死。

translations.literal: An edict ordered attack on both armies; Chongzhi, Xizuo, and others were beheaded along with several thousand other heads; the host all rushed into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: The armies attacked both forces, killed Chongzhi and Xizuo and thousands more; the rest drowned.

sentences.zh: 淮南之民皆詣軍降。

translations.literal: The people of Huainan all came to the armies to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Huainan surrendered en masse.

sentences.zh: 高梁王那出山陽，永昌王仁於壽陽出橫江，凡所經過，莫不風靡。

translations.literal: The Prince of Gaoliang Na came out from Shanyang; the Prince of Yongchang Ren came out from Hengjiang at Shouyang; wherever they passed, none failed to be swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Na of Gaoliang marched from Shanyang; Prince Ren from Hengjiang at Shouyang; all before them collapsed.

sentences.zh: 車駕登於瓜步，伐葦結筏，示欲渡江。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage ascended Guabu, cut reeds and bound rafts, showing intent to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor climbed Guabu, built reed rafts, and feigned crossing the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 義隆大懼，欲走吳會。

translations.literal: Yilong was greatly afraid and wished to flee to Wu and Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Yilong planned to flee to the southeast.

sentences.zh: 建業士女咸荷擔而立。

translations.literal: The gentlemen and women of Jianye all stood with packs on carrying-poles.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jianye stood ready to flee with packs on their shoulders.

sentences.zh: 義隆遣黃延年朝於行宮，獻百牢，貢其方物，并請和，求進女於皇孫。

translations.literal: Yilong sent Huang Yannian to court at the traveling palace, presented a hundred oxen in sacrifice, offered local products, and sought peace, asking to send a daughter to the imperial grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong sent Huang Yannian to the camp with tribute and a peace offer, proposing a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 世祖以師婚非禮，許和而不許婚。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu held that marriage by force was not ritual propriety; he granted peace but not marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu deemed forced marriage improper; he accepted peace but refused the bride.

sentences.zh: 初，義隆欲遣軍侵境，其臣江湛、徐湛之贊成其事，而義隆太子劭與蕭思話、沈慶之謂義隆曰：「昔檀道濟、到彥之無利而反，今將帥士眾不及於前，不可輕動兵甲。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yilong wished to send armies to invade the borders, his ministers Jiang Zhan and Xu Chenzhi endorsed the affair, but Yilong's Heir Liu Shao with Xiao Sihua and Shen Qingzhi said to Yilong: "In the past Tan Daoji and Dao Yanzhi returned without profit; today's commanders and troops are inferior to those before—arms must not be lightly moved."
translations.idiomatic: When Yilong planned invasion, Jiang Zhan and Xu Chenzhi approved, but the heir Shao, Xiao Sihua, and Shen Qingzhi warned: "Tan Daoji and Dao Yanzhi returned empty-handed; today's forces are weaker—do not move rashly."

sentences.zh: 時湛等在坐，義隆使與慶之謀議。

translations.literal: Zhan and the others were present; Yilong had them deliberate with Qingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan and the others were present; Yilong had them debate with Qingzhi.

sentences.zh: 慶之曰：「治國如治家，耕當問奴，織當問婢，今欲伐國，而與白面書生輩謀之，事何由濟。」

translations.literal: Qingzhi said: "Governing a state is like running a household—plowing one should ask the slave, weaving one should ask the maid. Now you wish to conquer a state yet consult pale-faced bookish fellows—how can the affair succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi said: "Governing a state is like running a household—ask the farmer about plowing, the weaver about weaving. You plan war with pale scholars—how can it succeed?"

sentences.zh: 義隆大笑，遂不納慶之言。

translations.literal: Yilong laughed loudly and would not accept Qingzhi's words.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong laughed and ignored Qingzhi.

sentences.zh: 至是，登石頭城樓而望，甚有憂色，歎曰：「若檀道濟在，豈應至此！」

translations.literal: At this time he ascended the tower of Stone City and looked out, his face full of worry, and sighed: "If Tan Daoji were here, how could it have come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: He climbed Stone City tower, worried, and sighed: "If only Tan Daoji were alive!"

sentences.zh: 邵乃委罪於江、徐。

translations.literal: Shao then laid the blame on Jiang and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Shao blamed Jiang and Xu.

sentences.zh: 義隆曰：「此自吾意，不關二人也。」

translations.literal: Yilong said: "This was my own intent—it has nothing to do with those two."
translations.idiomatic: Yilong said: "This was my decision—not theirs."

sentences.zh: 正平元年正月，世祖饗會於瓜步，既許和好，詔班師。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Zhengping, Emperor Shizu held a feast at Guabu; peace having been granted, he ordered withdrawal of the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhengping, Emperor Shizu feasted at Guabu and ordered withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 其江北之民歸降者數十萬計。

translations.literal: Those north of the river who submitted numbered in the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of thousands north of the river submitted.

sentences.zh: 凡克南兗、豫、徐、兗、青、冀六州，其軍鋒殺掠不可勝算。

translations.literal: In all they took Southern Yan, Yu, Xu, Yan, Qing, and Ji—six provinces; the killing and plunder of their army's edge could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: They took six provinces; the slaughter and plunder were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 時義隆江北蕭條，境內搔擾。

translations.literal: At the time Yilong's north of the river was desolate and the realm within was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: The north was devastated and the realm in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 義隆慮義康為亂，遣使殺之，葬以侯禮。

translations.literal: Yilong feared Yikang would cause disorder, sent envoys to kill him, and buried him with marquis rites.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Yikang, Yilong had him killed and buried as a marquis.

sentences.zh: 義隆慚恚，歸罪於下，降義恭為儀同三司，蕭斌、王玄謨並免所居職。

translations.literal: Ashamed and enraged, Yilong blamed those below, demoted Yigong to the ceremonial rank of the Three Excellencies, and dismissed Xiao Bin and Wang Xuemo from their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Yilong blamed his generals, demoted Yigong, and dismissed Xiao Bin and Wang Xuemo.

sentences.zh: 十月，義隆遣其將軍孫蓋等朝貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Yilong sent his general Sun Gai and others on tribute missions to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Yilong sent Sun Gai with tribute.

sentences.zh: 興安元年，[17]義隆遣撫軍將軍蕭思話率其將張永等攻碻磝，詔諸軍擊破之，永等退走。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xing'an,[17] Yilong sent the Pacifying Army General Xiao Sihua leading his general Zhang Yong and others to attack Que'ao; an edict ordered the armies to defeat them, and Yong and others fled.
translations.idiomatic: In Xing'an,[17] Xiao Sihua and Zhang Yong attacked Que'ao; the Wei armies routed them.

sentences.zh: 思話遣建武將軍垣護之至梁山逆軍，尚書韓茂率騎逆擊之，思話退還麋溝。

translations.literal: Sihua sent the General Who Establishes Might Yuan Huzhi to Liang Mountain against the army; the Master of Writing Han Mao led cavalry to strike them; Sihua withdrew to Migou.
translations.idiomatic: Sihua sent Yuan Huzhi to Liang Mountain; Han Mao routed them; Sihua withdrew to Migou.

sentences.zh: 義隆又遣雍州刺史臧質向崤陝，梁州刺史劉秀之、輔國將軍楊文德出子午。

translations.literal: Yilong again sent the Inspector of Yong Zang Zhi toward Xiao-Shan, and the Inspectors of Liang Liu Xiuzhi and the General Who Assists the State Yang Wende out through Ziwu.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong sent Zang Zhi toward Xiao-Shan and Liu Xiuzhi and Yang Wende through Ziwu Pass.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史長孫蘭遣騎破之，秀之等僅以身免。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Yu Zhangsun Lan sent cavalry to defeat them; Xiuzhi and others barely escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Lan routed them; Xiuzhi barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 臧質、柳元景、薛安都等至關城，並相繼敗走。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi, Liu Yuanjing, Xue Andu, and others reached Guancheng and were defeated and fled one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, Yuanjing, and Andu reached Guancheng and were routed in turn.

sentences.zh: 是年，義隆太子劭及始興王休明令女巫嚴道育呪詛義隆，事發，義隆憤愧自失，廢於政事。

translations.literal: That year Yilong's Heir Shao and the Prince of Shixing Xiuming had the witch Yan Daoyu curse Yilong; when the affair was exposed, Yilong was angry, ashamed, and lost in himself, neglecting government.
translations.idiomatic: That year Shao and Prince Xiuming of Shixing had a witch curse Yilong; exposed, Yilong was devastated and neglected government.

sentences.zh: 乃議黜劭殺休明，屢召尚書僕射徐湛之、吏部尚書江湛、侍中王僧綽等謀議。

translations.literal: He then debated deposing Shao and killing Xiuming, repeatedly summoning the Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xu Chenzhi, the Minister of Personnel Jiang Zhan, the Palace Attendant Wang Sengchuo, and others for counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He debated deposing Shao and killing Xiuming, summoning Xu Chenzhi, Jiang Zhan, and Wang Sengchuo repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 僧綽曰：「當斷不斷，反受其亂，惟願以義割恩，略小不忍。

translations.literal: Sengchuo said: "When one should cut but does not, one suffers disorder in return—I only wish you would sever affection by righteousness and set aside petty reluctance.
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo said: "Hesitation breeds chaos—cut ties by duty, not petty tenderness.

sentences.zh: 不爾，便應坦懷如初，無煩疑論，不可使難生慮表，取笑千載。」

translations.literal: Otherwise you should be open-hearted as at first, without troubling deliberation—you must not let trouble arise from outward signs and become a laughingstock for a thousand years."
translations.idiomatic: Or be open as before—do not invite trouble and mockery for ages to come."

sentences.zh: 義隆曰：「卿可謂能斷大事，此不可不殷勤三思。

translations.literal: Yilong said: "You may be said capable of deciding great affairs—this cannot but be pondered thrice with care.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong said: "You speak boldly—but this demands careful thought.

sentences.zh: 義康始死，人謂我無復慈愛之道。」

translations.literal: When Yikang first died, people said I had no further path of loving kindness."
translations.idiomatic: When I killed Yikang, people said I had no mercy left."

sentences.zh: 僧綽又云：「臣恐千載之後，言陛下易於裁弟，難於廢子。」

translations.literal: Sengchuo again said: "I fear that a thousand years hence they will say Your Majesty found it easy to judge a younger brother but hard to depose a son."
translations.idiomatic: Sengchuo added: "Posterity will say you could kill a brother but not a son."

sentences.zh: 義隆默然。

translations.literal: Yilong was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong fell silent.

sentences.zh: 休明母潘有寵於義隆，義隆以廢立之謀告之。

translations.literal: Xiuming's mother Pan had Yilong's favor; Yilong told her the plot to depose and install.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuming's mother Pan was favored; Yilong told her the plot.

sentences.zh: 潘請赦，弗許，遂告休明。

translations.literal: Pan begged a pardon; he would not grant it, and she then told Xiuming.
translations.idiomatic: Pan begged mercy; refused, she told Xiuming.

sentences.zh: 休明馳報劭，劭知己當廢，遂夜召左右隊主陳叔兒、詹叔兒，[18]齋帥張超之、任建之等總二千餘人被甲自衞。

translations.literal: Xiuming galloped to inform Shao; Shao knew he was to be deposed and therefore at night summoned the left and right squad leaders Chen Shu'er and Zhan Shu'er,[18] the fast-day guards Zhang Chaozhi, Ren Jianzhi, and others—in all more than two thousand in armor for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuming warned Shao; knowing he would be deposed, Shao summoned Chen and Zhan Shu'er[18] and Zhang Chaozhi and more than two thousand armored men.

sentences.zh: 又召左衞率袁淑、中舍人殷仲素、左積弩將軍王正見，又呼左軍長史蕭斌。

translations.literal: He also summoned the Left Guard Leader Yuan Shu, the Palace Attendant of the Heir Yin Zhongsu, the Left Crossbow General Wang Zhengjian, and called the Left Army Chief Clerk Xiao Bin.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Yuan Shu, Yin Zhongsu, Wang Zhengjian, and Xiao Bin.

sentences.zh: 劭曰：「朝廷信讒，當見罪廢，內省無過，不能受枉，明當入殿，卿等必不得異。」

translations.literal: Shao said: "The court believes slander; I am to be condemned and deposed. Looking within, I am without fault and cannot accept injustice. Tomorrow I enter the hall—you must not differ."
translations.idiomatic: Shao said: "The court believes slander and will depose me. I am innocent and will not accept this. Tomorrow I enter the hall—you must follow."

sentences.zh: 乃遍拜告哀。

translations.literal: He then bowed to each in turn and declared his grief.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed to each in turn.

sentences.zh: 眾皆驚，不得答。

translations.literal: All were alarmed and could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: All were stunned into silence.

sentences.zh: 袁淑良久曰：「自古無此類，願加善思。」

translations.literal: Yuan Shu after long silence said: "From antiquity there has been nothing like this—I beg you to think well."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu said at last: "Nothing like this in history—think again."

sentences.zh: 劭怒變色，於左右咸云伏聽令旨。

translations.literal: Shao's face changed in anger; to those at his side he said all should prostrate and heed his command.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's face darkened; his men were told to obey.

sentences.zh: 明晨斬淑。

translations.literal: The next morning he beheaded Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning he killed Shu.

sentences.zh: 劭守萬春門，乃告門者曰：「我受敕入，有所收，可助我督後隊令速。」

translations.literal: Shao guarded Wanchun Gate and told the gatekeepers: "I have received an edict to enter and make arrests—help me urge the rear ranks to hurry."
translations.idiomatic: At Wanchun Gate Shao told the guards: "I have imperial orders—help hurry the rear ranks."

sentences.zh: 劭又詐義隆敕云：「魯秀謀反，汝明可守關，將兵入討也。」

translations.literal: Shao also forged an edict of Yilong: "Lu Xiu plots rebellion—you may hold the gate and lead troops in to punish."
translations.idiomatic: He forged an edict: "Lu Xiu rebels—hold the gate and march in to punish him."

sentences.zh: 故士卒信之。

translations.literal: Therefore the soldiers believed him.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers believed him.

sentences.zh: 超之等率十餘人走入雲龍門，拔刃徑登含章殿。

translations.literal: Chaozhi and others led more than ten men into the Cloud Dragon Gate, drew blades, and went straight up to Hanzhang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozhi and a dozen men entered the Cloud Dragon Gate and rushed to Hanzhang Hall with drawn swords.

sentences.zh: 義隆夜與徐湛之屏人閑語，時猶未訖，門戶並無侍衞。

translations.literal: Yilong at night was in private talk with Xu Chenzhi, attendants dismissed; it was not yet finished, and at gate and door there were no guards.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong was speaking privately with Xu Chenzhi at night; no guards stood at the doors.

sentences.zh: 義隆迫急，以几自鄣，兵刃交下，五指俱落。

translations.literal: Yilong in extremity used a couch to shield himself; blades fell together and all five fingers were severed.
translations.idiomatic: Yilong shielded himself with a couch; blades struck and severed all five fingers.

sentences.zh: 超之斬義隆，徐湛之為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: Chaozhi beheaded Yilong; Xu Chenzhi was killed by the disorderly troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozhi killed Yilong; Xu Chenzhi died in the melee.

sentences.zh: 劭分遣掩江湛之，斬之。

translations.literal: Shao sent parties separately to seize Jiang Zhan and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent men to seize and kill Jiang Zhan.

sentences.zh: 休明時在西州，來屯中堂。

translations.literal: Xiuming was then in the Western Quarter and came to encamp in the Central Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuming was in the Western Quarter and marched to the Central Hall.

sentences.zh: 劭又使兵殺休明母。

translations.literal: Shao also sent troops to kill Xiuming's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Shao had Xiuming's mother killed.

sentences.zh: 是日，劭登殿受璽綬，下書曰：「徐湛之、江湛殺逆無狀，吾勒兵入殿，已無所及，號惋崩衂，心肝破裂。

translations.literal: That day Shao ascended the hall, received the seal and cord, and issued a document: "Xu Chenzhi and Jiang Zhan murdered the rebel without propriety; I led troops into the hall but could not reach them in time—I wail and my heart bursts, liver and lungs split.
translations.idiomatic: That day Shao took the throne and issued an edict: "Xu and Jiang murdered the emperor; I marched too late—my heart is broken.

sentences.zh: 今罪人斯得，元凶克殄，卜世靈祚，永享無窮，思與億兆覃茲更始，可大赦天下，改元嘉三十年為太初元年。」

translations.literal: Now the guilty are obtained, the chief culprit destroyed—the oracle of the age, spiritual blessing, enjoyed without end. Thinking to share renewal with the hundred millions, a great amnesty is proclaimed for all under heaven; the thirtieth year of Yuanjia is changed to the first year of Taichu."
translations.idiomatic: The villains are punished, the realm secured. Let all under heaven be renewed—proclaim amnesty and change the thirtieth year of Yuanjia to the first year of Taichu."

sentences.zh: 劭弟駿，時為江州刺史。

translations.literal: Shao’s younger brother Jun was then Inspector of Jiang province.
translations.idiomatic: Shao’s younger brother Jun was then Inspector of Jiang province.

sentences.zh: 先以西陽蠻反，義隆令東宮步兵校尉沈慶之、襄陽太守柳元景、司空中兵參軍宗慤並討之。

translations.literal: Earlier, because the Man of Xiyang had rebelled, Yilong had ordered Shen Qingzhi, Infantry Commandant of the Eastern Palace; Liu Yuanjing, Governor of Xiangyang; and Zong Que, Consulting Officer of the Minister of Works’ Central Troops, all to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because the Man of Xiyang had rebelled, Yilong had ordered Shen Qingzhi, Infantry Commandant of the Eastern Palace; Liu Yuanjing, Governor of Xiangyang; and Zong Que, Consulting Officer of the Minister of Works’ Central Troops, all to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 駿出次五洲，斬劭使於軍門。

translations.literal: Jun went out and halted at Wuzhou, where he beheaded Shao’s envoy at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: Jun went out and halted at Wuzhou, where he beheaded Shao’s envoy at the army gate.

sentences.zh: 司徒義宣、雍州刺史臧質、司州刺史魯爽同舉兵。

translations.literal: Situ Yixuan, Zang Zhi, Inspector of Yong province, and Lu Shuang, Inspector of Si province, raised troops together.
translations.idiomatic: Situ Yixuan, Zang Zhi, Inspector of Yong province, and Lu Shuang, Inspector of Si province, raised troops together.

sentences.zh: 駿以沈慶之、柳元景、宗慤為前軍。

translations.literal: Jun made Shen Qingzhi, Liu Yuanjing, and Zong Que the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Jun made Shen Qingzhi, Liu Yuanjing, and Zong Que the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 駿諮議參軍顏竣專主軍謀。

translations.literal: Jun’s Consulting Officer Yan Jun was put solely in charge of military planning.
translations.idiomatic: Jun’s Consulting Officer Yan Jun was put solely in charge of military planning.

sentences.zh: 劭葬義隆，託疾不出。

translations.literal: When Shao buried Yilong, he claimed illness and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao buried Yilong, he claimed illness and did not go out.

sentences.zh: 臧質子敦逃走，劭乃悉聚諸王及大臣徙入城內，移南岸百姓渡淮，貴賤皆被驅逼，建業淆亂。

translations.literal: When Zang Zhi’s son Dun fled, Shao gathered all the princes and great ministers and moved them inside the city, shifted the people of the south bank across the Huai, and drove nobles and commoners alike under compulsion, throwing Jianye into confusion.
translations.idiomatic: When Zang Zhi’s son Dun fled, Shao gathered all the princes and great ministers and moved them inside the city, shifted the people of the south bank across the Huai, and drove nobles and commoners alike under compulsion, throwing Jianye into confusion.

sentences.zh: 駿等發尋陽，檄至，劭乃移駿數子於侍中省，義宣諸男於大倉屋，以兵守之；

translations.literal: Jun and the others set out from Xunyang. When their proclamation arrived, Shao moved several of Jun’s sons to the Attendant-in-Ordinary office and Yixuan’s sons to the Great Granary building, guarding them with soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: Jun and the others set out from Xunyang. When their proclamation arrived, Shao moved several of Jun’s sons to the Attendant-in-Ordinary office and Yixuan’s sons to the Great Granary building, guarding them with soldiers;

sentences.zh: 使其將魯秀、王羅漢等為水陸之備，休明及蕭斌為之謀主；

translations.literal: he had his generals Lu Xiu, Wang Luohan, and others make preparations by water and land, while Xiuming and Xiao Bin served as his chief planners;
translations.idiomatic: he had his generals Lu Xiu, Wang Luohan, and others make preparations by water and land, while Xiuming and Xiao Bin served as his chief planners;

sentences.zh: 焚除淮中船舫。

translations.literal: and he burned and cleared away the boats in the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: and he burned and cleared away the boats in the Huai.

sentences.zh: 駿至南洲，頓漂洲，令柳元景等擊劭，劭眾崩潰，奔走還宮。

translations.literal: Jun reached Nanzhou and halted at Piaozhou. He ordered Liu Yuanjing and the others to attack Shao; Shao’s forces collapsed, and he fled back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jun reached Nanzhou and halted at Piaozhou. He ordered Liu Yuanjing and the others to attack Shao; Shao’s forces collapsed, and he fled back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 義恭單馬奔駿，勸即位。

translations.literal: Yigong rode alone to Jun and urged him to take the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong rode alone to Jun and urged him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 劭大怒，遣休明就西省殺義恭子南豐王朗等十二人。

translations.literal: Shao was furious and sent Xiuming to the western offices to kill Yigong’s son Lang, Prince of Nanfeng, and twelve others.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was furious and sent Xiuming to the western offices to kill Yigong’s son Lang, Prince of Nanfeng, and twelve others.

sentences.zh: 駿乃僭即大位于新亭。

translations.literal: Jun thereupon usurped the great throne at Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: Jun seized the throne at Xinting.

sentences.zh: 於是擒劭、休明，並梟首大桁，暴屍於市，經日壞爛，投之水中，男女妃妾一皆從戮。

translations.literal: Thereupon they seized Shao and Xiuming, both displayed heads on the great gibbet, exposed corpses in the market; after a day they rotted and were cast into the water; men and women, consorts and concubines—all were executed with them.
translations.idiomatic: They captured Shao and Xiuming, displayed their heads, exposed their corpses in the market, then cast them in the water; wives and concubines were executed with them.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「遙望建康城，小江逆流縈，前見子殺父，後見弟殺兄。」

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying: "Gazing at Jianye city, the little river winds countercurrent—first one sees a son kill his father, then a younger brother kill his elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: A popular rhyme ran: "Gazing at Jianye—the little river runs backward; first a son kills his father, then a brother kills his brother."

sentences.zh: 興光元年，駿改年曰孝建。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingguang, Jun changed the era name to Xiaojian.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingguang, Jun changed the era to Xiaojian.

sentences.zh: 其中軍府錄事參軍周朗啟駿曰：[20]「今士大夫父母在而兄弟異計，十家而七；

translations.literal: His Central Army headquarters Recording Officer Zhou Lang memorialized Jun:[20] "Today among gentry and officials, while parents live brothers keep separate accounts—seven in ten households;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Lang memorialized Jun:[20] "Among officials today, seven in ten households divide property while parents still live;

sentences.zh: 庶人父子殊產，八家而五。

translations.literal: among commoners fathers and sons hold separate estates—five in eight households.
translations.idiomatic: among commoners, five in eight divide estates between father and son.

sentences.zh: 凡甚者乃危亡不相知，飢寒不相恤，又疾讒害其間，[21]不可稱數。

translations.literal: In the worst cases they do not know one another in peril and death, do not pity one another in hunger and cold, and slander and harm run between them[21] beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: At worst they ignore one another in danger and cold, and slander runs rife[21] beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 宜明其禁，以易其風。」

translations.literal: The prohibitions should be made clear to change this custom.
translations.idiomatic: Prohibitions should be enforced to change these ways.

sentences.zh: 俗弊如此，駿不能革。

translations.literal: Customs were so corrupt, yet Jun could not reform them.
translations.idiomatic: Customs were so corrupt, but Jun could not reform them.

sentences.zh: 臧質遣使說荊州刺史南郡王義宣曰：「有大才，負大功，挾震主威，自古尠有全者。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi sent an envoy to persuade the Inspector of Jing, the Prince of Nan Commandery Yixuan: "With great talent, bearing great merit, holding a lord who trembles—since antiquity few have ended whole.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Zhi urged Prince Yixuan of Nan Commandery: "Great talent and merit that terrify the throne—few in history survive intact.

sentences.zh: 宜在人前，早有處分。」

translations.literal: One should act before others and dispose early."
translations.idiomatic: Act before others, while you still can."

sentences.zh: 義宣使要豫州刺史魯爽、兗州刺史徐遺寶、司州刺史魯秀等，剋秋起兵。

translations.literal: Yixuan had the Inspectors of Yu Lu Shuang, Yan Xu Yibao, and Si Lu Xiu and others summoned, to raise troops by autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan summoned Lu Shuang, Xu Yibao, and Lu Xiu to rise by autumn.

sentences.zh: 爽時昏醉，即日便戴黃標，稱建平元年，板義宣為天子，遣信至建業迎弟瑜。

translations.literal: Shuang was then drunk and dazed; that very day he donned the yellow badge, proclaimed the first year of Jianping, appointed Yixuan Son of Heaven by commission, and sent a messenger to Jianye to welcome his younger brother Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang, drunk, proclaimed Jianping, named Yixuan emperor, and sent for his brother Yu at Jianye.

sentences.zh: 由是駿知爽反，惶懼，欲遣迎義宣，其竟陵王誕執議不許，乃遣左衞將軍王玄謨率眾討爽，領軍將軍柳元景、鎮軍將軍沈慶之討義宣。

translations.literal: Thereby Jun knew Shuang had rebelled, was fearful, and wished to send to welcome Yixuan; his Prince of Jingling Dan held to his view and would not permit it. He then sent the Left Guard General Wang Xuemo with troops against Shuang, and the Army Commander Liu Yuanjing and Pacifying Army General Shen Qingzhi against Yixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jun learned of the rebellion, panicked, and wanted to welcome Yixuan; Prince Dan dissuaded him. He sent Wang Xuemo against Shuang and Yuanjing and Qingzhi against Yixuan.

sentences.zh: 臧質下戍大雷，馳報義宣，抗表以誅元景為名。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi went down to garrison Dalei, galloped to inform Yixuan, and submitted a memorial in defiance under the name of punishing Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi garrisoned Dalei, warned Yixuan, and submitted a memorial to punish Yuanjing.

sentences.zh: 遣軍就質，使爽與質會于江上。

translations.literal: He sent troops to join Zhi[22] and had Shuang meet Zhi on the river.
translations.idiomatic: He sent troops to Zhi[22] and ordered Shuang to join him on the river.

sentences.zh: 玄謨屯兵梁山。

translations.literal: Xuemo encamped his troops at Liang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Xuemo camped at Liang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 義宣率眾至尋陽，與質俱下。

translations.literal: Yixuan led his host to Xunyang and descended together with Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan marched to Xunyang and descended with Zhi.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史朱脩之不從義宣。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Yong Zhu Xiuzhi did not follow Yixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xiuzhi, Inspector of Yong, refused to join Yixuan.

sentences.zh: 臧質進計曰：「今萬人取南州，則梁山中絕；

translations.literal: Zang Zhi advanced a plan: "If ten thousand men take the southern province, Liang Mountain will be cut off in the middle;
translations.idiomatic: Zhi proposed: "Send ten thousand to seize the south and cut Liang Mountain in two;

sentences.zh: 萬人守梁山，玄謨必不敢動。

translations.literal: ten thousand hold Liang Mountain, and Xuemo will certainly not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: ten thousand to hold Liang Mountain, and Xuemo will not dare move.

sentences.zh: 下官浮舟外江，直向石頭，此上策也。」

translations.literal: This humble servant floats boats on the outer river straight to Stone City—this is the supreme stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: I will sail the outer river straight to Stone City—that is the best plan."

sentences.zh: 義宣將從之，其諮議劉諶之曰：「質不求前驅，[23]凶志難測，不如盡銳攻梁山，事克，然後長驅，萬安之計也。」

translations.literal: Yixuan was about to follow it; his Consultant Liu Chenzhi said: "Zhi does not ask to lead the vanguard[23]—his fierce intent is hard to fathom. Better to concentrate all elite forces on Liang Mountain; once that is taken, then drive forward—that is the plan of ten thousand safeties."
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan nearly agreed; Liu Chenzhi said: "Zhi won't take the vanguard[23]—his intent is suspect. Strike Liang Mountain with full force first—that is the safe course."

sentences.zh: 義宣乃止。

translations.literal: Yixuan then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan held back.

sentences.zh: 義宣遣劉諶之就質，步攻東壘。

translations.literal: Yixuan sent Liu Chenzhi to join Zhi and attack the eastern rampart on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan sent Chenzhi to Zhi to attack the eastern rampart.

sentences.zh: 義宣進自蕪湖，赴梁山，屯兵西岸。

translations.literal: Yixuan advanced from Wuhu toward Liang Mountain and encamped on the west bank.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan advanced from Wuhu to Liang Mountain and camped on the west bank.

sentences.zh: 玄謨拒質，駿將軍垣護之、薛安都又摧破之。

translations.literal: Xuemo resisted Zhi; Jun's generals Yuan Huzhi[24] and Xue Andu again crushed them.
translations.idiomatic: Xuemo held against Zhi; Yuan Huzhi[24] and Xue Andu routed them again.

sentences.zh: 義宣眾潰，因風放火，焚其舟艦。

translations.literal: Yixuan's host collapsed; they set fire with the wind and burned their ships.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan's army collapsed; they burned their fleet with the wind.

sentences.zh: 義宣閉船大泣，因而迸逸。

translations.literal: Yixuan shut his boats and wept greatly, then burst away in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan shut his ships and wept, then fled.

sentences.zh: 走至江陵，荊州司馬竺超民具儀服迎之，左右相率潰叛，超民送付刺姦。

translations.literal: He fled to Jiangling; the Jing province Marshal Zhu Chaomin prepared ritual garments to welcome him, but attendants fled and rebelled in succession; Chaomin delivered him to the executioners.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangling Zhu Chaomin welcomed him in state dress, but his men deserted; Chaomin handed him to the executioners.

sentences.zh: 朱脩之於獄殺之。

translations.literal: Zhu Xiuzhi killed him in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xiuzhi killed him in prison.

sentences.zh: 太安二年，駿改年為大明。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tai'an, Jun changed the era name to Daming.
translations.idiomatic: In Tai'an year two Jun changed the era to Daming.

sentences.zh: 駿於新亭造中興佛寺，設齋，忽有一僧形貌有異，眾皆愕然。

translations.literal: At Xinting Jun built the Zhongxing Buddhist temple and held a fast; suddenly a monk of strange appearance appeared and all were startled.
translations.idiomatic: At Xinting Jun built Zhongxing Temple; a monk of strange aspect appeared and all were startled.

sentences.zh: 問其名，答云名惠明，從天安寺來。

translations.literal: Asked his name, he answered Huiming, from Tian'an Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Asked his name, he said Huiming, from Tian'an Temple.

sentences.zh: 言竟，倐然而滅，乃改為天安寺。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking he vanished suddenly, and the temple was renamed Tian'an.
translations.idiomatic: He vanished; the temple was renamed Tian'an.

sentences.zh: 至天安初而彭城歸國。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Tian'an Pengcheng returned to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: By Tian'an Pengcheng had returned to Wei.

sentences.zh: 四年，駿遣其將殷孝祖寇濟州，高宗遣清水公封敕文等擊走之，又詔征西將軍皮豹子擊孝祖於清東。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Jun sent his general Yin Xiaozu to raid Jizhou; Emperor Gaozong sent the Duke of Clear Water Feng Wenwen and others to drive him off, and ordered the General Who Campaigns West Pi Baozi to strike Xiaozu east of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: In year four Yin Xiaozu raided Jizhou; Feng Wenwen drove him off and Pi Baozi struck him east of Qing.

sentences.zh: 五年，豹子還，遂掠地至高平，大獲而還。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Baozi returned and raided as far as Gaoping, taking a great haul before returning.
translations.idiomatic: In year five Baozi raided to Gaoping and returned with great booty.

sentences.zh: 駿以其南兗州刺史竟陵王誕得士庶之心，內畏忌之。

translations.literal: Jun feared his Inspector of Southern Yan, the Prince of Jingling Dan, who had won the hearts of gentry and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Jun feared Prince Dan of Jingling, Inspector of Southern Yan, who had won popular loyalty.

sentences.zh: 誕不自安，乃治城多聚糧仗。

translations.literal: Dan was ill at ease and fortified his city, gathering much grain and arms.
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy, Dan fortified his city and stockpiled grain and arms.

sentences.zh: 駿大怒，貶誕爵為侯，遣兗州刺史垣閬、給事中戴明寶討之。

translations.literal: Jun in great anger demoted Dan to marquis and sent the Inspector of Yan Yuan Lang and the Palace Attendant Dai Mingbao against him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun demoted Dan to marquis and sent Yuan Lang and Dai Mingbao against him.

sentences.zh: 誕遣眾出戰，斬垣閬。

translations.literal: Dan sent troops out to fight and beheaded Yuan Lang.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's troops killed Yuan Lang.

sentences.zh: 誕表駿曰：「往年元凶禍逆，陛下入討，臣背凶赴順，可謂常節。

translations.literal: Dan memorialized Jun: "In former years when the chief culprit rebelled, Your Majesty entered to punish him; I turned from the wicked to the loyal—this may be called constant conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Dan wrote to Jun: "When the usurper rebelled I sided with you—that was loyalty.

sentences.zh: 及丞相構難，臧魯協從，朝野怳忽，咸懷憂懼。

translations.literal: When the Chancellor stirred trouble and Zang and Lu joined him, court and countryside were dazed and all bore worry and fear.
translations.idiomatic: When the chancellor rebelled and Zang and Lu joined, all were afraid.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲建百官羽儀星馳推奉，臣前後固執，末方賜從。

translations.literal: Your Majesty wished to install the hundred officials and imperial regalia and urged me to accept; I firmly refused again and again before consent was granted.
translations.idiomatic: You urged me to accept the throne; I refused until I could refuse no more.

sentences.zh: 社稷獲全，是誰之力？

translations.literal: Who preserved the altars of state—whose merit was it?
translations.idiomatic: Who saved the realm—was it not mine?

sentences.zh: 陛下接遇殷勤，屢加崇寵，驃騎、揚州，旬月移授。

translations.literal: Your Majesty received me with earnest kindness, repeatedly raising my rank—Rapid Cavalry, Yang—transferred within a month.
translations.idiomatic: You heaped honors on me—Rapid Cavalry, Yang—in a month.

sentences.zh: 恩秩頻煩，復賜徐兗，仰屈皇輿，遠相餞送。

translations.literal: Favor and rank came in succession; Xu and Yan were granted again; bending the imperial carriage, you sent me off from afar.
translations.idiomatic: You gave me Xu and Yan and saw me off in person.

sentences.zh: 臣一遇之感，此何以忘，庶希偕老，永相娛慰。

translations.literal: Once touched by such feeling, how could I forget? I hoped we would grow old together in mutual joy.
translations.idiomatic: I hoped we would grow old together in peace.

sentences.zh: 豈謂陛下信用讒言，遂令小人來相掩襲。

translations.literal: Who expected Your Majesty to trust slander and send petty men to attack me by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you believed slander and sent men to attack me.

sentences.zh: 不任枉酷，即加誅揃，雀鼠貪生，仰違詔敕。

translations.literal: Unable to bear wrongful cruelty about to be executed, sparrow and mouse cling to life—I disobey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot accept unjust execution—I disobey.

sentences.zh: 今親勒部曲，鎮扞徐兗。

translations.literal: Now I personally lead my troops to guard Xu and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: I now lead my troops to defend Xu and Yan.

sentences.zh: 昔緣何福，同生皇家；

translations.literal: By what fortune were we born of the same house?
translations.idiomatic: What fortune that we share royal blood?

sentences.zh: 今有何罪，便成胡越。

translations.literal: What crime have I now, to become barbarian and Chinese to each other?
translations.idiomatic: What crime makes us strangers?

sentences.zh: 陵鋒奮戈，萬沒豈顧，定蕩之期，冀在旦夕。

translations.literal: With spears raised and blades drawn, ten thousand deaths I do not regard; the day of pacification I hope is near at hand.
translations.idiomatic: I will fight to the death; victory will come soon.

sentences.zh: 右軍、宣簡，爰及武昌，皆以無罪，並遇枉酷。

translations.literal: The Right Army, Xuanjian, and Wuchang—all without crime yet met wrongful cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: The Right Army and Wuchang were killed though innocent.

sentences.zh: 臣有何過，復致於此？

translations.literal: What fault have I that I meet this again?
translations.idiomatic: What fault brings this upon me?

sentences.zh: 陛下宮闈之醜，豈可一二。

translations.literal: The scandals of Your Majesty's inner quarters—can they be counted on one or two hands?
translations.idiomatic: Your palace scandals are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 臨紙悲塞，不止所言。」

translations.literal: Facing the paper my grief chokes me; I cannot say all I mean.
translations.idiomatic: My grief chokes me beyond words.

sentences.zh: 駿以沈慶之前軍討之，親勞軍人，賜以金帛。

translations.literal: Jun sent Shen Qingzhi as vanguard against him, personally encouraging the soldiers and bestowing gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent Shen Qingzhi and personally encouraged the troops with gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 慶之軍敗退，傷者十四五。

translations.literal: Qingzhi's army was defeated and withdrew; fourteen or fifteen in ten were wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Qingzhi was defeated; most of his men were wounded.

sentences.zh: 駿大怒，將自往。

translations.literal: Jun in great anger was about to go himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jun in fury meant to march himself.

sentences.zh: 久乃拔之，斬誕傳首。

translations.literal: After long siege he took it, beheaded Dan, and sent the head.
translations.idiomatic: After a long siege he took the city, killed Dan, and sent his head.

sentences.zh: 誕母殷、妻徐並自殺。

translations.literal: Dan's mother Yin and wife Xu both killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's mother Yin and wife Xu killed themselves.

sentences.zh: 城內誅者數千人，或先鞭殺而行戮。

translations.literal: Several thousand within the city were executed; some were flogged to death before execution.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands in the city were killed; some were flogged first.

sentences.zh: 並移首於石頭南岸，以為京觀，至於風晨雨夜，輒聞哀號之響。

translations.literal: The heads were moved to the south bank of Stone City as a war monument; on windy mornings and rainy nights one could hear sounds of lament.
translations.idiomatic: Heads were heaped on the south bank of Stone City; on stormy nights laments were heard.

sentences.zh: 駿淫亂無度，蒸其母路氏，穢汙之聲，布於甌越。

translations.literal: Jun was licentious beyond measure, violating his mother Lady Lu; the sound of filth spread through Ou and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Jun violated his mother Lady Lu; the scandal spread widely.

sentences.zh: 東揚州刺史顏竣恃舊，每戲弄之，駿慚怒殺竣。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Eastern Yang Yan Jun relied on old ties and often mocked him; Jun in shame and anger killed Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun mocked him; Jun killed him in shame and rage.

sentences.zh: 和平元年七月，駿使其散騎常侍明僧暠朝貢。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Heping, Jun sent his Regular Gentleman Attendant Ming Sengao on tribute missions to court.
translations.idiomatic: In Heping year one Jun sent Ming Sengao with tribute.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，又使其散騎常侍尹顯朝貢。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year he again sent his Regular Gentleman Attendant Yin Xian on tribute missions to court.
translations.idiomatic: In year two he sent Yin Xian with tribute.

sentences.zh: 駿雍州刺史、海陵王休茂謀將除駿，參軍尹玄慶斬休茂。

translations.literal: Jun's Inspector of Yong, the Prince of Hailing Xiumao, plotted to remove Jun; his staff officer Yin Xuanqing beheaded Xiumao.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiumao of Hailing plotted against Jun; Yin Xuanqing killed him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，凡諸郡士族婚官點雜者，悉黜為將吏，而人情驚怨，並不服役，逃竄山湖，聚為寇盜。

translations.literal: That year, wherever gentry marriages had mixed official ranks, all were demoted to soldiers and clerks; people were alarmed and resentful, refused service, and fled to mountains and lakes as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry of mixed rank were demoted to soldiers; many fled and became bandits.

sentences.zh: 侍中沈懷文苦諫不納。

translations.literal: The Palace Attendant Shen Huaiwen remonstrated bitterly but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaiwen remonstrated in vain.

sentences.zh: 三年三月，駿使其散騎常侍嚴靈護朝貢。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year Jun sent his Regular Gentleman Attendant Yan Linghu on tribute missions to court.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he sent Yan Linghu with tribute.

sentences.zh: 以沈懷文數直諫，付廷尉殺之。

translations.literal: Because Shen Huaiwen repeatedly spoke straight, he was handed to the Minister of Justice and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huaiwen was executed for his remonstrances.

sentences.zh: 駿寵姬殷死，贈貴妃，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: When Jun's favored concubine Yin died, she was posthumously made Noble Consort with the posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: When concubine Yin died Jun made her Noble Consort Xuan.

sentences.zh: 及葬龍山，給鑾輅、九旒、黃屋、左纛、羽葆、鼓吹、班劍、虎賁。

translations.literal: At burial on Dragon Mountain he gave imperial carriage, nine tassels, yellow canopy, left streamer, feathered banners, drums and pipes, ceremonial guards, and tiger guards.
translations.idiomatic: Her funeral on Dragon Mountain had imperial honors.

sentences.zh: 龍轜之麗，功妙萬端，山池雲鳳之屬，皆裝以眾寶，繡帷珠帶，重鈴疊眊，儀服之盛，古今尠有。

translations.literal: The splendor of the dragon hearse was wondrous beyond measure; mountain pools and cloud phoenixes were adorned with many jewels; embroidered curtains and pearl cords, layered bells and veils—the grandeur of ritual dress had scarcely been seen in antiquity or the present.
translations.idiomatic: The funeral regalia exceeded anything seen before.

sentences.zh: 駿自殷死，常懷悲惻，神情罔罔，廢棄政事。

translations.literal: From Yin's death Jun constantly bore grief, his spirit vacant, neglecting government.
translations.idiomatic: After Yin's death Jun neglected government in grief.

sentences.zh: 或親至殷靈牀，酌奠酒飲之，既而慟哭流連，不能自反。

translations.literal: Sometimes he went in person to Yin's spirit couch, poured libation and drank, then wailed and lingered, unable to return.
translations.idiomatic: He drank at her spirit couch and could not leave.

sentences.zh: 其耽昏若此。

translations.literal: His addiction to delusion was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his obsession.

sentences.zh: 四年，獵于烏江之榜口，又游湖縣之滿山，[25]並與母同行，宣淫肆意。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he hunted at Bangkou on the Wu River and toured Manshan in Huxian,[25] going with his mother together, indulging lust at will.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he hunted at Bangkou and Manshan[25] with his mother, indulging lust.

sentences.zh: 五年，三吳大飢，人食草木皮葉，親屬互相販鬻，劫掠蜂起，死者不可勝數。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the three Wu regions suffered great famine; people ate bark and leaves; kin sold one another; plunder swarmed; the dead were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In year five the three Wu starved; kin sold each other; the dead were countless.

sentences.zh: 是年駿死。

translations.literal: That year Jun died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Jun died.

sentences.zh: 子子業立，性尤凶悖。

translations.literal: His son Ziye succeeded, nature especially fierce and perverse.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ziye succeeded, vicious by nature.

sentences.zh: 其母疾篤，遣呼子業，子業曰：「病人間多鬼，那可往？」

translations.literal: When his mother was gravely ill she sent for Ziye; Ziye said: "The sickroom has many ghosts—how can I go?"
translations.idiomatic: His dying mother summoned him; he refused: "The sickroom is full of ghosts."

sentences.zh: 其母怒，語侍者曰：「將刀來破我腹，那得生如馨兒！」

translations.literal: His mother in anger told attendants: "Bring a knife to split my belly—how could I have borne a son like this!"
translations.idiomatic: His mother cried: "I should have cut him from my womb!"

sentences.zh: 六年，改為永光。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he changed the era to Yongguang.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he changed the era to Yongguang.

sentences.zh: 以奄人華願兒為散騎常侍，遊止必同。

translations.literal: He made the eunuch Hua Yuan'er Regular Gentleman Attendant; wherever they went they were always together.
translations.idiomatic: He made the eunuch Hua Yuan'er his constant companion.

sentences.zh: 越騎校尉戴法興屢相裁割，願兒深以為隙。

translations.literal: The Colonel of the Rapid Cavalry Dai Faxing often restrained him; Yuan'er deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Faxing restrained him; Yuan'er resented him.

sentences.zh: 或謂法興為真天子，子業為贋天子，願兒具以聞，子業乃殺法興。

translations.literal: Some said Faxing was the true Son of Heaven and Ziye the false; Yuan'er reported this fully, and Ziye killed Faxing.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Faxing was the "true emperor," Ziye killed him.

sentences.zh: 驃騎將軍柳元景、尚書左僕射顏師伯欲廢子業，立太宰義恭，以告沈慶之，慶之告子業。

translations.literal: The Rapid Cavalry General Liu Yuanjing and Left Vice Director Yan Shibo wished to depose Ziye and install the Grand Tutor Yigong; they told Shen Qingzhi, who informed Ziye.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing and Shibo plotted to depose Ziye; Qingzhi betrayed them.

sentences.zh: 子業出兵誅義恭，遂刳剔支體，抽裂心藏，挑其眼睛，投之蜜中，謂之鬼目粽。

translations.literal: Ziye sent troops to execute Yigong, then flayed and dismembered him, tore out his heart, scooped his eyes, and threw them in honey, calling them ghost-eye dumplings.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye had Yigong dismembered and made "ghost-eye dumplings" of his eyes in honey.

sentences.zh: 又殺柳元景、顏師伯，並諸子及弟姪。

translations.literal: He also killed Liu Yuanjing and Yan Shibo along with their sons and younger brothers and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: He killed Yuanjing, Shibo, and their kin.

sentences.zh: 乃改年為景和。

translations.literal: He then changed the era to Jinghe.
translations.idiomatic: He changed the era to Jinghe.

sentences.zh: 子業除去喪禮，服錦縠之衣。

translations.literal: Ziye abolished mourning rites and wore brocade and gauze.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye abandoned mourning and wore silks.

sentences.zh: 以石頭城為長樂宮，東城為未央宮，北邸為建章宮，南宅為長楊宮。

translations.literal: He made Stone City the Everjoy Palace, the eastern city the Weiyang Palace, the northern residence the Jianzhang Palace, the southern residence the Changyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He renamed palaces after Han models.

sentences.zh: 子業自以昔在東宮，不為駿所愛，及即位，常欲毀其墓。

translations.literal: Ziye felt that in the Eastern Palace he had not been loved by Jun; once enthroned he often wished to destroy Jun's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye hated Jun and wished to destroy his tomb.

sentences.zh: 乃遣發駿所寵殷氏冢。

translations.literal: He sent men to open the tomb of Yin, whom Jun had favored.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the tomb of Jun's favorite Yin.

sentences.zh: 殷死，駿為之造新安寺，於是壞之，復欲誅諸遠近尼僧。

translations.literal: When Yin died Jun had built Xin'an Temple for her; he now destroyed it and wished to execute nuns far and near.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed Xin'an Temple and meant to kill the nuns.

sentences.zh: 遣使殺其新安王子鸞，臨死歎曰：「惟願後身不復生天王家！」

translations.literal: He sent envoys to kill his Prince of Xin'an Ziluan; at death Ziluan sighed: "I only wish in the next life not to be born in a king's house again!"
translations.idiomatic: He killed Prince Ziluan of Xin'an, who wished never to be born royal again.

sentences.zh: 義恭既誅，徐州刺史義陽王昶大懼，遣典籤蘧法生啟求還建業。

translations.literal: After Yigong was killed, the Inspector of Xu Prince Yichang of Yiyang was greatly afraid and sent his Registrar Qu Fasheng to beg return to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yichang of Yiyang, afraid, asked to return to court.

sentences.zh: 子業謂法生曰：「義陽謀反，我正欲誅之。」

translations.literal: Ziye told Fasheng: "Yiyang is rebelling; I mean to execute him."
translations.idiomatic: Ziye said: "Yiyang rebels; I will kill him."

sentences.zh: 法生懼禍，走還彭城。

translations.literal: Fasheng feared disaster and fled back to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fasheng fled to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 子業遣沈慶之率師伐昶。

translations.literal: Ziye sent Shen Qingzhi with troops to campaign against Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye sent Shen Qingzhi against Yichang.

sentences.zh: 法生至彭城，昶便繕甲，諸郡不從，昶知事不捷，遂來奔。

translations.literal: Fasheng reached Pengcheng; Yichang armed his men; the commanderies would not follow; knowing affairs would not succeed, he came to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Yichang armed but his provinces would not follow; he fled.

sentences.zh: 子業淫其姑，稱為謝氏，為貴嬪、夫人，加以殊禮，虎賁劍戟，出警入蹕，鑾輅龍旂，在貴妃之上，即義隆第十女，其新蔡長公主也。

translations.literal: Ziye violated his aunt, calling her Lady Xie, made her Noble Consort and Lady, with special rites—tiger guards and halberds, escort in and out, imperial carriage and dragon banners above the Noble Consort—she was Yilong's tenth daughter, the Princess of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye took his aunt, Yilong's daughter, as consort with imperial honors.

sentences.zh: 子業矯云主喪，空設喪事，而實納之。

translations.literal: Ziye falsely announced her lord's mourning, set empty rites, but in fact took her in.
translations.idiomatic: He staged a funeral but kept her.

sentences.zh: 時其姊山陰主大見愛狎，淫恣過度，謂子業曰：「妾與陛下男女雖殊，俱託體先帝，陛下六宮百數，而妾惟一駙馬，事不均平，乃可如此。」

translations.literal: Then his elder sister the Princess of Shanyin, greatly favored and indulged in lust, said to Ziye: "Though you and I differ in sex, we both spring from the late emperor. Your six palaces number in the hundreds while I have but one husband—how uneven; it can be like this."
translations.idiomatic: His sister the Princess of Shanyin complained of his harem while she had one husband.

sentences.zh: 子業為主置面首左右三十人，進爵會稽郡長公主，秩同郡王，食湯沐邑二千戶，給鼓吹一部，加班劍二十人，每出遊，與羣臣陪乘。

translations.literal: Ziye set up thirty male favorites for her, promoted her to Princess of Kuaiji with rank equal to a prince, fief of two thousand households for bath and salary, one set of drums and pipes, twenty ceremonial guards; whenever she went out ministers attended her carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He gave her thirty lovers and princely rank.

sentences.zh: 吏部褚淵以有風貌，子業使淵侍主。

translations.literal: Chu Yuan of the Ministry of Personnel had fine looks; Ziye made Yuan attend the princess.
translations.idiomatic: He made Chu Yuan serve the princess.

sentences.zh: 子業皆令廟別畫其祖父形像，曾入裕廟，指裕像曰：「此渠大英雄，生擒數天子。」

translations.literal: Ziye had separate portraits painted of his ancestors; entering Yu's temple he pointed at Yu's image: "This fellow was a great hero—he captured several Sons of Heaven alive."
translations.idiomatic: In Yu's temple he mocked: "This one captured emperors alive."

sentences.zh: 次入義隆廟，指義隆像曰：「此渠亦不惡，但暮年中不免兒斫去頭。」

translations.literal: Next he entered Yilong's temple and pointed: "This fellow was not bad, but in his later years could not avoid having his head cut off by his son."
translations.idiomatic: Of Yilong he said: "His son cut off his head."

sentences.zh: 次入其父駿廟，指駿像曰：「此渠大好色，不擇尊卑。」

translations.literal: Next his father Jun's temple: "This fellow loved sex greatly and did not choose high or low."
translations.idiomatic: Of Jun he said: "He lusted without discrimination."

sentences.zh: 顧謂左右曰：「渠大齄鼻，如何不齄之？」

translations.literal: Turning to attendants he said: "The fellow had a big flat nose—why not make it flat?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked why Jun's portrait lacked his flat nose.

sentences.zh: 即令畫工齄駿像鼻。

translations.literal: He had the painter flatten Jun's nose in the portrait.
translations.idiomatic: He had the painter flatten Jun's nose.

sentences.zh: 其父子淫悖，書契所無也。

translations.literal: Such father-son debauchery is nowhere recorded in writing.
translations.idiomatic: Their debauchery is unmatched in records.

sentences.zh: 子業又殺沈慶之，撫軍諮議參軍何邁，即其新蔡主壻。

translations.literal: Ziye also killed Shen Qingzhi and the Pacifying Army Consultant He Mai, the new husband of the Princess of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: He killed Qingzhi and He Mai, the princess's husband.

sentences.zh: 其湘東王彧及建安王休仁、山陽王休祐常被猜忌，並欲誅之。

translations.literal: His Princes of Xiangdong Yu and Jian'an Xiuren and Shanyang Xiuyou were often suspected and all were to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Yu, Xiuren, and Xiuyou were marked for death.

sentences.zh: 休仁每以調謔悅之，故得推遷不死。

translations.literal: Xiuren often amused him with jest and banter, and so was promoted and not killed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren jested with him and survived.

sentences.zh: 彧、休祐形體肥大，遂以籠盛稱之，彧尤肥，號曰「猪王」。

translations.literal: Yu and Xiuyou were large of body; he caged them and called them by the cages—Yu was especially fat and called Pig King.
translations.idiomatic: He caged the fat princes; Yu he called Pig King.

sentences.zh: 廷尉劉矇妾懷孕，子業迎入宮，冀其生男，立為太子，及其生子，遂為大赦。

translations.literal: The Minister of Justice Liu Meng's concubine was pregnant; Ziye brought her into the palace hoping for a son to make heir; when she bore a son he proclaimed a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: He brought a pregnant concubine to court hoping for an heir.

sentences.zh: 子業召其南平王鑠妃江氏偶諸左右，江不從。

translations.literal: Ziye summoned the consort of his Prince of Nanping Shuo, Lady Jiang, to join his attendants; Jiang refused.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Lady Jiang; she refused.

sentences.zh: 子業曰：「若不從，當殺汝三子。」

translations.literal: Ziye said: "If you do not obey I will kill your three sons."
translations.idiomatic: He threatened her three sons.

sentences.zh: 江猶不從，乃鞭一百，殺其子敬猷等。

translations.literal: Jiang still refused; he flogged her a hundred times and killed her sons Jingyou and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: She still refused; he flogged her and killed her sons.

sentences.zh: 巫覡云「湘州有天子氣」，子業將南行以厭之，未行前，欲悉誅諸叔。

translations.literal: Wizards said Xiang province had the aura of a Son of Heaven; Ziye was about to go south to suppress it; before departing he wished to kill all his uncles.
translations.idiomatic: Wizards said Xiang had imperial aura; he planned to kill his uncles.

sentences.zh: 時彧被拘祕書省，與子業左右阮佃夫等謀廢子業。

translations.literal: Yu was confined in the Secretariat and plotted with Ziye's attendant Ruan Tianfu and others to depose Ziye.
translations.idiomatic: Yu plotted with Ruan Tianfu to depose him.

sentences.zh: 子業出華林園，共巫竹林堂前射鬼。

translations.literal: Ziye went out to Hualin Garden and with wizards shot at ghosts before the bamboo hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye went to Hualin to shoot at ghosts.

sentences.zh: 佃夫時為內監，乃以告外監典事朱幼、主衣壽寂之、細鎧主姜產之等，寂之抽刃而前，產之繼進。

translations.literal: Tianfu was then inner attendant; he informed the outer attendant director Zhu You, the master of robes Shou Jizhi, the fine-armor chief Jiang Chanzi, and others; Jizhi drew his blade and advanced, Chanzi followed.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu told Zhu You, Shou Jizhi, Jiang Chanzi, and others; Jizhi drew his blade and advanced, Chanzi behind him.

sentences.zh: 子業引弓射寂之，不中，寂之乃斬其首。

translations.literal: Ziye bent his bow and shot at Jizhi but missed; Jizhi then cut off his head.
translations.idiomatic: Ziye shot at Jizhi and missed; Jizhi beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 彧既誅子業，憂遽不知所為。

translations.literal: Once Yu had killed Ziye he was anxious and rushed, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: After killing Ziye, Yu was frantic with uncertainty.

sentences.zh: 休仁推立彧。

translations.literal: Xiuren pushed to install Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuren pressed Yu to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 彧時失履，徒跣登西堂，備天子儀服，呼諸大臣入見，事無巨細，稱令施行。

translations.literal: Yu had lost his shoes and barefoot ascended the Western Hall, prepared the Son of Heaven's ritual dress, summoned the great ministers to audience, and whether matters were great or small proclaimed orders for execution.
translations.idiomatic: Shoeless, Yu ascended the Western Hall in imperial regalia, summoned the ministers, and issued orders on every matter.

sentences.zh: 彧以豫章王子尚及山陰主為子業所狎，殺之。

translations.literal: Yu killed the Prince of Yuzhang Zishang and the Princess of Shanyin, whom Ziye had favored.
translations.idiomatic: He killed Zishang and the Princess of Shanyin, whom Ziye had favored.

sentences.zh: 十二月，僭即帝位，改年為泰始。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he usurped the throne and changed the era to Taishi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he seized the throne and proclaimed Taishi.

sentences.zh: 先是，子業敕其弟子勛曰：「聞汝與何邁謀共廢我，汝自量體氣何如孝武？

translations.literal: Earlier Ziye had ordered his younger brother Zixun: "I hear you and He Mai plotted to depose me—do you measure your strength against Emperor Xiaowu?
translations.idiomatic: Ziye had warned his brother Zixun: "I hear you plotted with He Mai to depose me—do you match Xiaowu in strength?

sentences.zh: 尋當遣使送藥與汝。」

translations.literal: I will soon send envoys with medicine for you."
translations.idiomatic: I will soon send you medicine."

sentences.zh: 子勛長史鄧琬與錄事參軍陶亮等起兵，遣其黨俞伯奇出頓大雷，[26]巴東太守孫仲之至于平石，[27]與陶亮並統前軍。

translations.literal: Zixun's Chief Clerk Deng Wan and Recording Officer Tao Liang and others raised troops, sent his partisan Yu Boqi to encamp at Dalei,[26] the Administrator of Badong Sun Chongzhi reached Pingshi,[27] and with Tao Liang jointly commanded the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan and Tao Liang raised troops; Yu Boqi encamped at Dalei,[26] Sun Chongzhi reached Pingshi,[27], and with Tao Liang led the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 始彧未知子勛起兵，加子勛車騎將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: At first Yu did not know Zixun had risen; he promoted Zixun to General of Chariots and Cavalry with ceremonial rank of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, unaware of the revolt, promoted Zixun to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 符至尋陽，鄧琬乃投於地，攘袂而起曰：「殿下當開端門，何黃閤之有！」

translations.literal: When the commission reached Xunyang, Deng Wan threw it to the ground, rolled up his sleeves, and rose, saying: "Your Highness should open the Gate of Beginning—what need for the Yellow Gate!"
translations.idiomatic: At Xunyang Wan threw down the commission: "Open the main gate—why the side entrance!"

sentences.zh: 與陶亮等徵兵馳檄，建牙於桑厄。

translations.literal: With Tao Liang and others he raised troops and issued proclamations, setting up headquarters at Sanger.
translations.idiomatic: He raised troops with Tao Liang and set up headquarters at Sanger.

sentences.zh: [28]時雍州刺史袁顗便勸子勛即位，琬乃立宗廟，設壇場，造乘輿法服，立子勛為天子，即位江州，號義嘉元年。

translations.literal: [28] The Inspector of Yong Yuan Yi then urged Zixun to ascend; Wan erected the ancestral temple, set the altar, made imperial carriage and ritual robes, and installed Zixun as Son of Heaven at Jiang province, era Yijia year one.
translations.idiomatic: [28] Yuan Yi urged Zixun to ascend; Wan installed him at Jiangzhou as emperor, era Yijia.

sentences.zh: 子勛以袁顗為尚書左僕射，鄧琬為尚書右僕射，左司馬張悅為領軍將軍、吏部尚書，州郡並加爵號。

translations.literal: Zixun made Yuan Yi Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Deng Wan Right Vice Director, Left Army Marshal Zhang Yue Army Commander and Minister of Personnel; commanderies and prefectures all received ennoblements.
translations.idiomatic: Zixun appointed Yuan Yi, Wan, and Zhang Yue; provinces received new ranks.

sentences.zh: 彧乃遣領軍將軍王玄謨討之，復遣其將沈攸之、劉靈出據虎檻。

translations.literal: Yu then sent Army Commander Wang Xuemo against him and again sent his generals Shen Youzhi and Liu Ling to hold Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent Wang Xuemo, Shen Youzhi, and Liu Ling against him.

sentences.zh: 初彧聞四方反亂，憂遽不知所為，休仁請前鋒決勝，於是始有防禦之軍。

translations.literal: When Yu first heard of rebellion everywhere he was anxious; Xiuren asked to lead the vanguard for decisive victory, and only then were defensive armies raised.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of rebellion, Yu panicked until Xiuren offered to lead the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 攸之軍至江州，斬子勛。

translations.literal: Youzhi's army reached Jiang province and beheaded Zixun.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi reached Jiangzhou and killed Zixun.

sentences.zh: 彧慮子勛弟松滋侯子房等年大終不相服，休仁遂勸除之，因誅駿舅子路休之等，以陷子房兄弟。

translations.literal: Yu feared Zixun's younger brother the Marquis of Songzi Zifang and others, grown large, would not submit; Xiuren urged their removal and by framing Zifang's brothers killed Jun's maternal kin Zilu Xiuzhi and others.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Zifang and his brothers, Yu and Xiuren killed Jun's kin and framed the princes.

sentences.zh: 於是殺駿子安陸王子綏及子房、臨海王子頊、[29]永嘉王子仁、始安王子真、邵陵王子元、淮南王子孟、臨賀王子產、晉熙王子輿及子起、子期、子悅、子頓。
