translations.literal: Thereupon he killed Jun's sons the Prince of Anlu Zisui, Zifang, the Prince of Linhai Zixu,[29] the Prince of Yongjia Ziren, the Prince of Shi'an Zizhen, the Prince of Shaoling Ziyuan, the Prince of Huainan Zimeng, the Prince of Linhe Zichan, the Prince of Jinxi Ziyu, and Ziqi, Ziqi, Ziyue, and Zidun.
translations.idiomatic: He killed Jun's sons Zisui, Zifang, Zixu,[29], Ziren, Zizhen, Ziyuan, Zimeng, Zichan, Ziyu, Ziqi, Ziqi, Ziyue, and Zidun.

sentences.zh: [30]初，駿二十八男，其餘先早夭，及子業殺子鸞等，至是盡殪之矣，其骨肉相殘若此之甚。

translations.literal: [30] Earlier Jun had twenty-eight sons; the rest had died young earlier, and after Ziye killed Ziluan and others, now they were all exterminated—such was the depth of kin slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: [30] Of Jun's twenty-eight sons, all were now dead—kin slaughter at its worst.

sentences.zh: 彧南新蔡太守常珍奇奉啟請降，顯祖詔遣西河公元石、京兆侯張窮奇率軍援之。

translations.literal: Yu's Administrator of Nanxin'cai Chang Zhenqi submitted a memorial requesting surrender; Emperor Xianzu ordered the Duke of Xihe Yuan Shi and the Marquis of Jingzhao Zhang Qiongqi with troops to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Zhenqi surrendered; Xianzu sent Yuan Shi and Zhang Qiongqi to aid him.

sentences.zh: 皇興元年正月，彧遣其散騎常侍貝思、散騎侍郎崔小白朝貢。

translations.literal: In the first month of Huangxing year one Yu sent his Regular Gentleman Attendant Bei Si and Regular Attendant Cui Xiaobai on tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangxing year one Yu sent Bei Si and Cui Xiaobai with tribute.

sentences.zh: 初，彧遣其鎮軍張永、領軍沈攸之以大眾迎其徐州刺史薛安都。

translations.literal: Earlier Yu had sent his Pacifying Army Zhang Yong and Army Commander Shen Youzhi with a great host to welcome his Inspector of Xu Xue Andu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had sent Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi to fetch Xue Andu.

sentences.zh: 安都聞永將發，乃遣信請降。

translations.literal: When Andu heard Yong was setting out he sent word requesting surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Andu requested surrender.

sentences.zh: 顯祖詔博陵公尉元、城陽公孔伯恭率騎二萬救之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu ordered the Duke of Boling Wei Yuan and the Duke of Chengyang Kong Bogong with twenty thousand horse to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu sent Wei Yuan and Kong Bogong with twenty thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 永等。

translations.literal: Yong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and his forces.

sentences.zh: 前後奮擊，斬首凍沒死者不可勝數。

translations.literal: Attacking repeatedly before and after, heads taken and frozen or drowned dead were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In repeated battles, Song dead by blade and frost were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: [31]又其兗州刺史畢眾敬亦來降款，至是，徐兗及淮西諸郡、青齊二州相尋歸附。

translations.literal: [31] His Inspector of Yan Bi Zhongjing also came to submit; by then Xu, Yan, and the commanderies west of the Huai, and Qing and Qi in succession submitted.
translations.idiomatic: [31] Bi Zhongjing surrendered; Xu, Yan, Huai west, Qing, and Qi followed.

sentences.zh: 彧又遣其中領軍沈攸之、太子左衞率劉勔寇彭城，兗州刺史申纂守無鹽。

translations.literal: Yu again sent his Central Army Commander Shen Youzhi and the Heir's Left Guard Leader Liu Mi to raid Pengcheng; the Inspector of Yan Shen Zuan held Wuyan.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi and Liu Mi raided Pengcheng; Shen Zuan held Wuyan.

sentences.zh: 時薛安都略有廣平、順陽、義成、扶風諸郡。

translations.literal: Andu then held Guangping, Shunyang, Yicheng, Fufeng, and other commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Andu held several commanderies.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之至下邳，與元等戰敗而走。

translations.literal: Youzhi reached Xiapi, fought Yuan and others, was defeated, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi was defeated at Xiapi and fled.

sentences.zh: 初，彧青州刺史沈文秀、冀州刺史崔道固並請歸順，詔遣征南大將軍慕容白曜率眾援之。

translations.literal: Earlier the Inspectors of Qing Shen Wenxiu and Ji Cui Daogu had requested submission; an edict ordered the General Who Campaigns South Murong Baiyao with troops to aid them.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiu and Daogu had submitted; Baiyao was sent to aid them.

sentences.zh: 文秀等復叛歸彧。

translations.literal: Wenxiu and the others rebelled again and returned to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: They rebelled and rejoined Yu.

sentences.zh: 白曜進軍圍城。

translations.literal: Baiyao advanced and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyao besieged them.

sentences.zh: 二年，克歷城，獲道固。

translations.literal: In the second year he took Licheng and captured Daogu.
translations.idiomatic: In year two he took Licheng and captured Daogu.

sentences.zh: 彧遣其員外散騎常侍李豐朝貢。

translations.literal: Yu sent his Extraordinary Gentleman Attendant Li Feng on tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent Li Feng with tribute.

sentences.zh: 彧遣沈文秀弟文靜海道救青州，文靜至東萊之不期城，白曜遣軍克之。

translations.literal: Yu sent Wenxiu's younger brother Wenjing by sea to relieve Qing; Wenjing reached Buqi city in Donglai; Baiyao sent troops and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing sailed to relieve Qing; Baiyao took Buqi.

sentences.zh: 尋獲東陽城。

translations.literal: Soon he took Dongyang city.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 彧遣其員外散騎常侍王希涓朝貢。

translations.literal: Yu sent his Extraordinary Gentleman Attendant Wang Xijuan on tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent Wang Xijuan with tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年六月，彧又遣員外散騎常侍劉航朝貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year Yu again sent Extraordinary Gentleman Attendant Liu Hang on tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: In month six of year four Yu sent Liu Hang with tribute.

sentences.zh: 延興元年，彧於巖山射雉，休祐從在後，與其左右相失。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanxing Yu hunted pheasants at Yanshan; Xiuyou followed behind and was separated from his attendants.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanshan Yu hunted; Xiuyou was separated from his party.

sentences.zh: 彧遣壽寂之率諸壯士追躡休祐，蹴令墜馬，拉而殺之，乃揚聲曰：「驃騎墮馬死。」

translations.literal: Yu sent Shou Jizhi with stalwarts in pursuit of Xiuyou, kicked him from his horse, pulled him down and killed him, then proclaimed loudly: "The Rapid Cavalry fell from his horse and died."
translations.idiomatic: Yu had Jizhi kill Xiuyou and announced he died in a fall.

sentences.zh: 召司徒休仁宿尚書下省，鴆而殺之。

translations.literal: He summoned Minister of Education Xiuren to lodge in the Masters of Writing quarters below and poisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He poisoned Xiuren at the Secretariat quarters.

sentences.zh: 自彧立之後，民庶凋弊，而宮殿器服多更興造。

translations.literal: From Yu's establishment the people were depleted while palaces, vessels, and dress were largely rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yu the people suffered while palaces were rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 初其即位，軍人多被超越，或有不與戎勤，寄名受賞。

translations.literal: At his accession many soldiers were promoted beyond merit; some who had not shared in military toil bore names and received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers were promoted without merit.

sentences.zh: 阮佃夫等並被信委，凡所談笑，言無不行，抽進阿黨，咸受不次之位。

translations.literal: Ruan Tianfu and others were all trusted; whatever they said in jest was carried out; they advanced partisans and all received offices out of order.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu and favorites held unchecked power.

sentences.zh: 故佃夫左右，乃有四軍、五校、羽林、給事等官，皆市井傭販之人，諂附而獲。

translations.literal: Thus Tianfu's attendants held posts of four armies, five commandants, imperial guard, and attendants—all marketplace peddlers who flattered their way to office.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu's men were marketplace flatterers in high office.

sentences.zh: 至綱紀不立，風政頹弊，境內多難，民庶嗷然。

translations.literal: Discipline was not established, customs declined, difficulties multiplied within the borders, and the people groaned.
translations.idiomatic: Discipline collapsed and the people groaned.

sentences.zh: 遂廣募義勇，置為部曲。

translations.literal: He then broadly recruited volunteers and installed them as private troops.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited private troops.

sentences.zh: 於是官品淪褫，士人渾亂，民眾顒顒，咸願來奔矣。

translations.literal: Official ranks were debased, gentry confused, the masses eager—all wished to flee to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks collapsed; many wished to flee north.

sentences.zh: 彧遣其司州刺史垣叔通為益州刺史，叔通極為聚斂，蜀還之貨過數千金，知彧好財，先送家資之半，彧猶嫌少。

translations.literal: Yu made his Inspector of Si Yuan Shutong Inspector of Yi; Shutong extorted heavily; goods from Shu returning exceeded several thousand in gold; knowing Yu loved wealth he first sent half his household goods—Yu still thought it too little.
translations.idiomatic: Shutong extorted Yi; Yu extorted Shutong in turn.

sentences.zh: 及叔通至建業，遣詣廷尉，彧先令獄官留之於訊堂，彌旬不得出。

translations.literal: When Shutong reached Jianye he was sent to the Minister of Justice; Yu first had prison officials detain him in the interrogation hall for more than ten days without release.
translations.idiomatic: Shutong was imprisoned until he paid more.

sentences.zh: 叔通於是悉送其財，然後原遣。

translations.literal: Shutong then sent all his wealth, and only then was he released.
translations.idiomatic: He sent all his wealth and was released.

sentences.zh: 凡蠻夷不受鞭罰，輸財贖罪，謂之賧，時人謂叔通被賧刺史。

translations.literal: Barbarians who did not accept whipping paid wealth to redeem guilt, called dian; people said Shutong was the dian Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Shutong was called the "ransom inspector."

sentences.zh: 彧嘗宮內大集而裸婦人觀之，以為忻笑。

translations.literal: Yu once gathered a great assembly in the palace with naked women to watch, taking it as delight.
translations.idiomatic: He entertained himself with naked women in court.

sentences.zh: 其妻王氏以扇鄣面，獨無所言。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Wang screened her face with a fan and alone said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang hid her face in silence.

sentences.zh: 彧怒曰：「外舍家寒乞，今共為笑樂，何獨不視！」

translations.literal: Yu in anger said: "The outer household are cold beggars—now we share laughter; why alone do you not look!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu raged: "Why will you not look!"

sentences.zh: 王曰：「為樂之事，其方自多，豈有姑姊妹集聚，而裸婦人形體，以此為樂！

translations.literal: Wang said: "For delight there are many ways—how can there be a gathering of aunts and sisters with naked women's bodies as the amusement!
translations.idiomatic: Wang said: "This is no amusement for kin to share.

sentences.zh: 外舍之為忻，適與此不同。」

translations.literal: The outer household's delight is quite unlike this."
translations.idiomatic: Their joy is not this."

sentences.zh: 彧大怒，遣王起去。

translations.literal: Yu in great anger sent Wang away.
translations.idiomatic: Yu drove her out.

sentences.zh: 彧末年好事鬼神，多所忌諱，言語文書有禍敗凶喪及疑似之言應回避者數百千品，有犯必加罪戮。

translations.literal: In his later years Yu favored ghosts and spirits and had many taboos; in speech and documents there were hundreds and thousands of types of ill-omen, defeat, mourning, and suspicious words to be avoided—violation always brought punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he obsessed over taboo words and punished violations.

sentences.zh: 改騧馬字為馬邊瓜，以「騧」似「禍」字故也。

translations.literal: He changed the character for piebald horse to "horse by melon," because "piebald" resembled the character for "calamity."
translations.idiomatic: He renamed characters to avoid ill omens.

sentences.zh: 嘗以南苑借張永，言且給三百年，期訖更申。

translations.literal: He once lent the Southern Park to Zhang Yong, saying he would grant it for three hundred years and renew when the term ended.
translations.idiomatic: He joked he lent the Southern Park for three hundred years.

sentences.zh: 其事皆如此。

translations.literal: His affairs were all like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such were his ways.

sentences.zh: 又以宣陽門之名不善，甚諱之。

translations.literal: He also thought the name Xuanyang Gate ill-omened and greatly avoided it.
translations.idiomatic: He feared the name Xuanyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 其太后停屍漆牀，移出東宮，見之怒甚，免中庶子官，職局以下坐死者數十人。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager's corpse lay on a lacquered couch moved out of the Eastern Palace, he saw it and raged; the Palace Attendant of the Heir was dismissed; dozens below in the bureau were executed for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his mother's corpse enraged him; dozens were executed.

sentences.zh: 內外常慮犯誤，人不自保。

translations.literal: Inside and outside constantly feared error; none could protect themselves.
translations.idiomatic: None felt safe.

sentences.zh: 移牀治壁，必祭土神，文士為辭，祝事如大祭。

translations.literal: Moving beds or repairing walls he always sacrificed to the earth god; literati composed prayers as for great sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He sacrificed to earth gods when moving furniture.

sentences.zh: 又更忍虐好殺，左右失旨忤意，往往有刳斮斷截者。

translations.literal: He grew more cruel and fond of killing; attendants who missed his intent were often dismembered or cut apart.
translations.idiomatic: He dismembered attendants who displeased him.

sentences.zh: 時遣窺覘淮泗，軍旅不息，荒弊積久，府藏空虛，內外百官，普斷祿俸。

translations.literal: He constantly sent spies to the Huai and Si; armies never ceased; ruin accumulated long; treasuries were empty; all officials within and without had salaries cut.
translations.idiomatic: War and empty treasuries beggared officials.

sentences.zh: 而彧奢費過度，務為彫侈，每所造制，必為正御三十、副御三十、次副三十，須一物輒造九十枚。

translations.literal: Yet Yu spent excessively, pursuing carved luxury; each object made was thirty for primary use, thirty for secondary, thirty for tertiary—one item required ninety made.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered ninety copies of every luxury object.

sentences.zh: 境內騷然，人不堪命。

translations.literal: The realm was in turmoil; people could not bear the burden.
translations.idiomatic: The people were crushed.

sentences.zh: 彧又以壽寂之有膽決，乃殺之。

translations.literal: Yu also killed Shou Jizhi because of his bold decisiveness.
translations.idiomatic: He killed Jizhi for his boldness.

sentences.zh: 又追降休仁、休祐為庶人，絕其屬籍，諸子徙遠郡。

translations.literal: He also pursued the demoted Xiuren and Xiuyou to commoner status, cut them from the genealogy, and moved sons to distant commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He degraded Xiuren and Xiuyou's families.

sentences.zh: 休祐母邢、妻江，付廷尉殺之。

translations.literal: Xiuyou's mother Xing and wife Jiang were handed to the Minister of Justice and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyou's mother and wife were executed.

sentences.zh: 遣員外散騎侍郎田廉、員外散騎侍郎祖德朝貢。

translations.literal: He sent Extraordinary Attendant Tian Lian and Extraordinary Attendant Zu De on tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Tian Lian and Zu De with tribute.

sentences.zh: 又殺其巴陵王休若。

translations.literal: He also killed his Prince of Baling Xiuruo.
translations.idiomatic: He killed Prince Xiuruo of Baling.

sentences.zh: 改年為泰豫。

translations.literal: He changed the era to Taiyu.
translations.idiomatic: He changed the era to Taiyu.

sentences.zh: 又遣田廉及員外散騎侍郎劉惠秀朝貢。

translations.literal: He again sent Tian Lian and Extraordinary Attendant Liu Huixiu on tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Tian Lian and Liu Huixiu with tribute.

sentences.zh: 彧又殺太子太傅王景文，畏其族盛故也。

translations.literal: Yu also killed the Grand Tutor of the Heir Wang Jingwen, fearing his clan's power.
translations.idiomatic: He killed Wang Jingwen fearing his clan.

sentences.zh: 彧死，子昱僭立，改為元徽。

translations.literal: Yu died; his son Yu usurped the throne and changed the era to Yuanhui.
translations.idiomatic: Yu died; his son Yu seized power as Yuanhui.

sentences.zh: 昱遣員外散騎常侍田惠紹、員外散騎侍郎劉惠秀朝貢。

translations.literal: Yu sent Extraordinary Attendant Tian Huishao and Extraordinary Attendant Liu Huixiu on tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 其司空桂陽王休範奔尋陽舉兵，[33]右衞將軍蕭道成率眾軍出頓新亭。

translations.literal: His Minister of Works the Prince of Guiyang Xiufan fled to Xunyang and raised troops;[33] the General of the Right Guard Xiao Daocheng led the mass of armies to encamp at Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiufan of Guiyang rebelled at Xunyang;[33] Xiao Daocheng marched to Xinting.

sentences.zh: 越騎校尉張苟兒斬休範首，其左右皆散，道成遣送其首，塗中遇賊，遂棄於水中。

translations.literal: The Colonel of the Rapid Cavalry Zhang Gou'er cut off Xiufan's head; his attendants all scattered; Daocheng sent the head but met bandits on the road and cast it into the water.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gou'er killed Xiufan; his head was lost in transit.

sentences.zh: 休範之徒乃詐曰：「殿下猶在新亭。」

translations.literal: Xiufan's partisans then falsely said: "Your Highness is still at Xinting."
translations.idiomatic: Rebels claimed Xiufan still lived at Xinting.

sentences.zh: 於是士庶奔馳候迎。

translations.literal: Thereupon gentry and commoners rushed to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: People rushed to welcome the false report.

sentences.zh: 是夜，休範將杜墨騾等又攻新亭東廂，休範參軍江珉等破二縣六署，竊掠金帛，放諸徒隸。

translations.literal: That night Xiufan's general Du Moluan and others again attacked the eastern wing at Xinting; Xiufan's staff officer Jiang Min and others broke six offices of two counties, plundered gold and silk, and released convict laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels raided Xinting and freed prisoners.

sentences.zh: 由是徒眾復盛，燒東宮津陽門，乃領軍右府。

translations.literal: Thus the mob swelled again, burned the Jinyang Gate of the Eastern Palace—the headquarters of the Right Army.
translations.idiomatic: Mobs burned the Eastern Palace gate.

sentences.zh: 昱將陳顯達率所領至杜姥宅，破墨騾軍主全景淵。

translations.literal: Yu's general Chen Xianda led his command to the Du family mansion and defeated Moluan's army commander Quan Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda defeated Quan Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 進平白壁，宣陽、津陽二門，斬墨騾等。

translations.literal: He advanced to pacify Bai Bi, Xuanyang, and Jinyang gates, and beheaded Moluan and others.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified the gates and killed Moluan.

sentences.zh: 昱遣其員外散騎常侍明曇徽、員外散騎侍郎江山圖朝貢。

translations.literal: Yu sent Extraordinary Attendant Ming Tanhui and Extraordinary Attendant Jiang Shantu on tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sent Ming Tanhui and Jiang Shantu with tribute.

sentences.zh: 五年，又遣員外散騎常侍李祖、員外散騎侍郎魚長耀朝貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he again sent Extraordinary Attendant Li Zu and Extraordinary Attendant Yu Changyao on tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: In year five he sent Li Zu and Yu Changyao with tribute.

sentences.zh: 承明初，昱建平王景素據京口叛昱，昱遣蕭道成前軍將軍周盤龍、殿中將軍張倪奴討之，攻陷京口，斬景素。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chengming Yu's Prince of Jianping Jingsu held Jingkou in rebellion; Yu sent Daocheng's vanguard Zhou Panlong and Palace General Zhang Ninu against him, took Jingkou, and beheaded Jingsu.
translations.idiomatic: Jingsu rebelled at Jingkou; Daocheng's generals killed him.

sentences.zh: 太和初，昱以其母數諫責之，遂使太醫煮藥欲鴆之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe Yu because his mother repeatedly remonstrated scolded her and had the imperial physician brew medicine to poison her.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to poison his mother.

sentences.zh: 左右止之曰：「若行此事，官便應作孝，豈復得出入狡獪。」

translations.literal: Attendants stopped him: "If you do this, Your Majesty should observe mourning and could no longer go out in mischief."
translations.idiomatic: Attendants said he could not carouse if he killed her.

sentences.zh: 昱曰：「汝語大有理。」

translations.literal: Yu said: "Your words make great sense."
translations.idiomatic: Yu agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: He stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped.

sentences.zh: 初昱母陳氏，本李道兒妾，彧納之，生昱，故世中皆呼昱為李氏子，昱每自稱李將軍，或自名為李統。

translations.literal: Earlier Yu's mother Lady Chen was originally concubine to Li Dao'er; Yu took her in and she bore Yu—thus all called Yu Li's son; Yu often called himself General Li or named himself Li Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was known as Li's son and called himself General Li.

sentences.zh: 昱直閤將軍申伯宗、步兵校尉朱幼、司徒左長史沈勃等欲廢昱，昱親率羽林兵掩之，乃躬運矛鋋，手殺勃等，闔門嬰稚，莫不臠截。

translations.literal: Yu's Regular Attendant Shen Bozong, Commandant of Footsoldiers Zhu You, Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education Shen Bo, and others wished to depose Yu; Yu personally led imperial guards to seize them, himself wielding spear and halberd, hand-killing Bo and others; every infant of the household was dismembered.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Bozong and others plotted against Yu; he killed them and their families.

sentences.zh: 昱狂走逸遊，不捨晝夜，腹心所寄數十許人，並執兵刃為人之牙爪，路行逢人，便加斫刺，或入人家劫略財賄，往來倐忽，狀若鬼魅。

translations.literal: Yu ran wild day and night without rest; several dozen trusted men carried weapons as his claws, hacking anyone met on the road or robbing houses—coming and going like ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: Yu rampaged day and night with armed thugs, killing and robbing like ghosts.

sentences.zh: 建業惶振，並重關自守。

translations.literal: Jianye was terrified; all barred their gates in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Jianye barred its gates in terror.

sentences.zh: 又搥拍鍼鑿錐鋸之屬，常以自隨，或有忤意，輒加酷暴，搥陰刺心剖腹之誅，日有十數。

translations.literal: He carried hammers, awls, chisels, and saws; those who displeased him suffered torture—dozens daily of chest-striking, yin-stabbing, heart-gutting punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He tortured dozens daily with hammers and blades.

sentences.zh: 常見臥屍流血，然後為樂，無所誅害，則憂思草草。

translations.literal: He delighted only when he saw corpses and flowing blood; without killings he grew restless.
translations.idiomatic: He needed bloodshed to be happy.

sentences.zh: 於耀靈殿上養驢數十頭，造露車，以銀為校具，或乘以出入。

translations.literal: He kept dozens of donkeys in Yaoling Hall and made open carts with silver fittings, sometimes riding out.
translations.idiomatic: He rode donkey carts with silver fittings through the palace.

sentences.zh: 著小袴衫，帶挾刀劍。

translations.literal: He wore short trousers and belted sword and blade.
translations.idiomatic: He wore short trousers and swords.

sentences.zh: 與營署女子通好，自齎私服贈之。

translations.literal: He favored camp women and gave them his own clothes as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He slept with camp women and gave them gifts.

sentences.zh: 常入壚肆飲酒，輒與左右歌唱，略民鷄犬，躬自屠割。

translations.literal: He often drank in taverns, sang with attendants, seized people's chickens and dogs, and butchered them himself.
translations.idiomatic: He drank in taverns, sang, and slaughtered stolen livestock.

sentences.zh: 內外畏惡，人不自保。

translations.literal: Inside and outside feared and hated him; none could protect themselves.
translations.idiomatic: All feared him.

sentences.zh: 昱往新安寺，夕乃還殿，寢於氈幄。

translations.literal: Yu went to Xin'an Temple and at evening returned to the hall, sleeping in a felt tent.
translations.idiomatic: He slept drunk in a felt tent.

sentences.zh: 昱左右楊玉夫、楊萬年等見其醉眠，乃於幄斬之。

translations.literal: Attendants Yang Yufu and Yang Wannian saw him drunk asleep and cut off his head in the tent.
translations.idiomatic: Yufu and Wannian beheaded him in his sleep.

sentences.zh: 左右陳奉伯稱敕開承明門出，送首於直閤王敬則，夜送昱首與中領軍蕭道成。

translations.literal: Chen Fengbo proclaimed an edict to open Chenming Gate; he sent the head to Regular Attendant Wang Jingze, who at night delivered Yu's head to Central Army Commander Xiao Daocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fengbo sent the head to Daocheng through Jingze.

sentences.zh: 道成率左右數十人，稱昱行還，開承明門入殿，云其皇太后令廢昱為蒼梧王，立昱弟揚州刺史安成王準。

translations.literal: Daocheng led several dozen men, claiming Yu was returning, opened Chenming Gate, entered the hall, and announced the Empress Dowager's order deposing Yu as Prince of Cangwu and installing Yu's younger brother the Inspector of Yang, Prince Ancheng Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng entered, deposed Yu, and installed Prince Zhun of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 初，彧晚年痿疾，不能內御，諸弟姬人有懷孕者，輒取以入宮，及生男，皆殺其母而與其宮人所愛者養之。

translations.literal: Earlier Yu in his later years was impotent; when brothers' concubines became pregnant he took them into the palace; when sons were born he killed the mothers and raised the boys with favored palace women.
translations.idiomatic: Yu stole pregnant concubines and killed the mothers of the sons he raised.

sentences.zh: 準即桂陽王休範子也。

translations.literal: Zhun was the son of the Prince of Guiyang Xiufan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun was Xiufan's son.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史沈攸之興兵討道成。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Jing Shen Youzhi raised troops against Daocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi rebelled against Daocheng.

sentences.zh: 準改年為昇明。

translations.literal: Zhun changed the era to Shengming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun changed the era to Shengming.

sentences.zh: 遣其員外散騎常侍李祖、員外散騎侍郎陶貞寶赴國訃，并貢方物。

translations.literal: He sent Extraordinary Attendant Li Zu and Extraordinary Attendant Tao Zhenbao to announce the mourning mission to the realm and offer local products.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys with tribute and mourning notice.

sentences.zh: 準司徒袁粲、丹陽尹劉秉、中領軍劉韞、前湘州刺史王蘊等以道成專恣，潛謀圖之，共推粲為主，要引沈攸之以為外援。

translations.literal: Zhun's Minister of Education Yuan Can, Governor of Danyang Liu Bing, Central Army Commander Liu Yun, former Inspector of Xiang Wang Yun, and others, because Daocheng was arbitrary, secretly plotted against him, jointly promoting Can as leader and intending to draw Shen Youzhi as external aid.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can and others plotted against Daocheng with Youzhi as ally.

sentences.zh: 丹陽丞王遜告道成，並斬之。

translations.literal: The Assistant of Danyang Wang Xun informed Daocheng; all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun exposed the plot; all were killed.

sentences.zh: 準遣員外散騎常侍何僴、員外散騎侍郎孔逷朝貢。

translations.literal: Zhun sent Extraordinary Attendant He Xian and Extraordinary Attendant Kong Yuan on tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun sent He Xian and Kong Yuan with tribute.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，準遣其員外散騎常侍殷靈誕、員外散騎侍郎苟昭先朝貢。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year Zhun sent Extraordinary Attendant Yin Lingding and Extraordinary Attendant Gou Zhaoxian on tribute missions.
translations.idiomatic: In year three month one he sent Yin Lingding and Gou Zhaoxian.

sentences.zh: 準尋禪位於道成，居于東邸。

translations.literal: Zhun soon abdicated to Daocheng and dwelt in the Eastern Residence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun abdicated to Daocheng.

sentences.zh: 道成僭立，封準汝陰郡王，尋死於丹陽。

translations.literal: Daocheng usurped the throne, enfeoffed Zhun as Prince of Ruyin, and soon he died in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Daocheng seized power; Zhun died soon after as Prince of Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：桓玄侏張，馮、劉乃厥。

translations.literal: The historian says: Huan Xuan rose in arrogance; Feng and Liu followed. Doubtful. Utterly vicious and deluded, a laughingstock under heaven—is this the constant nature of the Yi and Chu?
translations.idiomatic: The historian judges: Xuan, Feng, and Liu were rebels beyond measure—perhaps the nature of southern lords.

translations.literal: 〈Doubt〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Doubt〉

sentences.zh: 窮凶極迷，為天下笑，其夷、楚之常性乎？

translations.literal: Utterly vicious and deluded, a laughingstock under heaven—is this the constant nature of the Yi and Chu?
translations.idiomatic: Such cruelty and folly—was it the nature of the southern realms?

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 仲堪遣龍驤將軍殷邁振威將軍劉山民等統眾七千至西江口 晉書卷八四殷仲堪傳稱：「遣從弟遹等水軍七千至江西

translations.literal: Zhongkan sent the Dragon Cavalry General Yin Mai, General Who Quells Might Liu Shanmin, and others commanding seven thousand to the West River mouth. Jin shu 84 Yin Zhongkan biography states: "He sent his younger cousin Kui and others with a water army of seven thousand to the west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: "Mai" should be "Kui" per Jin shu 84.

sentences.zh: 〈西江口誤倒〉。」

translations.literal: 〈West River mouth transposed〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈West River mouth transposed〉

sentences.zh: 同書同卷楊佺期傳、卷九九桓玄傳亦見仲堪從弟遹，這裏「邁」當是「遹」之訛。

translations.literal: Jin shu 84 Yang Quanqi biography and 99 Huan Xuan biography also mention Zhongkan's younger cousin Kui; here "Mai" is likely a corruption of "Kui."
translations.idiomatic: Mai" is likely a corruption of "Kui."

sentences.zh: 比來收集 諸本「比」訛「北」，不可通，今據晉書卷八四楊佺期傳、通鑑卷一一一

translations.literal: Recently collected. All editions corrupt "recent" to "north," which makes no sense; now per Jin shu 84 Yang Quanqi biography and Zizhi tongjian 111.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: "recent" was corrupted to "north."

sentences.zh: 〈三五０三頁〉

translations.literal: 〈3503 pages〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈3503 pages〉

sentences.zh: 改。

translations.literal: Corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected.

sentences.zh: 德宗以玄為持節都督荊司雍秦梁益寧江八州及揚豫并八郡諸軍事 晉書卷九九桓玄傳云：「進督八州及揚、豫八郡。」

translations.literal: Dezong made Xuan Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of the eight provinces of Jing, Si, Yong, Qin, Liang, Yi, Ning, and Jiang and military affairs of Yang, Yu, and eight commanderies. Jin shu 99 Huan Xuan biography: "Advanced to command eight provinces and eight commanderies of Yang and Yu." Yang and Yu were not fully supervised—only eight subordinate commanderies—so "and" below Yang-Yu should not have "and"; it is likely interpolated text.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: redundant "and" in the eight-province commission.

sentences.zh: 揚豫二州非全督，止督所屬之八郡，「揚豫」下不合有「并」字，當是衍文。

translations.literal: Xuan had Huan Qian and He Danzhi encamp at the Eastern Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Collation note on Eastern Gate.

sentences.zh: 玄使桓謙何澹之屯於東掖門 下文劉裕傳及晉書桓玄傳「東掖門」作「東陵」，宋書卷一武帝紀作「東陵口」。

translations.literal: Below in Liu Yu's biography and Jin shu Huan Xuan biography "Eastern Gate" is "Eastern Mound"; Song shu 1 Emperor Wu annals has "Eastern Mound mouth."
translations.idiomatic: Variants: Eastern Gate vs Eastern Mound.

sentences.zh: 通鑑卷一一三

translations.literal: Zizhi tongjian 113
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi tongjian 113

sentences.zh: 〈三五六三頁〉

translations.literal: 〈3563 pages〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈3563 pages〉

sentences.zh: 也作「東陵」，胡注：「東陵，在覆舟山東北。」

translations.literal: also has "Eastern Mound"; Hu note: "Eastern Mound is northeast of Fuzhou Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: Hu note on Eastern Mound location.

sentences.zh: 按當時桓、何二人與卞範之合兵二萬以拒劉裕，卞屯覆舟山西，桓、何屯覆舟山東，故云「眾合二萬」。

translations.literal: At that time Huan and He with Bian Fanzhi combined twenty thousand to resist Liu Yu; Bian was west of Fuzhou Mountain, Huan and He east—hence "hosts combined twenty thousand."
translations.idiomatic: Troop positions around Fuzhou Mountain.

sentences.zh: 「東掖門」無考，當是宮門，和卞範之不相及，豈得云「合」。

translations.literal: "Eastern Gate" is unattested; it should be "Eastern Mound mouth," corrupted from Xuan's exit by the Southern Gate.
translations.idiomatic: "Eastern Gate" should be "Eastern Mound mouth."

sentences.zh: 這裏「東掖門」當作「東陵口」，涉下桓玄出「南掖門」而訛。

translations.literal: Here "Eastern Gate" should be Eastern Mound mouth, corrupted from mention of Xuan leaving the Southern Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Textual corruption note.

sentences.zh: 振自為都督八州鎮軍將軍荊州刺史 百衲本「鎮軍」二字空格，南本以下諸本作「鎮軍」，晉書卷七四桓彝附桓振傳作「鎮西」。

translations.literal: Zhen made himself Commander-in-Chief of Eight Provinces, Pacifying Army General, Inspector of Jing. Bai na edition leaves blank for "Pacifying Army"; southern editions have "Pacifying Army"; Jin shu 74 Huan Yi appendix Huan Zhen biography has "Pacifying West."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Pacifying Army vs Pacifying West.

sentences.zh: 按荊州刺史的軍號，資歷地位較高者例多加「安西」，又進「征西將軍」，荊州亦稱西州，疑當作「鎮西」。

translations.literal: For Inspector of Jing the higher military title was usually "Pacifies West," then "Campaigns West"; Jing was also called Western Province—likely should read "Pacifying West."
translations.idiomatic: For the Inspector of Jing province, men of higher seniority and standing usually received the additional title General Who Pacifies the West and were then promoted to General Who Campaigns West. Jing province was also called Western Province; the text here probably should read General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 或舊本「鎮」字不缺，後人以意補「軍」字。

translations.literal: Or the original "Pacifying" was intact and later someone supplied "Army."
translations.idiomatic: Alternatively, the original character for Pacifying may not have been missing, and a later reader supplied the character for Army according to his own understanding.

sentences.zh: 但無他證，今姑從南本。

translations.literal: But without other evidence, we follow the southern edition for now.
translations.idiomatic: But without other supporting evidence, the text here provisionally follows the southern edition.

sentences.zh: 稍遷衞中郎將 北史卷九三馮跋傳作「衞中將軍」。

translations.literal: Gradually promoted to Guard Central Army General. Beishi 93 Feng Ba biography has "Guard Central General."
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Central Army General of the Guard. The biography of Feng Ba in Beishi, juan 93, reads General of the Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 按本書卷九五慕容垂附慕容熙傳、晉書卷一二五馮跋載記並作「中衞將軍」。

translations.literal: Per this book 95 Murong Chui appendix Murong Xi biography and Jin shu 125 Feng Ba annals: Central Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: According to the appended biography of Murong Xi in Murong Chui's account in this book, juan 95, and the annals of Feng Ba in Jin shu, juan 125, the title is given as General of the Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 唯晉書卷一二四慕容熙載記作「衞中將軍」，與北史馮跋傳合，然御覽卷一二五引十六國春秋後燕錄慕容熙條仍作「中衞將軍」。

translations.literal: Only Jin shu 124 Murong Xi annals has Guard Central General, matching Beishi Feng Ba; yet Imperial Readings 125 Sixteen Kingdoms Spring and Autumn Later Yan Records Murong Xi still has Central Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Only Jin shu, juan 124, in the annals of Murong Xi, reads General of the Guard at Center, agreeing with the Beishi biography of Feng Ba; yet the Imperial Readings, juan 125, citing the Sixteen Kingdoms Spring and Autumn Later Yan Record entry for Murong Xi, still reads General of the Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 檢晉書卷二０職官志稱「魏文帝置中衞將軍，晉武帝分為左右衞將軍」，則中衞將軍舊有此官，晉雖分置左右衞，而後燕則中、左、右並置。

translations.literal: Jin shu 20 Offices Annals: Wei Wendi established Central Guard General; Jin Wudi split into Left and Right Guard—Later Yan kept all three.
translations.idiomatic: Examination of Jin shu, juan 20, Monographs on Offices, states that Emperor Wen of Wei established the General of the Central Guard and that Emperor Wu of Jin divided the post into Left and Right Guard Generals. Thus the Central Guard General existed as an earlier office; although Jin later split the post into left and right guards, Later Yan maintained central, left, and right guards together.

sentences.zh: 這裏本當作「中衞將軍」，先誤倒為「衞中」，後又訛「將軍」為「郎將」。

translations.literal: Here it should be Central Guard General; first transposed to Guard Central, then "General" corrupted to "Colonel."
translations.idiomatic: Here the text originally should have read General of the Central Guard; it was first transposed to Guard at Center, and later the word general was corrupted to commandant.

sentences.zh: 絹三萬匹 宋書卷一高祖紀「絹」上有「賜」字，此字不宜省，當是脫文。

translations.literal: Thirty thousand bolts of silk. Song shu 1 Emperor Gaozu annals has "granted" before "silk"—should not be omitted; likely lost text.
translations.idiomatic: Missing "granted" before silk.

sentences.zh: 右僕射劉穆之為左僕射領軍中軍二府軍司 諸本「右」作「左」。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Liu Muzhi as Left Vice Director, Army Secretary of Guard and Central Army headquarters. All editions "Right" as "Left."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Right vs Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 按宋書卷二武帝紀中義熙十二年八月稱：「尚書右僕射劉穆之為左僕射，領監軍、中軍二府軍司。」

translations.literal: Song shu 2 Emperor Wu annals Yixi year 12 month 8: Right Vice Director Liu Muzhi as Left Vice Director, overseeing Guard and Central Army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: According to Song shu, juan 2, Basic Annals of Emperor Wu, in the eighth month of the twelfth year of the Yixi era: the Vice Minister of the Right Liu Muzhi was made Vice Minister of the Left, concurrently supervising the military affairs offices of the Supervisor of the Army and the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 同書卷四二劉穆之傳同。

translations.literal: Song shu 42 Liu Muzhi biography agrees.
translations.idiomatic: Song shu 42 agrees.

sentences.zh: 此傳即本宋書，「左」字顯訛，今據改。

translations.literal: This biography follows Song shu; "Left" is clearly wrong—corrected here.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected to Right.

sentences.zh: 「監軍府」即指劉義符所任的「監太尉留府事」，這裏「領」下當脫「監」字。

translations.literal: "Guard Army headquarters" refers to Yifu's "oversee Grand Marshal headquarters affairs"; "oversee" likely lost "oversee Guard."
translations.idiomatic: The Supervisor of the Army office refers to Liu Yifu’s post as Supervisor of the Grand Marshal’s remaining headquarters affairs; the word oversee is probably missing after the word concurrently here.

sentences.zh: 裕遣其中軍將軍沈範索季孫等朝貢 宋書卷九五索虜傳「中軍」作「殿中」。

translations.literal: Yu sent his Central Army General Shen Fan, Suo Jisun, and others on tribute. Song shu 95 Northern Wei biography has "Palace" for "Central Army."
translations.idiomatic: Central Army should be Palace.

sentences.zh: 按晉宋中軍將軍名號甚重，決無帶此官出使之理。

translations.literal: Jin and Song Central Army General was too exalted to be sent on missions.
translations.idiomatic: Rank argument.

sentences.zh: 這時出使北魏例為殿中將軍，下文屢見。

translations.literal: Envoys to Wei were usually Palace Generals—as often below.
translations.idiomatic: Palace General usage.

sentences.zh: 這裏「中軍」必是「殿中」之訛。

translations.literal: Here "Central Army" must be corruption of "Palace."
translations.idiomatic: Emend to Palace.

sentences.zh: 安西將軍古弼 諸本「安西」誤倒作「西安」，今據卷二八古弼傳乙正。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West Gu Bi. All editions transpose to "Pacifies West" as "West Pacifies"—now corrected per this book 28 Gu Bi biography.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Pacifies West (Anxi) was transposed as West Pacifies (Xi'an); corrected per biography 28.

sentences.zh: 永昌王仁擊破之 諸本「仁」訛「位」，今據卷四下世祖紀下太平真君十一年二月條及卷一七永昌王健附仁傳改。

translations.literal: Prince of Yongchang Ren defeated them. All editions "Ren" as "Wei"—now per this book 4b Emperor Shizu Taiping Zhenjun 11 month 2 and 17 Prince Yongchang Wang Jian appendix Ren biography.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: the name should be Ren, not Wei, per the Yongchang prince's biography and the Taiping Zhenjun annals.

sentences.zh: 右將軍豫州刺史南平王鑠 按宋書卷九五載宋檄文，此傳記宋諸將進兵全據此檄。

translations.literal: General of the Right, Inspector of Yu, Prince of Nanping Shuo. Song shu 95 Song proclamation—this passage on Song generals follows that text.
translations.idiomatic: Right General, Inspector of Yu province, Prince Shuo of Nanping: according to Song shu, juan 95, which preserves the Song proclamation; this account of the Song generals’ advance is drawn entirely from that proclamation.

sentences.zh: 檄文稱鑠「悉荊河之師，方軌齊進」。

translations.literal: Proclamation says Shuo "leads all Jing-He forces, advancing on parallel tracks."
translations.idiomatic: Proclamation citation.

sentences.zh: 這裏「鑠」下戛然而止，和下文連讀，遂似鑠和義恭同為「諸軍節度」，「鑠」字下當有脫文。

translations.literal: Here under "Shuo" the text breaks off; read with what follows it seems Shuo and Yigong jointly commanded—text likely lost after "Shuo."
translations.idiomatic: Text lost after Shuo.

sentences.zh: 今於「鑠」字句斷。

translations.literal: Sentence break after "Shuo."
translations.idiomatic: Sentence break.

sentences.zh: 南兗及青冀兗豫三五簡發 諸本「三五」作「三吳」。

translations.literal: Southern Yan and Qing, Ji, Yan, Yu three-five levy. All editions "three-five" as "three Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: "three-five" levy was corrupted to "three Wu"; corrected.

sentences.zh: 宋書卷九五云：「發南兗三五民丁」，即此事，唯只舉「南兗」，下當有脫文。

translations.literal: Song shu 95: "levy three-five militia of Southern Yan"—only Southern Yan named; text below likely lost.
translations.idiomatic: Missing provinces in levy.

sentences.zh: 通鑑卷一二五

translations.literal: Zizhi tongjian 125
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi tongjian 125

sentences.zh: 〈三九四七頁〉

translations.literal: 〈3947 pages〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈3947 pages〉

sentences.zh: 作「悉發青、冀、徐、豫、二兗六州三五民丁」，知此傳也脫「徐」字。

translations.literal: has "levy three-five militia of Qing, Ji, Xu, Yu, two Yan, six provinces"—this biography also lost Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Also lost Xu.

sentences.zh: 胡注：「三五者，三丁發其一，五丁發其二。」

translations.literal: Hu note: "Three-five means one in three households, two in five."
translations.idiomatic: Hu note on three-five levy.

sentences.zh: 三五發卒乃晉以來舊制，晉書卷一一０慕容儁載記稱為「三五占兵」，本書卷九肅宗紀正光五年八月詔書中也有「三五簡發」語，這裏「吳」字乃「五」之訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Three-five levy is old Jin practice; Jin shu 110 Murong Jun annals calls it "three-five soldier allocation"; this book 9 Emperor Suzong Zhengguang 5 year 8 edict also has "three-five selection"—here "Wu" is corruption of "five," now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: "three-five" is the old levy ratio (one man per three or two per five households); "Wu" here is a corruption of "five" and is corrected.

sentences.zh: 揚南徐兗江州富民並四分之一 宋書卷九五作「揚、南徐、兗、江州富有之民家資滿五千萬，僧尼滿二千萬者並四分換一」。

translations.literal: Yang, Southern Xu, Yan, Jiang wealthy households one quarter. Song shu 95: households with assets over fifty million, monks over twenty million, all quarter redeemed.
translations.idiomatic: Missing wealth thresholds in text.

sentences.zh: 這裏「富民」下當脫去「家資」等字，連上文遂似徵發富民四分之一為兵。

translations.literal: Here under "wealthy households" the asset clauses were lost; read with above it seems levying a quarter of wealthy households as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Lost qualification text.

sentences.zh: 屯兵於孫叔敖冢 諸本「冢」作「家」，獨局本作「冢」。

translations.literal: Encamped at Sun Shu'ao's tomb. All editions "tomb" as "house"; bureau edition "tomb."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: "tomb" (zhong) was corrupted to "house" (jia); follow the bureau edition.

sentences.zh: 按宋書卷九五作「冢」。

translations.literal: Song shu 95 has "tomb."
translations.idiomatic: Song shu has tomb.

sentences.zh: 本書卷一九中任城王雲附子澄傳稱澄為揚州刺史，「下車，封孫叔敖之墓」。

translations.literal: This book 19c Ren Chengzi appendix Cheng biography as Yang Inspector "on taking office sealed Sun Shu'ao's tomb."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng sealed the tomb.

sentences.zh: 北齊書卷三二王琳傳載朱瑒與徐陵書，有云：「孫叔云亡，仍芍陂而楸檟。」

translations.literal: Beiqi shu 32 Wang Lin biography Zhu Yang letter to Xu Ling: "When Sun Shu died, still mulberry at Shao Dam."
translations.idiomatic: Bei Qi shu, juan 32, biography of Wang Lin, preserves a letter from Zhu Yang to Xu Ling containing the line: when Sun Shu died, they still raised mulberry stakes at Shao Dam.

sentences.zh: 魏之揚州治壽春，芍陂在壽春南。

translations.literal: Wei Yang province seat Shouchun; Shao Dam south of Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Wei’s Yang province was administered from Shouchun, and Shao Dam lay south of Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 知傳說其地有孫叔敖墓。

translations.literal: Thus the tradition of Sun Shu'ao's tomb in that region.
translations.idiomatic: Tomb tradition.

sentences.zh: 今從局本。

translations.literal: Follow bureau edition.
translations.idiomatic: Follow bureau edition.

sentences.zh: 陳叔兒詹叔兒 諸本「詹」下無「叔兒」二字，宋書卷九九二兇傳有，且下文又兩見詹叔兒名，一次也是和陳叔兒同舉，知陳、詹同名「叔兒」，這裏乃涉上「陳叔兒」而脫去「叔兒」二字。

translations.literal: Chen Shu'er and Zhan Shu'er. All editions lack second "Shu'er" under Zhan; Song shu 99 Ferocity biography has it; below Zhan Shu'er appears twice with Chen—Zhan lost "Shu'er" by assimilation to Chen Shu'er.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: restore the name Zhan Shu'er, omitted by assimilation to Chen Shu'er in the received text.

sentences.zh: 此傳即本宋書，今據補。

translations.literal: This biography follows Song shu—supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: This biography is based on the Song shu and has been supplemented from that source.

sentences.zh: 頓漂洲 宋書卷六孝武帝紀「漂」作「溧」。

translations.literal: Encamped at Piao Isle. Song shu 6 Emperor Xiaowu annals "Piao" as "Li."
translations.idiomatic: Piao vs Li.

sentences.zh: 按晉書卷八四劉牢之傳稱牢之「率北府文武屯洌洲」。

translations.literal: Jin shu 84 Liu Laozhi biography says Laozhi "led Northern Mansion civil and military to encamp at Lie Isle."
translations.idiomatic: Jin shu Lie Isle.

sentences.zh: 通鑑卷一一二

translations.literal: Zizhi tongjian 112
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi tongjian 112

sentences.zh: 〈三五三七頁〉

translations.literal: 〈3537 pages〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈3537 pages〉

sentences.zh: 「洌」作「溧」，胡注：「『洌』『溧』聲相近，故又為溧洲。

translations.literal: "Lie" as "Li"—near homophones; Zhang Shunmin says "passing Three Mountains over ten li to Li Isle.
translations.idiomatic: The character read lie is written as li in some texts. Hu’s commentary notes that lie and li are close in sound, which is why the place was also called Li prefecture.

sentences.zh: 張舜民曰『過三山十餘里至溧洲』。」

translations.literal: Thus here "Piao" should be "Li."
translations.idiomatic: Piao to Li.

sentences.zh: 則這裏「漂」字當是「溧」之訛。

translations.literal: But Hu also cites "Huan Chong left Jiankang, Xie An saw him off to Li Isle"—Jin shu commercial edition 74 Huan Yi appendix Chong biography has "Piao Isle"—Jin shu also varies; unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Jin shu variant retained.

sentences.zh: 但胡注又以「桓沖發建康，謝安送至溧洲」為證，今檢晉書商務影宋本卷七四桓彝附桓沖傳却作「漂洲」。

translations.literal: But Hu also cites Huan Chong leaving Jiankang with Xie An seeing him off to Li Isle—Jin shu commercial edition 74 Huan Chong biography has Piao Isle—Jin shu also varies; unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Jin shu itself reads Piao Isle in the Huan Chong passage, so the text is left unchanged despite the homophone argument.

sentences.zh: 知此字晉書亦有異文，今不改。

translations.literal: Jin shu has variant—unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: It is known that Jin shu also has a variant reading for this character; the text is left unchanged here.

sentences.zh: 其中軍府錄事參軍周朗啟駿曰 諸本「朗」作「殷」。

translations.literal: Central Army headquarters Recording Officer Zhou Lang memorialized Jun. All editions "Lang" as "Yin."
translations.idiomatic: Lang not Yin.

sentences.zh: 按語見宋書卷八二周朗傳，傳稱「朗字義利」，不云一名「殷」。

translations.literal: Words in Song shu 82 Zhou Lang biography; styled Yili, not called Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Lang name.

sentences.zh: 「殷」字訛，今改正。

translations.literal: "Yin" corrupted—corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected to Lang.

sentences.zh: 又疾讒害其間 宋書卷八二此句作「嫉謗讒害其間」。

translations.literal: Also slander and harm between them. Song shu 82: "jealousy, slander, and harm between them."
translations.idiomatic: Missing slander character.

sentences.zh: 這裏「疾」下當脫「謗」字。

translations.literal: Here under "between them" the character "slander" is lost. Song shu 82 reads "jealousy, slander, and harm between them."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: the character for "slander" is missing below "jealousy" and should be restored per Song shu 82.

sentences.zh: 遣軍就質 按這裏上無主名，當脫「義宣」二字。

translations.literal: Send troops to join Zhi. No subject above—likely "Yixuan" is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: the subject "Yixuan" is probably lost before the clause about sending troops to Zhi.

sentences.zh: 質不求前驅 宋書卷七四臧質傳無「不」字。

translations.literal: Zhi does not seek the vanguard. Song shu 74 Zang Zhi biography lacks "not."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Song shu 74 lacks "not," but the narrative context may still require it.

sentences.zh: 按上文記質要求「浮舟外江，直至石頭」，正是「求前驅」，若作「不求」，和質語不合。

translations.literal: Above records Zhi asking to "float boats on the outer river straight to Stone City"—that is seeking the vanguard; if "does not seek," it conflicts with Zhi's words.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: since Zhi explicitly sought a river assault on Stone City, "does not seek the vanguard" conflicts with his own plan.

sentences.zh: 這裏「不」字當是衍文。

translations.literal: Here "not" is likely interpolated text.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: the negative "not" is probably an interpolation.

sentences.zh: 駿將軍垣護之 諸本「護之」上無「垣」字。

translations.literal: Jun's general Yuan Huzhi. All editions lack "Yuan" before Huzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: the surname Yuan is missing before Huzhi in received editions.

sentences.zh: 按上文既未見垣護之姓名，這裏不應逕稱「護之」，當是脫文，今據宋書卷六八南郡王義宣傳補。

translations.literal: Above never named Yuan Huzhi—cannot say "Huzhi" alone; likely lost text—now supplemented per Song shu 68 Prince of Nan Commandery Yixuan biography.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Yuan is supplemented from Song shu 68, since Huzhi cannot stand alone here.

sentences.zh: 又遊湖縣之滿山 按宋書卷六孝武帝紀大明七年十月己巳，劉駿「校獵於姑孰」，十一月乙酉，「訊溧陽、永世、丹陽囚」，癸己，「習水軍於梁山」，十二月丙午，至歷陽，己未，「於博望、梁山立雙闕」。

translations.literal: Also toured Manshan in Huxian. Song shu 6 Emperor Xiaowu annals: tenth month gui si of year 7, Liu Jun "hunted at Guniu"; eleventh month yi you "interrogated prisoners of Liyang, Yongshi, Danyang"; gui si "drilled navy at Liang Mountain"; twelfth month bingwu reached Liyang, ji wei "set double gates at Bowang and Liang Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: He also toured Manshan in Huxian county. According to Song shu, juan 6, Basic Annals of Emperor Xiaowu: on the guisi day of the tenth month of the seventh year of the Daming era, Liu Jun conducted a hunt at Guniu; on yiyou of the eleventh month he examined prisoners of Liyang, Yongshi, and Danyang; on guisi he drilled the navy at Liang Mountain; on bingwu of the twelfth month he reached Liyang; and on jiwei he erected double gate towers at Bowang and Liang Mountain. That itinerary does not mention Huxian or Manshan.

sentences.zh: 所經之地並無所謂「湖縣滿山」。

translations.literal: No such place as "Huxian Manshan" on that route.
translations.idiomatic: No Huxian Manshan on the route.

sentences.zh: 這次行踪實在南豫州，孝武紀大明五年九月甲戌記「移南豫州治淮南于湖縣」。

translations.literal: The journey was in Southern Yuzhou; Xiaowu annals year 5 month 9 jiaxu records "moved Southern Yuzhou seat from Huainan to Huxian."
translations.idiomatic: Southern Yuzhou seat at Huxian.

sentences.zh: 于湖即劉駿於此校獵的姑孰。

translations.literal: Huxian is Guniu where Jun hunted.
translations.idiomatic: Huxian is Guniu.

sentences.zh: 這裏「湖縣」上脫「于」字。

translations.literal: Here "Huxian" lost "Yu" above—should be "Yu Huxian."
translations.idiomatic: Missing Yu before Huxian.

sentences.zh: 「滿山」乃「梁山」之訛。

translations.literal: "Manshan" is corruption of "Liang Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: Manshan should be Liang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 梁山在歷陽

translations.literal: Liang Mountain is in Liyang
translations.idiomatic: Liang Mountain at Liyang

sentences.zh: 〈今安徽和縣〉，

translations.literal: 〈modern He county, Anhui〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈modern He county, Anhui〉

sentences.zh: 實在于湖

translations.literal: actually opposite Huxian
translations.idiomatic: opposite Huxian

sentences.zh: 〈今安徽當塗縣〉

translations.literal: 〈modern Dangtu, Anhui〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈modern Dangtu, Anhui〉

sentences.zh: 對岸，魏收北人，誤以為在于湖。

translations.literal: Wei Shou a northerner mistook the geography.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou misread the geography.

sentences.zh: 遣其黨俞伯奇出頓大雷 諸本「大雷」作「大電」，宋書卷八四鄧琬傳作「大雷」。

translations.literal: Sent his partisan Yu Boqi to encamp at Dalei. All editions "Dalei" as "great lightning"; Song shu 84 Deng Wan biography has "Dalei."
translations.idiomatic: He sent his partisan Yu Boqi to encamp at Dalei. In various editions Dalei is written as great lightning, but Song shu, juan 84, biography of Deng Wan, reads Dalei.

sentences.zh: 按大雷屢見紀載，「電」字顯訛，今改正。

translations.literal: Dalei appears often in records—"lightning" is clearly wrong; corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected to Dalei.

sentences.zh: 巴東太守孫仲之至于平石 按宋書卷八０晉安王子勛傳、卷八四鄧琬傳「仲」並作「沖」。

translations.literal: Administrator of Badong Sun Chongzhi reached Pingshi. Song shu 80 Prince of Jin'an Zixun biography and 84 Deng Wan biography both have "Chong" not "Zhong."
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Chongzhi, Administrator of Badong, reached Pingshi: according to Song shu, juan 80, biography of Zixun, Prince of Jin'an, and juan 84, biography of Deng Wan, the name is written Chong rather than Zhong.

sentences.zh: 「仲」字當是形近而訛。

translations.literal: "Zhong" is likely shape-corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong corrupted from Chong.

sentences.zh: 建牙於桑厄 宋書鄧琬傳「厄」作「尾」，通鑑卷一三０

translations.literal: Set up headquarters at Sanger. Song shu Deng Wan biography "er" as "wei"; Zizhi tongjian 130
translations.idiomatic: Sanger tail variant.

sentences.zh: 〈四０九二頁〉

translations.literal: 〈4092 pages〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈4092 pages〉

sentences.zh: 同宋書，胡注：「桑尾，即桑落洲尾。」

translations.literal: same as Song shu; Hu note: "Sangwei is the tail of Sangluo Isle."
translations.idiomatic: Hu note on Sangwei.

sentences.zh: 疑「厄」字訛。

translations.literal: Likely "er" corrupted.
translations.idiomatic: Likely er corrupted.

sentences.zh: 臨海王子頊 諸本「頊」作「瑱」。

translations.literal: Prince of Linhai Zixu. All editions "Xu" as "Zhen."
translations.idiomatic: Zixu not Zhen.

sentences.zh: 按宋書卷六孝武帝紀、卷八明帝紀、卷八０孝武十四王傳都作「子頊」。

translations.literal: Song shu 6 Xiaowu annals, 8 Mingdi annals, 80 Fourteen Sons of Xiaowu all have "Zixu."
translations.idiomatic: Song shu has Zixu.

sentences.zh: 「瑱」乃形近而訛，今改正。

translations.literal: "Zhen" is shape-corruption—corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected to Zixu.

sentences.zh: 子起子期子悅子頓 宋書卷八０傳序「子起」作「子趨」，又無「子頓」名。

translations.literal: Ziqi, Ziqi, Ziyue, Zidun. Song shu 80 sequence "Ziqi" as "Ziqu"; no "Zidun."
translations.idiomatic: Ziqi and missing Zidun note.

sentences.zh: 劉駿二十八子，傳序列舉無遺，此「子頓」疑是「子頊」重出，又訛「頊」為「頓」。

translations.literal: Liu Jun's twenty-eight sons listed without omission—"Zidun" likely duplicate of "Zixu" with Xu corrupted to Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: "Zidun" is probably a duplicate of "Zixu" with one character corrupted.

sentences.zh: 永等前後奮擊斬首凍沒死者不可勝數 按事見本書卷五０尉元傳、宋書卷五三張永傳。

translations.literal: Yong and others repeatedly attacked; heads taken and frozen drowned dead beyond counting. Event in this book 50 Wei Yuan biography, Song shu 53 Zhang Yong biography.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: the account is documented in the Wei Yuan and Zhang Yong biographies.

sentences.zh: 所謂「斬首凍沒死者不可勝數」乃指張永所統之宋軍。

translations.literal: "Heads taken and frozen drowned" refers to Zhang Yong's Song army.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: the countless dead are Zhang Yong's Song troops, not Wei forces.

sentences.zh: 這裏「永等」下有脫文，連讀遂似永等奮擊魏軍，魏軍死者不可勝數。

translations.literal: Here after "Yong and others" text is lost; read together it seems Yong attacked Wei and Wei dead were countless—wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: a clause break is needed after "Yong and others" to avoid misreading who suffered the losses.

sentences.zh: 今於「永等」下句斷。

translations.literal: Sentence break after "Yong and others."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: punctuate with a new sentence after "Yong and others."

sentences.zh: 遣員外散騎侍郎田廉員外散騎侍郎祖德朝貢 按自劉駿

translations.literal: Sent Extraordinary Attendant Tian Lian and Extraordinary Attendant Zu De on tribute. From Liu Jun
translations.idiomatic: Collation: this envoy notice concerns the ranks used under Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 〈宋孝武帝〉

translations.literal: 〈Song Emperor Xiaowu〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Song Emperor Xiaowu〉

sentences.zh: 以來，宋魏遣使，通常正使為散騎常侍，副使為散騎侍郎，此傳下文所記皆然，無正副並為散騎侍郎之例。

translations.literal: onward Song-Wei envoys: principal usually Regular Attendant, deputy Regular Attendant—below all match; no case of both as Extraordinary Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: from Emperor Xiaowu onward Song envoys to Wei were normally led by a Regular Attendant with a Regular Attendant as deputy, not two Extraordinary Attendants.

sentences.zh: 如果這次正副同官，則又何須兩舉官銜。

translations.literal: If both same rank, why state both titles twice.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: if both envoys held the same rank, repeating both titles would be redundant.

sentences.zh: 上「散騎侍郎」當是「散騎常侍」之訛。

translations.literal: Upper "Extraordinary Attendant" should be "Regular Attendant" corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Collation: the first title should read Regular Attendant, not Extraordinary Attendant.

sentences.zh: 其司空桂陽王休範奔尋陽舉兵 按宋書卷七九休範傳，休範早於泰始六年為江州刺史，尋陽是江州治所，又何須「奔」。

translations.literal: His Minister of Works Prince of Guiyang Xiufan fled to Xunyang and raised troops. Song shu 79 Xiufan biography: Xiufan was already Inspector of Jiang in year 6 of Taishi—Xunyang is Jiang seat—why "fled"?
translations.idiomatic: Collation: Song shu shows Xiufan already at Xunyang as Jiang inspector, so "fled to Xunyang" is questionable.

sentences.zh: 「奔」字疑當作「於」。

translations.literal: The character "fled" is suspected to should be "at."
translations.idiomatic: Collation: "fled" is probably a corruption of the preposition "at."
